items.q: What is the central contention of the passage?
o: Debt restructurings fail chiefly because sovereigns and creditors cannot agree on the size of the haircut.
The technical calculation of losses is rarely the main obstacle; disputes over comparability of treatment and holdout tactics are what prolong restructurings.
Paris Club creditors are structurally unwilling to ever accept any losses on bilateral debt.
Collective action clauses have eliminated the problem of holdout creditors entirely.
items.e: Die zentrale These lautet, dass „the central arithmetic is seldom in serious dispute“ – der eigentliche Streit entzündet sich an der Gleichbehandlung der Gläubigerklassen und an Holdout-Investoren, nicht an der Höhe des Schuldenschnitts.
items.passage:
When a government first concedes that it can no longer service its obligations on the agreed terms, the admission rarely surprises anyone but the public. Bondholders will long since have priced in the likelihood of default, and rating agencies will have downgraded the sovereign well before the finance ministry acknowledges the obvious. What follows, however, is seldom swift. The machinery of restructuring — Paris Club deliberations for official bilateral debt, ad hoc committees for private bondholders, and an IMF programme to anchor the whole exercise — grinds forward at a pace that owes as much to legal caution as to genuine disagreement over numbers.

The central arithmetic is seldom in serious dispute: independent debt-sustainability analyses converge, more often than not, on a haircut in the broad vicinity of the eventual settlement. What consumes years rather than months is the argument over comparability of treatment — the insistence, chiefly from official creditors, that no class of lender should emerge from the exercise better compensated than another. Private creditors, for their part, resist any formula that would bind them to concessions calibrated by committees on which they hold no seat.

Holdout investors complicate matters further. A small minority, calculating that litigation promises a better return than participation, can delay an exchange offer for years, as courts in New York and London have repeatedly demonstrated. Collective action clauses, now standard in most sovereign bond documentation, were devised precisely to blunt this tactic, aggregating votes across bond series so that a supermajority can bind reluctant holders. Bonds issued before the last crisis, however, often lack such aggregation features, leaving the debtor exposed to exactly the holdout dynamic the newer instruments were built to prevent.

None of this renders restructuring impossible — merely slow, litigious, and psychologically punishing for a finance ministry that must simultaneously reassure its citizens and negotiate away a portion of what creditors were once promised. The countries that emerge fastest from the process, negotiators privately concede, are rarely those with the strongest legal teams, but those willing to concede the arithmetic early and spend their political capital on comparability rather than delay.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, what typically happens before a finance ministry publicly admits default?
o: The IMF unilaterally imposes a restructuring programme.
Rating agencies downgrade the sovereign and bondholders price in the likelihood of default.
Paris Club members vote to suspend the country's UN membership.
Private creditors voluntarily offer a haircut before being asked.
items.e: Zitat: „rating agencies will have downgraded the sovereign well before the finance ministry acknowledges the obvious.“

items.q: What is the function of the Paris Club in the process described in the passage?
o: It represents private bondholders in litigation.
It handles negotiations over official bilateral debt.
It sets global interest rates for sovereign bonds.
It replaces the IMF as lender of last resort.
items.e: Zitat: „Paris Club deliberations for official bilateral debt“.

items.q: What can be inferred about bonds issued before collective action clauses became standard?
o: They are automatically restructured alongside newer bonds.
They leave issuers more vulnerable to holdout creditors.
They cannot legally be included in any restructuring.
They carry a lower yield than newer bonds.
items.e: Der Text folgert: Ältere Anleihen „often lack such aggregation features, leaving the debtor exposed to exactly the holdout dynamic“ – also erhöhte Anfälligkeit für Holdouts.

items.q: In the passage, the word 'aggregating' (third paragraph) most nearly means…
items.e: „Aggregating votes across bond series“ bedeutet, Stimmen über verschiedene Anleiheserien hinweg zusammenzufassen – also „combining“.

items.q: The author's tone toward the restructuring process described can best be characterised as…
items.e: Der Text argumentiert sachlich mit Belegen (Gerichte, Klauseln, Analysen) ohne emotionale Anklage – also nüchtern-analytisch.

items.q: What is the primary function of the third paragraph, beginning 'Holdout investors complicate matters further'?
o: To summarize the entire argument of the passage.
To introduce a complicating factor and explain the legal tool designed to address it.
To contradict the claim made in the second paragraph.
To provide statistical evidence for the size of typical haircuts.
items.e: Der Absatz führt Holdout-Investoren als zusätzliches Hindernis ein und erklärt anschließend Collective Action Clauses als Gegenmittel.

items.q: Per the closing paragraph, which negotiators tend to emerge fastest from a restructuring?
o: Those with the largest legal teams.
Those who delay conceding the numbers as long as possible.
Those willing to accept the arithmetic early and focus their effort on comparability.
Those who rely exclusively on IMF mediation.
items.e: Zitat: „those willing to concede the arithmetic early and spend their political capital on comparability rather than delay.“

items.q: The republic had been ____ on its coupon payments for nearly six months before the restructuring talks began.
items.e: Feste Wendung „to be in arrears (on sth.)“ = mit Zahlungen im Rückstand sein.

items.q: Bondholders ultimately accepted a 40 percent ____ on the face value of their holdings.
items.e: „Haircut“ ist der feststehende Fachbegriff für den prozentualen Wertabschlag, den Gläubiger hinnehmen; die anderen Wörter sind keine gängigen Finanzbegriffe.

items.q: Creditors agreed to a temporary ____, suspending debt-service payments while the terms of the exchange were finalised.
items.e: „Standstill (agreement)“ = vereinbarter Zahlungsaufschub während der Verhandlungen; die anderen „stand-“Komposita bedeuten etwas anderes.

items.q: Economists warned that a persistent ____ would continue to deter new investment even after the restructuring concluded.
items.e: „Debt overhang“ bezeichnet eine Schuldenlast, die Investitionen lähmt, weil künftige Erträge ohnehin an Gläubiger fließen würden.

items.q: The government launched an ____ inviting bondholders to swap old instruments for new ones with a longer maturity.
items.e: „Exchange offer“ ist der Fachbegriff für das Umtauschangebot alter gegen neue Anleihen im Rahmen einer Umschuldung.

items.q: A handful of ____ funds refused every proposed exchange, betting instead on a favourable court judgment.
items.e: „Holdout creditors/funds“ sind Gläubiger, die einer Umschuldung nicht zustimmen und stattdessen den Klageweg suchen.

items.q: The IMF's debt-____ analysis concluded that the current repayment schedule was simply unaffordable.
items.e: „Debt sustainability analysis (DSA)“ ist der feste IWF-Fachbegriff für die Tragfähigkeitsanalyse der Verschuldung.

items.q: The banks agreed to a substantial ____ of the loan's principal as part of the settlement.
items.e: „Write-down“ = teilweise Wertberichtigung des Nominalbetrags, im Unterschied zur vollständigen Abschreibung („write-off“).

items.q: Without an emergency ____ from multilateral lenders, the government would have been forced into an immediate default.
items.e: „Bailout“ = Rettungspaket/finanzielle Nothilfe; die übrigen Wörter sind nur lautlich ähnlich, aber sachfremd.

items.q: The IMF programme was contingent on a package of ____ measures, including cuts to public-sector wages.
items.e: „Austerity measures“ ist die feste Kollokation für staatliche Sparmaßnahmen im Zuge eines Hilfsprogramms.

items.q: Regulators feared that a disorderly default could trigger financial ____ across neighbouring markets.
items.e: „Financial contagion“ ist der etablierte Fachbegriff für die Ausbreitung einer Finanzkrise auf andere Märkte.

items.q: The bond ____ prohibited the issuer from taking on additional senior debt without creditor consent.
items.e: „Bond covenant“ ist die feststehende Bezeichnung für vertragliche Nebenpflichten/Auflagen einer Anleihe.

items.q: The loan was secured against future export revenues, pledged as ____ to reassure lenders.
items.e: „Collateral“ = Sicherheit, die zur Besicherung eines Kredits verpfändet wird.

items.q: By the time talks began, the treasury was already on the brink of ____.
items.e: „Insolvency“ = Zahlungsunfähigkeit; die Distraktoren sind lautlich ähnliche, aber inhaltlich falsche Substantive.

items.q: A sudden ____ crunch, rather than outright insolvency, had forced the ministry's hand.
items.e: „Liquidity crunch“ = akuter Mangel an kurzfristig verfügbaren Zahlungsmitteln.

items.q: The new bonds were structured to ____ gradually over twenty years rather than in a single bullet payment.
items.e: „To amortize“ = eine Schuld über die Zeit in Raten tilgen, im Gegensatz zur Einmalzahlung („bullet payment“).

items.q: Traders exploited the price gap between the old and new bonds through simple ____.
items.e: „Arbitrage“ = Ausnutzen von Preisunterschieden zwischen zwei Märkten; nicht zu verwechseln mit „arbitration“ (Schiedsverfahren).

items.q: Every ____ of record was entitled to vote on the proposed exchange.
items.e: „Bondholder“ = Inhaber einer Anleihe; die übrigen „-holder“-Komposita bezeichnen andere Beteiligte.

items.q: The restructured bonds carried a lower ____ than the defaulted instruments they replaced.
items.e: „Coupon“ = der periodisch gezahlte Zinssatz einer Anleihe; „dividend“ betrifft Aktien, nicht Anleihen.

items.q: As talks dragged on, bond ____ climbed to levels that priced in a near-certain default.
items.e: „Bond yield“ = Anleiherendite; feststehender Fachbegriff, die Distraktoren passen hier nicht kollokativ.

items.q: The exchange extended the average ____ of the debt stock from five to fifteen years.
items.e: „Maturity“ = Fälligkeit/Laufzeit einer Anleihe; feststehender Fachbegriff im Anleihekontext.

items.q: Neither side was prepared to make further ____ until the comparability question was resolved.
items.e: „To make concessions“ = Zugeständnisse machen; die Distraktoren klingen ähnlich, bedeuten aber etwas anderes.

items.q: Talks reached a ____ over which creditor class should bear the largest share of losses.
items.e: „reach a stalemate“ = sich in eine festgefahrene Lage manövrieren (Verhandlungsstillstand).

items.q: Analysts accused both delegations of engaging in reckless ____ rather than good-faith bargaining.
items.e: „Brinkmanship“ = Politik des Vorantreibens einer Konfrontation bis an den Rand des Scheiterns.

items.q: Multilateral lenders traditionally insist on preferred ____, meaning they are repaid before other creditor classes.
items.e: „Seniority“ ist der finanzfachliche Begriff für den Rang eines Gläubigers bei der Rückzahlung (senior vor subordiniert).

items.q: The clause guaranteed that all bondholders would be treated ____, ranking equally without preference.
items.e: „Pari passu“ (lat. „mit gleichem Schritt“) ist die Standardklausel, die Gleichrangigkeit der Gläubiger sichert.

items.q: The mediator insisted that each delegation ____ its final position in writing before the deadline.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach „insist that“: Grundform ohne -s, unabhängig vom Subjekt.

items.q: It is essential that the creditor committee ____ informed of any change to the repayment schedule.
items.e: Nach „it is essential that“ steht der mandative Subjunktiv „be“, nicht die konjugierte Form.

items.q: If the ministry had accepted the initial offer, the negotiations ____ concluded months ago.
items.e: Typ-3-Konditional (Bedingung und Folge beide in der Vergangenheit): „would have + Partizip II“.

items.q: If the country were not so heavily indebted, the talks ____ far less contentious now.
items.e: Gemischtes Konditional: zeitlose Bedingung (Typ 2) + Folge in der Gegenwart „would be“.

items.q: Rarely ____ a restructuring conclude without at least one round of litigation.
items.e: Nach vorangestelltem „rarely“ folgt Inversion mit Hilfsverb: „rarely does a restructuring conclude…“.

items.q: ____ had the exchange offer been published than holdout funds filed suit.
items.e: Feste Korrelativkonstruktion „no sooner … than …“; „hardly/scarcely“ verlangen „when“, nicht „than“.

items.q: ____ the comparability clause, not the size of the haircut, that delayed the agreement.
items.e: Spaltsatz (cleft sentence) „It was X that…“ zur Hervorhebung; der Vergangenheitsbezug verlangt „was“.

items.q: ____ the finance minister who ultimately signed the exchange agreement.
items.e: Cleft-Konstruktion „It was … who …“ betont das Subjekt; „there was“ wäre in dieser Hervorhebung grammatisch falsch.

items.q: The negotiator said that the offer ____ under review since the previous session.
items.e: Backshift bei indirekter Rede: Vorzeitigkeit vor dem Sagen-Zeitpunkt erfordert das Past Perfect „had been“.

items.q: She told reporters that the committee ____ its decision the following week.
items.e: Backshift: „will“ wird in indirekter Rede zu „would“, wenn das einleitende Verb in der Vergangenheit steht.

items.q: The delegation ____ anticipated the holdouts' legal strategy — the litigation had been public knowledge for months.
items.e: „Must have + Partizip II“ drückt eine logische Schlussfolgerung über die Vergangenheit aus.

items.q: In hindsight, the ministry ____ accepted the earlier, less generous offer.
items.e: „Should have + Partizip II“ drückt Bedauern über eine verpasste Handlung in der Vergangenheit aus.

items.q: ____ the sustainability analysis, the IMF board approved the disbursement.
items.e: Vorzeitiges Partizip „having + Partizip II“ zeigt an, dass die Prüfung vor der Genehmigung abgeschlossen war.

items.q: ____ by three successive credit-rating downgrades, the government finally requested IMF assistance.
items.e: Passives Partizip „pressured“ (= being pressured) beschreibt den Zustand des Subjekts; es ist Empfänger, nicht Ausführender der Handlung.

items.q: The longer the negotiations dragged on, ____ the eventual settlement became.
items.e: Korrelativkonstruktion „the + Komparativ …, the + Komparativ …“; beide Satzhälften benötigen „the“.

items.q: The plan ____ addressed the arrears but also restored access to capital markets.
items.e: Korrelative Konjunktion „not only … but also …“.

items.q: The terms ____ the debt was restructured left the sovereign considerably better off.
items.e: Vorangestellte Präposition im Relativsatz: „the terms under which…“ ist das formellere Register statt „which… under“.

items.q: This is precisely the impasse ____ the mediators had been warning.
items.e: Formeller Relativsatz mit vorangestellter Präposition: „warn about sth.“ → „the impasse about which…“.

items.q: By the time the bonds mature, the government ____ its entire external debt stock.
items.e: Future Perfect für eine bis zu einem zukünftigen Zeitpunkt abgeschlossene Handlung: „will have + Partizip II“.

items.q: By next quarter, the committee ____ every creditor class at least twice.
items.e: Future Perfect: Abschluss der Handlung vor einem festgelegten zukünftigen Zeitpunkt.

items.q: ____ IMF and ____ Paris Club coordinated closely throughout the negotiations.
items.e: Institutionsnamen, die eine einzigartige Organisation bezeichnen, verlangen den bestimmten Artikel: „the IMF“, „the Paris Club“.

items.q: ____ finance minister who negotiated the deal later became ____ ambassador to Washington.
items.e: Beide Ämter — „finance minister“ und „ambassador to Washington“ — sind konkrete, einzigartige Posten und benötigen den bestimmten Artikel.

items.q: The committee had already scheduled the vote, but ultimately decided to ____.
items.e: Bei trennbaren Phrasal Verbs muss ein Pronomen-Objekt zwischen Verb und Partikel stehen: „put it off“, nicht „put off it“.

items.q: The two sides had significant differences, but eventually managed to ____.
items.e: Trennbares Phrasal Verb „iron out sth.“ mit Pronomen-Objekt: das Pronomen muss zwischen Verb und Partikel stehen — „iron them out“.

items.q: The delegation now wishes it ____ more time before signing the initial term sheet.
items.e: Nach „wish“ mit Bezug auf die Vergangenheit steht das Past Perfect: „wish + had + Partizip II“.

items.q: The final settlement was not nearly ____ generous as creditors had originally demanded.
items.e: Vergleichskonstruktion „as + Adjektiv + as“; nach „not nearly“ ist „as … as“ die Standardform.

run16.label: Run 16 – Trainingslauf (C2) · 60 Fragen / 60 Punkte
run16.note: Aufbau analog Sprachtest Russisch: Teil 1 Textverständnis (8 Fragen zu einem Textabschnitt), Teil 2 Wortschatz/Idiomatik (26 Fragen), Teil 3 Grammatik/Zeitformen (26 Fragen). Jede Frage 1 Punkt, insgesamt 60 Punkte, bestanden ab 30 Punkten (50 %). Trainingsniveau C2 – offizielles Prüfungsniveau C1+. Nicht offiziell.

items.q: Which of the following best captures the author's main argument?
o: Export licences have become a central, consequential instrument of statecraft despite their unglamorous mechanics.
Lithography firms should be nationalised to prevent chokepoint abuse.
Extraterritorial rules have proven entirely ineffective against circumvention.
Allied governments have already achieved full coordination on export controls.
items.e: Kernthese im ersten Absatz: „What was once the preserve of customs officials and legal counsel has become… a lever wielded by cabinets.“ Option D widerspricht dem Schluss, der Koordination als „scarcest commodity“ bezeichnet.
items.passage:
Few instruments of statecraft have migrated so swiftly from the technical annex to the front page as the export licence. What was once the preserve of customs officials and legal counsel has become, in the contest over chokepoint technologies, a lever wielded by cabinets and summoned by name in communiqués. The mechanics are unglamorous — a widened entity list here, a tightened definition of dual-use goods there — yet the cumulative effect has been to redraw, quietly but unmistakably, the map of who may sell what to whom.

Nowhere is this more visible than in the contest over advanced lithography. The handful of firms capable of etching circuits at the smallest nodes sit, whether they relish it or not, at a genuine chokepoint: deny them a licence to ship to a given foundry, and years of downstream ambition stall on a factory floor. Governments have grasped this leverage and, increasingly, have sought to extend it beyond their own borders through rules that reach any product built, however distantly, on their equipment or designs. Trading partners grumble at what they regard as an extraterritorial overreach; officials in Washington and Brussels counter that a chokepoint left ungoverned is a chokepoint someone else will exploit.

Whether this amounts to decoupling or merely a more cautious de-risking is, in practice, a distinction without much of a difference for the engineers now redrawing supply chains. Firms once content to single-source a wafer fabrication step are quietly building redundancy, at real cost, into designs that assumed none would be needed. Some of this hedging is prudent; some is theatre performed for boards anxious to be seen taking precautions. What should trouble policymakers more than either is the growing appetite among intermediaries for helping targeted buyers route around the rules altogether — a shadow trade that no entity list, however long, can fully anticipate. Coordination among allied capitals remains the likeliest antidote, yet it is also, for now, the scarcest commodity in the toolkit.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, why do the handful of advanced lithography firms sit at a 'genuine chokepoint'?
o: Because they are the only firms permitted to trade with Washington.
Because denying them a licence to ship to a foundry can stall years of downstream ambition.
Because they set global tariff rates for semiconductors.
Because they own the entity list.
items.e: Zitat: „deny them a licence to ship to a given foundry, and years of downstream ambition stall on a factory floor.“

items.q: Why do trading partners object to rules that reach products built on Western equipment or designs, per the passage?
o: They regard it as extraterritorial overreach.
They believe it violates most-favoured-nation treatment.
They argue it duplicates the entity list unnecessarily.
They consider it a form of double taxation.
items.e: Zitat: „Trading partners grumble at what they regard as an extraterritorial overreach.“

items.q: What can be inferred about the author's view of firms 'quietly building redundancy… at real cost'?
o: The author believes all such redundancy is wasteful theatre.
The author suggests some of this hedging is sensible while some is performative.
The author claims redundancy has eliminated single-sourcing risk entirely.
The author states governments mandated this redundancy by law.
items.e: Zitat: „Some of this hedging is prudent; some is theatre performed for boards anxious to be seen taking precautions.“ — differenzierte Einschätzung, keine pauschale Verurteilung.

items.q: In the passage, the word 'grasped' (as in 'Governments have grasped this leverage') is closest in meaning to …
items.e: „to grasp“ bedeutet hier „erfassen/erkennen und ergreifen“ — Regierungen haben die Hebelwirkung erkannt und genutzt.

items.q: The author's tone toward the effectiveness of allied coordination is best described as …
items.e: Schlusssatz: Koordination sei „the likeliest antidote, yet it is also, for now, the scarcest commodity in the toolkit“ — Anerkennung des Potenzials bei gleichzeitiger Zurückhaltung.

items.q: What is the primary function of the final paragraph in relation to the rest of the passage?
o: It introduces a completely new topic unrelated to export controls.
It qualifies the decoupling/de-risking distinction and identifies a further risk the earlier paragraphs had not addressed.
It refutes the claims made in the second paragraph about lithography.
It summarises statistics presented earlier in the passage.
items.e: Der letzte Absatz relativiert die Unterscheidung „decoupling“ vs. „de-risking“ und führt mit der Umgehung durch Mittelsmänner ein neues Risiko ein, das zuvor nicht behandelt wurde.

items.q: What does the author identify as something 'no entity list, however long, can fully anticipate'?
o: The rise of intermediaries helping targeted buyers circumvent the rules.
The expansion of foundry capacity in allied countries.
The tightening of dual-use goods definitions.
items.e: Zitat: „the growing appetite among intermediaries for helping targeted buyers route around the rules altogether — a shadow trade that no entity list, however long, can fully anticipate.“

items.q: Once regulators formally added the supplier to the ____, no further shipments could proceed without a specific exemption.
items.e: „entity list“ = feste Fachbezeichnung im US-Exportkontrollrecht für die Liste kontrollierter/sanktionierter Empfänger.

items.q: The valves were classified as ____ goods because they had both civilian and potential military applications.
items.e: „dual-use goods“ = Güter mit doppeltem Verwendungszweck (zivil/militärisch) — feste exportkontrollrechtliche Bezeichnung.

items.q: Advanced lithography machines represent a genuine ____ in the semiconductor supply chain, since only a handful of firms can produce them.
items.e: „chokepoint“ = Engpass, an dem sich Kontrolle bündelt; die Distraktoren implizieren keine Engstelle.

items.q: Brussels increasingly frames its policy as ____ rather than a wholesale severing of economic ties.
items.e: „de-risking“ = gezielte Risikominderung statt vollständiger Entkopplung — aktueller Begriff der EU-Wirtschaftsdiplomatie.

items.q: Some hawks in the debate favour full ____ of the two economies rather than managed interdependence.
items.e: „decoupling“ = vollständige wirtschaftliche Entflechtung, Gegenbegriff zu „de-risking“.

items.q: The ministry's white paper called for greater ____ so that a single supplier disruption could not paralyse production.
items.e: „supply-chain resilience“ = Widerstandsfähigkeit der Lieferkette — zentraler Begriff wirtschaftlicher Sicherheitspolitik.

items.q: Without a valid ____, the firm was legally barred from shipping the controlled equipment abroad.
items.e: „export licence“ = Ausfuhrgenehmigung — zentrale rechtliche Voraussetzung im Exportkontrollrecht.

items.q: Customs demanded an ____ confirming that the equipment would not be diverted to a sanctioned buyer.
items.e: „end-user certificate“ = Endverbleibserklärung, die den tatsächlichen Empfänger und Verwendungszweck bestätigt.

items.q: Investigators discovered that the buyer was in fact a ____ set up to disguise the equipment's true destination.
items.e: „front company“ = Tarnfirma, die die wahre Identität des Empfängers verschleiert.

items.q: The chip designer has no fabrication facilities of its own and depends entirely on a contract ____ overseas.
items.e: „foundry“ = Halbleiter-Auftragsfertiger; die Distraktoren passen nicht zur Chipherstellung.

items.q: Construction of the new ____ is expected to take at least four years and cost tens of billions.
items.e: „fabrication plant“ (kurz „fab“) = Halbleiterfertigungsanlage.

items.q: The export ban targets the most advanced ____ machines, without which the smallest circuit nodes cannot be etched.
items.e: „lithography“ = Fachbegriff für das Belichtungsverfahren der Chipherstellung; die Distraktoren sind keine feststehenden Begriffe der Halbleiterfertigung.

items.q: Anticipating tighter controls, several manufacturers began to ____ critical components as a hedge against future shortages.
items.e: „to stockpile“ = strategisch bevorraten; „hoard“ wirkt negativ/eigennützig, „warehouse“ ist als Verb unüblich, „accumulate“ ist zu allgemein für den strategischen Kontext.

items.q: Domestic suppliers moved quickly to ____ the shortfall left by the departing foreign vendor.
items.e: „to backfill“ = eine entstandene Lücke/einen Engpass auffüllen — gängige Kollokation im Lieferketten-Kontext.

items.q: Lawyers were quick to identify a ____ that allowed shipments to be rerouted through a third country.
items.e: „loophole“ = Gesetzeslücke/Schlupfloch; die anderen Begriffe bezeichnen reguläre Vertrags-/Rechtsbestandteile, keine Umgehungsmöglichkeit.

items.q: Several intermediaries specialise in helping clients ____ the very controls they are meant to observe.
items.e: „to circumvent“ = umgehen; die Distraktoren bedeuten das Gegenteil oder sind neutral.

items.q: The firm was swiftly ____ after investigators traced its shipments to a sanctioned end user.
items.e: „to blacklist“ = auf eine Sperrliste setzen; die Distraktoren bedeuten das Gegenteil oder etwas Neutrales.

items.q: Control over a single chokepoint technology gives a government considerable ____ over rival economies.
items.e: „leverage“ = Hebelwirkung/Einflussmacht — zentraler Begriff der Wirtschaftsdiplomatie.

items.q: The new restrictions were designed to ____ the flow of advanced components to the targeted industry.
items.e: „to choke off“ = eine Zufuhr abwürgen/unterbinden — passendes Phrasal Verb zum Thema Chokepoint.

items.q: A shortage of specialised technicians has become an unexpected ____ in ramping up production.
items.e: „bottleneck“ = Engpass, der den Gesamtprozess verlangsamt.

items.q: The announcement signalled a broader ____ on the export of sensitive manufacturing know-how.
items.e: „clampdown“ = verschärftes, entschlossenes Vorgehen/Restriktion — passt zur angekündigten Verschärfung.

items.q: Officials promised a ____ on brokers found to be facilitating illicit re-exports.
items.e: „crackdown“ = hartes, energisches Vorgehen gegen etwas — stärker als eine bloße Überprüfung.

items.q: Diplomats negotiated a narrow ____ exempting humanitarian medical equipment from the new controls.
items.e: „carve-out“ = gezielte Ausnahmeregelung innerhalb eines größeren Regelwerks.

items.q: As the only viable supplier of the machines, the company effectively became the ____ of the entire industry's growth.
items.e: „gatekeeper“ = Instanz, die den Zugang zu etwas Entscheidendem kontrolliert.

items.q: Analysts warned of significant ____ effects on unrelated sectors once the controls took hold.
items.e: „spillover effect“ = Übergreifen/Ausstrahlungswirkung auf andere Bereiche — feste Kollokation.

items.q: Firms began to ____ against further restrictions by diversifying their supplier base across several countries.
items.e: „to hedge against“ = sich gegen ein Risiko absichern — feste Kollokation, auch im Finanz-/Handelsjargon.

items.q: It is imperative that the licence ____ reviewed before the shipment leaves the port.
items.e: Mandative Subjunctive nach „it is imperative that“ — Grundform „be“ unabhängig vom Subjekt.

items.q: Rarely ____ export controls of this scope been coordinated across so many capitals in recent memory.
items.e: Inversion nach vorangestelltem negativen Adverb „Rarely“: Hilfsverb vor Subjekt; Plural-Subjekt „controls“ und „in recent memory“ verlangen Present Perfect „have… been coordinated“.

items.q: ____ the lithography bottleneck, more than any single sanction, that has reshaped the industry's strategy.
items.e: It-Cleft-Konstruktion „It is X that…“ hebt „the lithography bottleneck“ hervor; der Zeitbezug passt zum Present Perfect „has reshaped“.

items.q: The spokesperson said the ministry ____ the new rules the following month.
items.e: Backshift in indirekter Rede: „will“ wird zu „would“; „the following month“ statt „next month“ bestätigt den Zeitversatz.

items.q: Given the leaked documents, the agency ____ known about the diversion for months before acting.
items.e: „must have + Partizip II“ drückt eine sichere Vermutung über die Vergangenheit aus.

items.q: ____ secured an exemption for medical equipment, the negotiators turned to the harder question of dual-use goods.
items.e: Vorzeitiges Partizip Aktiv „Having secured…“ (= nachdem sie gesichert hatten); „Having been“ wäre Passiv und ergäbe hier keinen Sinn, da die Negotiators selbst handelten.

items.q: No sooner ____ the restrictions been announced than three allied governments issued matching measures.
items.e: Inversion nach „No sooner…than“: Past Perfect „had…been announced“ für die früher abgeschlossene Handlung.

items.q: ____ tighter the controls became, the more inventive the circumvention schemes grew.
items.e: Korrelativkonstruktion „The + Komparativ …, the + Komparativ …“ — hier „The tighter…, the more inventive…“.

items.q: The committee identified the precise mechanism ____ which components were being rerouted through third countries.
items.e: Formelles Relativsatzmuster mit vorangestellter Präposition „…mechanism by which…“ (= „…rerouted by this mechanism“).

items.q: By the time the new regulation takes effect, several firms ____ their supply chains to avoid disruption.
items.e: Future Perfect für eine Handlung, die vor einem zukünftigen Zeitpunkt abgeschlossen sein wird.

items.q: ____ Secretary of Commerce is expected to brief lawmakers on the new licensing requirements next week.
items.e: Bestimmter Artikel bei einmaligen Ämtern/Institutionen („the Secretary of Commerce“).

items.q: Once the front company was identified, investigators wasted no time in ____.
items.e: Bei trennbaren Phrasal Verbs mit Pronomen-Objekt steht das Pronomen zwingend zwischen Verb und Partikel: „tracking it down“, nicht „tracking down it“.

items.q: The ministry ____ to be reviewing the licensing criteria, though no official statement has been issued.
items.e: Unpersönliche Passivkonstruktion mit Infinitiv „is understood to be + -ing“ — gängig im diplomatischen/journalistischen Register für unbestätigte Informationen.

items.q: If only the agency ____ the warning signs sooner, the diversion might have been prevented.
items.e: „If only + Past Perfect“ drückt Bedauern über eine vergangene, nicht erfolgte Handlung aus.

items.q: If the ministry had acted on the intelligence last year, the loophole ____ closed by now.
items.e: Mixed Conditional: vergangene Bedingung (Past Perfect) + gegenwärtiges Ergebnis (would + Infinitiv), da die Auswirkung bis heute andauert.

items.q: The new controls proved ____ effective than officials had originally anticipated.
items.e: Steigerung mit Verstärkung durch „far“ vor dem Komparativ „more effective“.

items.q: Under no circumstances ____ be shipped without a valid end-user certificate.
items.e: Nach vorangestelltem negativen Ausdruck „Under no circumstances“ muss das Hilfsverb vor das Subjekt treten: „may the equipment be shipped“, nicht die normale Wortstellung „the equipment may“.

items.q: Not until the final round of talks ____ the two sides reach a compromise on dual-use goods.
items.e: Inversion nach „Not until…“: im Simple Past wird das Hilfsverb „did“ vor das Subjekt gestellt, gefolgt vom Infinitiv „reach“.

items.q: Officials insisted the exporter had broken no rule; the paperwork ____ comply with every requirement.
items.e: Emphatisches „did“ zur Betonung/Widerlegung eines Zweifels, gefolgt vom Infinitiv „comply“.

items.q: ____ the allied coordination achieved last spring, the controls would already have been circumvented wholesale.
o: If it were not for that
items.e: Formelle Inversion „Were it not for + Nomen“ ersetzt „If it were not for“ im gehobenen Register.

items.q: ____ the agency flagged the shipment earlier, the components would never have reached the sanctioned buyer.
items.e: Bedingungssatz-Inversion ohne „if“: „Had the agency flagged…“ = „If the agency had flagged…“, typisch für den gehobenen/formellen Stil; „If“ allein passt nicht zur Zeitform „flagged“ im Kontext des Type-3-Ergebnisses.

items.q: The negotiators insisted on ____ every clause before signing off on the exemption.
items.e: Nach der festen Präposition „insist on“ folgt zwingend das Gerundium „reviewing“.

items.q: Midway through the audit, the inspectors stopped ____ the paperwork and requested the original certificates instead.
items.e: „stop + Gerundium“ = eine Handlung beenden („aufhören, etwas zu tun“); „stop + to-Infinitiv“ hieße „anhalten, um etwas zu tun“ und ergäbe hier keinen Sinn.

items.q: The delegation insisted that the clause ____ removed from the final text.
items.e: Mandative Subjunctive nach „insist that“: Grundform „be“ unabhängig von Person/Numerus.

items.q: The agreement established a mechanism ____ exemptions could be granted case by case.
items.e: „whereby“ = „durch das/wodurch“ — formelles Relativadverb, das beschreibt, wie ein Mechanismus funktioniert.

items.q: According to the original timetable, the new rules ____ into force at the start of the following quarter.
items.e: „were to + Infinitiv“ (Future in the Past) beschreibt eine aus damaliger Sicht geplante zukünftige Handlung.

run17.note: Aufbau analog Sprachtest Russisch: Teil 1 Textverständnis (8 Fragen zu einem Textabschnitt), Teil 2 Wortschatz/Idiomatik (26 Fragen), Teil 3 Grammatik/Zeitformen (26 Fragen). Jede Frage 1 Punkt, insgesamt 60 Punkte, bestanden ab 30 Punkten (50 %). Trainingsniveau C2 – offizielles Prüfungsniveau C1+. Nicht offiziell.

items.q: What is the central claim the author is making?
o: Currency manipulation charges are easy to prove and routinely successful.
The instruments designed to police currency manipulation are ill-suited to modern, fluid currency markets, allowing diplomats to exploit the ambiguity.
The IMF's Article IV consultations are the most effective enforcement tool available.
The US Treasury's report is purely technical and entirely free of political calculation.
items.e: Kernthese im Schlussabsatz: Die Instrumente wurden „designed for a world of fixed pegs and capital controls, not the fluid, multipolar currency markets of today — and diplomats have grown adept at exploiting the resulting ambiguity.“
items.passage:
Few charges in international economic diplomacy carry quite the same rhetorical charge as that of currency manipulation, and few are quite so difficult to substantiate. The accusation implies a deliberate policy of holding an exchange rate below its equilibrium value in order to cheapen exports and gain an unearned edge over trading partners — a practice that, if proven, would violate the spirit if not always the letter of the IMF's Articles of Agreement. Yet establishing intent, as opposed to mere effect, has proved to be the perennial stumbling block for any government or institution minded to level the charge.

Washington's periodic exercise in naming and shaming — a biannual report that scores trading partners against a checklist of bilateral surplus, current-account surplus and the scale of one-sided intervention — illustrates the difficulty neatly. A country can trip two of the three thresholds through entirely orthodox monetary policy, low interest rates pursued for domestic reasons that happen, as a side effect, to weaken the currency. Whether that constitutes manipulation or merely the unglamorous business of managing an economy is a question the report's authors have never satisfactorily answered, and successive administrations have found the designation more useful as a bargaining chip than as an analytical finding.

The IMF's own Article IV consultations, ostensibly the more rigorous mechanism, suffer a different affliction: they are toothless. A finding of 'fundamental exchange rate misalignment' obliges a government to do precisely nothing beyond enduring an unflattering paragraph in a report few finance ministers read past the executive summary. Sanctions, tariffs and countervailing duties are pursued instead through domestic trade law, where the evidentiary bar is lower and the political payoff considerably higher.

None of which is to say the underlying grievance is imaginary. Persistent, one-sided intervention does distort trade flows, and the accumulation of reserves well beyond any plausible precautionary need is not easily explained as innocent housekeeping. The trouble is that the instruments built to police the offence were designed for a world of fixed pegs and capital controls, not the fluid, multipolar currency markets of today — and diplomats have grown adept at exploiting the resulting ambiguity.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, what does the US Treasury's biannual report use to score trading partners?
o: A checklist of bilateral surplus, current-account surplus and the scale of one-sided intervention.
A single measure of reserve accumulation only.
A vote among G7 finance ministers.
The IMF's Article IV misalignment finding.
items.e: Zitat: „a biannual report that scores trading partners against a checklist of bilateral surplus, current-account surplus and the scale of one-sided intervention.“

items.q: What does the passage say happens when the IMF finds 'fundamental exchange rate misalignment'?
o: The country is automatically referred to the WTO.
The government must devalue or revalue within six months.
The government is obliged to do nothing beyond enduring an unflattering paragraph that few finance ministers read.
items.e: Zitat: „obliges a government to do precisely nothing beyond enduring an unflattering paragraph in a report few finance ministers read past the executive summary.“

items.q: What can be inferred about why governments prefer domestic trade law over IMF findings when pursuing action?
o: Domestic trade law carries a lower evidentiary bar and a higher political payoff.
The IMF has no jurisdiction over any member state whatsoever.
Domestic trade law is faster because it requires no evidence at all.
The WTO forbids the use of IMF findings in trade disputes.
items.e: Schlussfolgerung direkt gestützt durch: „pursued instead through domestic trade law, where the evidentiary bar is lower and the political payoff considerably higher.“

items.q: In the context of the passage, 'toothless' (describing the IMF's Article IV mechanism) most nearly means…
items.e: „toothless“ = zahnlos, d. h. ohne wirksame Durchsetzungsmacht; wird im folgenden Satz durch das Beispiel der wirkungslosen Feststellung belegt.

items.q: The author's attitude toward the US Treasury's currency-manipulator designation can best be described as…
o: skeptical of its analytical rigor, viewing it chiefly as a political bargaining chip
entirely dismissive of the very concept of currency manipulation
items.e: „successive administrations have found the designation more useful as a bargaining chip than as an analytical finding“ zeigt kritische Distanz zum Verfahren, nicht generelle Ablehnung des Themas (siehe letzter Absatz: „the underlying grievance is [not] imaginary“).

items.q: What is the primary function of the final paragraph in the overall argument?
o: To concede that the underlying grievance is real while explaining why current enforcement tools fail to address it.
To introduce a completely new topic unrelated to currency manipulation.
To retract the criticisms made earlier in the passage.
To argue that reserve accumulation is always entirely innocent.
items.e: Konzessiv-Struktur: „None of which is to say the underlying grievance is imaginary“ leitet ein, dass das Problem real ist, bevor erklärt wird, warum die Instrumente dafür ungeeignet sind.

items.q: Why does the passage say a country can trip two of the three US Treasury thresholds without necessarily manipulating its currency?
o: Because low interest rates pursued for domestic reasons can weaken the currency as an unintended side effect.
Because the thresholds are chosen at random each reporting cycle.
Because the Treasury never publishes its methodology.
Because only military allies are exempt from the thresholds.
items.e: Zitat: „through entirely orthodox monetary policy, low interest rates pursued for domestic reasons that happen, as a side effect, to weaken the currency.“

items.q: For nearly two decades the central bank kept its currency ____ to the dollar within a narrow band.
items.e: „to peg a currency (to)“ = eine Währung an eine andere binden/koppeln; feste Kollokation.

items.q: Once capital controls were lifted, the authorities allowed the exchange rate to ____ .
items.e: „to float freely“ = frei/flexibel schwanken lassen; feste Kollokation für einen flexiblen Wechselkurs.

items.q: Critics argued that the currency was deliberately kept ____ to boost export competitiveness.
items.e: „undervalued“ = unterbewertet; Gegensatz zu „overvalued“ (überbewertet).

items.q: The central bank drew down its ____ to defend the currency against a speculative attack.
items.e: „foreign-exchange reserves“ = Devisenreserven; feste Fachkollokation.

items.q: Fears of an imminent devaluation triggered a wave of ____ as investors moved funds offshore.
items.e: „capital flight“ = Kapitalflucht; fester Fachbegriff für den überstürzten Kapitalabzug.

items.q: To offset the inflationary effect of its intervention, the central bank moved to ____ the resulting liquidity.
items.e: „to sterilize (an intervention)“ = die geldpolitischen Nebenwirkungen einer Intervention neutralisieren.

items.q: Under pressure from trading partners, the government eventually agreed to a modest ____ of the yuan.
items.e: „revaluation“ = Aufwertung; Gegensatz zu „devaluation“ (Abwertung), hier durch „modest“ und den Kontext des Drucks von außen nahegelegt.

items.q: The currency board collapsed within days under a sustained ____ .
items.e: „speculative attack“ = spekulativer Angriff auf eine Währung; fester Fachbegriff.

items.q: To stem the outflow of hot money, the finance ministry reluctantly reimposed ____ .
items.e: „capital controls“ = Kapitalverkehrskontrollen; feste Kollokation.

items.q: Exporters in the region increasingly demand payment in ____ rather than the local, inflation-prone denomination.
items.e: „hard currency“ = harte, stabile Währung; Gegensatz zu „soft currency“.

items.q: The peg was redefined to track a ____ of major trading partners' currencies rather than the dollar alone.
items.e: „currency basket“ = Währungskorb, ein gewichteter Durchschnitt mehrerer Währungen.

items.q: Analysts expect the currency to ____ further as capital inflows continue to accelerate.
items.e: „to appreciate“ = an Wert gewinnen (intransitiv); passt zu den beschriebenen Kapitalzuflüssen.

items.q: A persistent ____ was cited by Treasury officials as evidence of an artificially cheap currency.
items.e: „current-account surplus“ = Leistungsbilanzüberschuss; einer der klassischen Indikatoren für Manipulationsverdacht.

items.q: Competitive devaluations of this kind are often dismissed by economists as a ____ policy, since gains for one country come directly at another's expense.
items.e: „beggar-thy-neighbour policy“ = fester ökonomischer Fachbegriff für eine Politik, die dem Nachbarland auf eigene Kosten schadet.

items.q: The regime is best described neither as a hard peg nor a free float, but as a ____ in which the bank intervenes only to smooth volatility.
items.e: „managed float“ = gelenktes Floaten, ein Mittelweg zwischen fixem Peg und freiem Floaten.

items.q: Rather than a single fixed rate, the country adopted a ____ that adjusted gradually in line with inflation differentials.
items.e: „crawling peg“ = gleitende Anbindung mit regelmäßigen kleinen Anpassungen.

items.q: Under the ____ arrangement, every unit of domestic money in circulation was fully backed by foreign reserves.
items.e: „currency board“ = Currency-Board-System mit voller Deckung der Geldmenge durch Devisenreserven.

items.q: In times of turmoil, investors typically flock to currencies regarded as a ____ .
items.e: „safe haven (currency)“ = sicherer Hafen; feste Kollokation für Fluchtwährungen.

items.q: The two central banks established a ____ to ensure either could access the other's currency in a liquidity crunch.
items.e: „currency swap line“ = Währungsswap-Linie zwischen Zentralbanken.

items.q: Economists comparing living standards across countries often adjust exchange rates for ____ .
items.e: „purchasing power parity (PPP)“ = Kaufkraftparität; fester Fachbegriff der Außenwirtschaft.

items.q: The theory of ____ holds that countries benefit from specializing in what they produce relatively most efficiently.
items.e: „comparative advantage“ (Ricardo) = komparativer Vorteil, nicht zu verwechseln mit „competitive advantage“.

items.q: Washington imposed a ____ on the imports after concluding they had been unfairly subsidised.
items.e: „countervailing duty“ = Ausgleichszoll, gezielt gegen unfaire Subventionierung, zu unterscheiden von Anti-Dumping-Maßnahmen.

items.q: By keeping labour costs and the exchange rate low simultaneously, the exporters were able to ____ their foreign rivals on price.
items.e: „to undercut (a rival)“ = preislich unterbieten.

items.q: The central bank spent billions in reserves in a bid to ____ the currency amid the sell-off.
items.e: „to prop up (a currency)“ = stützen; feste Kollokation im Devisenkontext.

items.q: Multinational firms increasingly ____ against currency risk through forward contracts rather than absorbing losses outright.
items.e: „to hedge against (risk)“ = sich mittels Termingeschäften gegen Risiko absichern.

items.q: Persistent inflation can gradually ____ a currency's real value even where the nominal exchange rate remains stable.
items.e: „to erode (value)“ = allmählich aushöhlen/schmälern.

items.q: It is essential that the finance minister ____ the report before the summit.
items.e: Mandativer Konjunktiv nach „It is essential that…“: Grundform unabhängig vom Subjekt.

items.q: If the central bank had intervened earlier, the currency ____ so sharply now.
items.e: Gemischter Konditionalsatz: Bedingung in der Vergangenheit (had intervened), Folge in der Gegenwart (would not be falling).

items.q: Not until the reserves had been nearly exhausted ____ the authorities abandon the peg.
items.e: Vorangestelltes „Not until…“ erzwingt Inversion mit „did“ + Grundform des Verbs.

items.q: ____ that ultimately forced the central bank's hand.
items.e: Es-Spaltsatz (it-cleft) „It was X that…“ betont das Subjekt; Vergangenheitsform passend zum Kontext.

items.q: The governor said the currency ____ undervalued for years.
items.e: Backshift in indirekter Rede: Nach einem Vergangenheitsverb („said“) wird „has been“ zu „had been“ zurückverschoben.

items.q: The intervention ____ better coordinated, given how quickly the rally reversed.
items.e: Modalverb + Perfektinfinitiv „should have been“ = Kritik an einer vergangenen, nicht erfolgten Handlung.

items.q: ____ with mounting pressure from exporters, the government reluctantly agreed to devalue.
items.e: Verkürzter Partizipialsatz mit Partizip Perfekt Passiv „Faced with“, da das Subjekt dem Druck ausgesetzt ist.

items.q: No sooner ____ the peg than speculators began testing the new float.
items.e: Feste invertierte Konstruktion „No sooner had… than…“ mit Past Perfect nach vorangestelltem „No sooner“.

items.q: The more aggressively the central bank intervened, ____ the speculative pressure became.
items.e: Korrelativkonstruktion „the + Komparativ …, the + Komparativ …“.

items.q: The summit ____ the ministers finally reached agreement was held in Basel.
items.e: Formelles Register: vorangestellte Präposition vor dem Relativpronomen („at which“) statt nachgestelltem „which… at“.

items.q: By the time the next Article IV review takes place, the reserves ____ significantly.
items.e: Future Perfect Passive „will have been depleted“ für einen bis zu einem Zeitpunkt in der Zukunft abgeschlossenen Vorgang.

items.q: ____ Secretary of the Treasury is expected to testify before the committee next week.
items.e: Bestimmter Artikel „The“ bei einem einmaligen, eindeutigen Amt; „A/An“ und kein Artikel passen hier nicht.

items.q: The rumours were false, and the spokesperson moved quickly to shoot them ____ .
items.e: Trennbares Phrasal Verb „shoot down“ (Gerüchte widerlegen); das Pronomen-Objekt steht zwingend zwischen Verb und Partikel: „shoot them down“.

items.q: The ambassador explained that the government ____ revalue the currency if pressure persisted.
items.e: Backshift in indirekter Rede: „may“ wird nach einem Vergangenheitsverb zu „might“ zurückverschoben.

items.q: The IMF recommended that the peg ____ reviewed within six months.
items.e: Mandativer Konjunktiv nach „recommended that…“: Grundform, hier passivisch „be reviewed“.

items.q: The currency ____ closely monitored by the central bank since the start of the crisis.
items.e: Present Perfect Passive „has been monitored“ für einen andauernden Zustand seit einem Zeitpunkt in der Vergangenheit („since…“).

items.q: Had the authorities intervened sooner, the sell-off ____ contained.
items.e: Irrealer Bedingungssatz der Vergangenheit (3rd conditional) mit Inversion statt „if“: „Had… intervened“ + „would have been contained“.

items.q: The committee postponed ____ a decision until the next quarterly review.
items.e: „postpone“ wird zwingend mit dem Gerundium ergänzt: „postponed making“, nicht mit dem Infinitiv.

items.q: The central bank ____ intervene, contrary to what critics had predicted.
items.e: Betontes „did“ (emphatic do) hebt hervor, dass die Handlung entgegen der Erwartung tatsächlich stattfand.

items.q: The two governments signed a currency swap agreement ____ each could draw on the other's reserves in an emergency.
items.e: „whereby“ = formelles Relativadverb für „wodurch/durch das“, typisch für Vertragssprache.

items.q: The finance ministry ____ the report translated into three languages before the summit.
items.e: Kausative Konstruktion „have something done“: „had the report translated“ = etwas [von jemandem] machen lassen.

items.q: ____ the negotiations to collapse, both currencies would likely come under renewed pressure.
items.e: Formelle Inversion ohne „if“: „Were… to collapse“ = hypothetischer Bedingungssatz; nur „Were“ passt vor „to collapse“.

items.q: By the time the summit convened, officials ____ for months over the terms of the swap line.
items.e: Past Perfect Continuous „had been negotiating“ betont die andauernde Vorvergangenheit bis zu einem Zeitpunkt in der Vergangenheit.

items.q: The two central banks ____ coordinate their interventions during the previous decade, though the practice has since lapsed.
items.e: „used to“ für eine abgeschlossene, heute nicht mehr bestehende Gewohnheit der Vergangenheit.

items.q: Rarely ____ a currency come under such sustained speculative pressure without government intervention.
items.e: Vorangestelltes „Rarely“ erzwingt Inversion; mit singularischem Subjekt „a currency“ steht das Present-Perfect-Hilfsverb „has“.

items.q: The markets reacted as if the peg ____ already been abandoned.
items.e: Nach „as if/as though“ für eine unreale Vorvergangenheit steht der Past Perfect: „had already been abandoned“.

run18.label: Run 18 – Trainingslauf (C2) · 60 Fragen / 60 Punkte
run18.note: Aufbau analog Sprachtest Russisch: Teil 1 Textverständnis (8 Fragen zu einem Textabschnitt), Teil 2 Wortschatz/Idiomatik (26 Fragen), Teil 3 Grammatik/Zeitformen (26 Fragen). Jede Frage 1 Punkt, insgesamt 60 Punkte, bestanden ab 30 Punkten (50 %). Trainingsniveau C2 – offizielles Prüfungsniveau C1+. Nicht offiziell.

items.q: What is the author's central contention about anti-dumping and countervailing-duty regimes?
o: They are purely technical exercises free from controversy.
Their technical procedures conceal considerable scope for discretion and self-reinforcing outcomes.
They have been rendered obsolete by countervailing duties.
Sunset reviews reliably terminate duties once evidence of dumping disappears.
items.e: Kernthese: Hinter der scheinbar mathematischen Fassade steckt erheblicher Ermessensspielraum, der Ergebnisse begünstigt, die sich selbst verstärken (Wahl des Vergleichslands, Sunset-Reviews, die fast nie zur Aufhebung führen).
items.passage:
For an instrument ostensibly designed to police fair competition, the anti-dumping regime has acquired a curious reputation: many of its keenest users are also its most persistent critics. Investigators calculate a dumping margin by comparing the export price of a good with its 'normal value' in the exporter's home market, then impose duties calibrated to close the gap. In principle the exercise is arithmetic; in practice it is anything but. Where a producer's domestic prices are deemed too distorted by state intervention to serve as a benchmark, authorities reach instead for a 'surrogate' country, substituting the costs of an ostensibly comparable economy. The choice of surrogate can swing a margin from negligible to punitive, and litigants on both sides know it.

Complicating matters further is the injury test that must accompany any finding of dumping: it is not enough to show that goods were sold below normal value; petitioners must also demonstrate that the domestic industry suffered material harm as a result, not merely that it faced competition. Distinguishing the two is seldom straightforward, particularly in sectors plagued by chronic overcapacity, where prices would likely have fallen regardless of any pricing practice abroad. Provisional duties, meanwhile, can be imposed within months of a complaint being lodged, well before the underlying investigation is complete — a sequencing that critics say inverts the presumption of innocence and grants domestic petitioners a valuable head start.

Nor does the story end once duties are imposed. Measures are typically capped at five years, after which a sunset review must establish whether their expiry would likely lead to a recurrence of dumping and injury. In practice, few reviews conclude that it would not; duties, once entrenched, tend to persist by inertia rather than fresh evidence. The parallel machinery of countervailing duties, aimed at subsidised rather than merely underpriced goods, has grown busier still, as governments increasingly treat both instruments as complementary tools for levelling a playing field they suspect was never quite level to begin with.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, how is a dumping margin calculated?
o: By comparing the export price with the price charged domestically in the importing country.
By comparing the export price with the exporter's 'normal value' in its home market.
By calculating the exporter's total production overcapacity.
By comparing subsidy levels across competing exporters.
items.e: Zitat: „comparing the export price of a good with its 'normal value' in the exporter's home market“.

items.q: Why, according to the passage, do investigators sometimes rely on a 'surrogate' country?
o: Because the exporting country lacks any domestic industry.
Because domestic prices in the exporting country are considered too distorted by state intervention to serve as a reliable benchmark.
Because WTO rules require a random benchmark every five years.
Because the importing country demands it for political reasons.
items.e: Zitat: „Where a producer's domestic prices are deemed too distorted by state intervention to serve as a benchmark, authorities reach instead for a 'surrogate' country“.

items.q: What can be inferred about the outcome of most sunset reviews?
o: They almost always result in the immediate lifting of duties.
They tend to renew duties, since a genuine likelihood of recurrence is rarely found to be absent.
They are conducted only once, ever.
They apply exclusively to subsidised goods.
items.e: Inferenz aus: „few reviews conclude that it would not; duties, once entrenched, tend to persist by inertia rather than fresh evidence.“

items.q: In the phrase 'duties, once entrenched, tend to persist by inertia', the word 'entrenched' is closest in meaning to …
items.e: 'entrenched' bedeutet fest verankert/etabliert, nicht abgeschafft oder ausgesetzt.

items.q: Which best characterises the author's tone toward the anti-dumping and countervailing-duty system?
o: Sceptically analytical, highlighting procedural quirks that favour petitioners.
Neutral to the point of indifference, offering no evaluative comment.
items.e: Der Ton ist analytisch-kritisch, z. B. „a sequencing that critics say inverts the presumption of innocence“ — keine Forderung nach Abschaffung, aber deutliche Skepsis.

items.q: What is the primary function of the second paragraph (beginning 'Complicating matters further')?
o: To summarise the entire history of the World Trade Organization.
To introduce the injury test and explain why distinguishing genuine harm from ordinary competition is difficult, especially amid overcapacity.
To describe how surrogate countries are chosen.
To argue that provisional duties should be abolished outright.
items.e: Der Absatz führt den injury test ein und erklärt die Schwierigkeit, Schaden von normalem Wettbewerb zu unterscheiden, besonders bei Überkapazität.

items.q: According to the passage, provisional duties may be imposed …
o: only after the final investigation has concluded.
within months of a complaint being lodged, before the investigation concludes.
only with unanimous WTO member approval.
items.e: Zitat: „Provisional duties, meanwhile, can be imposed within months of a complaint being lodged, well before the underlying investigation is complete“.

items.q: Investigators calculated the ____ by comparing the export price with the normal value in the home market.
items.e: Die Dumpingspanne (dumping margin) ist die Differenz zwischen Exportpreis und Normalwert.

items.q: To offset unfair subsidisation, the commission imposed a ____ on the imported steel.
items.e: Ein Ausgleichszoll (countervailing duty) wird gegen subventionierte Importe verhängt, im Unterschied zum Antidumpingzoll gegen Dumping.

items.q: Before duties can be imposed, authorities must conduct an ____ to establish material harm to domestic producers.
items.e: Der injury test prüft, ob der heimischen Industrie ein materieller Schaden entstanden ist.

items.q: Facing a sudden surge of imports, the government invoked a temporary ____ permitted under WTO rules.
items.e: Eine safeguard measure ist eine befristete Schutzmaßnahme gegen plötzliche Importsteigerungen, unabhängig von unfairem Handel.

items.q: Chronic ____ in the steel sector has depressed global prices for a decade.
items.e: Overcapacity (Überkapazität) bezeichnet Produktionskapazitäten, die die Nachfrage weit übersteigen.

items.q: Five years after the duties took effect, a ____ was launched to decide whether they should be extended.
items.e: Die sunset review prüft nach Ablauf der üblichen fünf Jahre, ob eine Verlängerung der Zölle nötig ist.

items.q: State-directed lending, critics argued, amounted to a serious market ____.
items.e: market distortion = Marktverzerrung; die anderen Optionen bilden keine gängige Kollokation mit 'market'.

items.q: Negotiators insisted that any agreement must guarantee a ____ for domestic and foreign producers alike.
items.e: a level playing field = gleiche Wettbewerbsbedingungen für alle Marktteilnehmer.

items.q: Since the exporter's domestic prices were unreliable, investigators calculated ____ using data from a comparable third country.
items.e: normal value = Normalwert, der Referenzpreis im Herkunftsland zur Ermittlung des Dumpings.

items.q: Where an economy is not treated as market-based, authorities may turn to a ____ instead.
items.e: surrogate country (Vergleichsland) liefert Ersatzdaten, wenn die heimischen Preise als verzerrt gelten.

items.q: The petitioners accused foreign rivals of systematic ____, selling well below prevailing local prices.
items.e: price undercutting = Preisunterbietung; die Konkurrenz bietet bewusst unter dem Marktpreis an.

items.q: Rather than lowering prices outright, the flood of imports caused ____, preventing domestic producers from raising theirs.
items.e: price suppression = Preisdruck/Preisunterdrückung, wenn Preise am Steigen gehindert werden statt gesenkt.

items.q: The commission found that the dumped imports had caused ____ to the domestic industry.
items.e: material injury = wesentlicher Schaden, die zentrale Schwelle im Injury-Test.

items.q: Establishing a ____ between the dumped imports and the industry's decline proved the most contentious part of the case.
items.e: causal link = Kausalzusammenhang zwischen Dumping und Schaden.

items.q: The ____, comprising several mid-sized manufacturers, petitioned for anti-dumping duties.
items.e: domestic industry = heimische Industrie, die den Antrag auf Schutzmaßnahmen stellt.

items.q: Investigators must first define the ____, the precise category of goods under investigation.
items.e: product scope = Warenumfang, die genaue Abgrenzung der untersuchten Produkte.

items.q: Rival exporters complained that cheap government loans functioned as a disguised ____.
items.e: export subsidy = Exportsubvention, staatliche Vergünstigung zur Förderung der Ausfuhr.

items.q: Anti-dumping duties are only one of several available ____ that governments can deploy against unfair trade.
items.e: trade remedy(ies) = handelspolitische Schutzinstrumente, Oberbegriff für Antidumping-, Ausgleichs- und Schutzzölle.

items.q: Some exporters tried to ____ the duties by routing shipments through a third country.
items.e: to circumvent duties = Zölle umgehen, z. B. durch Umladung in Drittländern.

items.q: To close this loophole, the authorities adopted ____ measures covering transshipped goods.
items.e: anti-circumvention measures = Maßnahmen gegen die Umgehung bestehender Zölle.

items.q: When imports from several countries were assessed together, the practice of ____ significantly raised the injury finding.
items.e: cumulation = kumulative Bewertung von Importen aus mehreren Ländern in einer einzigen Schadensanalyse.

items.q: Because the country's prices were shaped by extensive state planning, it was classified as a ____ for the purposes of the investigation.
items.e: non-market economy = Nichtmarktwirtschaft, Status, der die Nutzung eines Vergleichslands rechtfertigt.

items.q: Once confirmed, the duties were applied ____ to shipments made after the announcement of provisional measures.
items.e: retroactively = rückwirkend; Zölle können auf bereits erfolgte Einfuhren rückwirkend angewendet werden.

items.q: The tribunal acknowledged the ____ effect of the dumped imports on smaller competitors.
items.e: injurious effect = schädigende Wirkung; 'injurious' ist das passende Adjektiv zu 'injury'.

items.q: Only companies with demonstrable ____ to file a complaint were permitted to initiate the case.
items.e: standing = Klagebefugnis/Antragsberechtigung, die Voraussetzung, um ein Verfahren einleiten zu können.

items.q: Under the ____, duties were capped at the level needed merely to remove the injury, rather than the full dumping margin.
items.e: lesser-duty rule = Regel, wonach der Zoll nur so hoch angesetzt wird, wie zur Beseitigung des Schadens nötig, auch wenn die Dumpingspanne höher wäre.

items.q: The panel recommended that the tariff ____ immediately.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach 'recommend that': Grundform ohne -s, hier passivisch 'be suspended'.

items.q: If the exporter had disclosed its costs earlier, the investigation ____ so protracted now.
items.e: Gemischter Konditionalsatz: Bedingung in der Vergangenheit (3rd conditional), Konsequenz in der Gegenwart (2nd conditional) → 'would not be'.

items.q: ____ had the duty been lifted than shipments resumed at the old prices.
items.e: 'No sooner had... than...' ist eine feste invertierte Korrelativkonstruktion; nach 'No sooner' folgt Inversion (had + Subjekt).

items.q: ____ the surge in cheap imports that ultimately triggered the safeguard investigation.
items.e: Cleft sentence 'It was X that...' hebt 'the surge in cheap imports' als fokussiertes Satzelement hervor; die Zeitform passt zu 'triggered' (Vergangenheit).

items.q: The spokesperson said the commission ____ the case within six months.
items.e: Backshift in indirekter Rede: 'will' wird zu 'would', da die Einleitung ('said') in der Vergangenheit steht.

items.q: Given the evidence, the tribunal ____ the injury finding much earlier.
items.e: 'should have + Partizip II' drückt eine versäumte, in der Vergangenheit erwartete Handlung aus (Kritik im Nachhinein).

items.q: ____ by mounting overcapacity, the industry lobbied hard for safeguard protection.
items.e: Partizip-Perfekt-Konstruktion (Passiv): 'Squeezed by...' = 'Because it was squeezed by...', verkürzter Passiv-Partizipialsatz.

items.q: ____ the dumping margin, ____ the resulting duty is likely to be.
o: The more high / the more steep
items.e: Doppelte Vergleichskonstruktion 'the + Komparativ, the + Komparativ' drückt proportionale Zunahme aus.

items.q: The regulation ____ the duties were imposed has since been amended.
items.e: Vorangestellte Präposition im Relativsatz (formeller Stil): 'under which' statt 'which... under'.

items.q: By the time the sunset review concludes, the duties ____ in force for a full decade.
items.e: Future Perfect ('will have been') für eine Handlung, die bis zu einem zukünftigen Zeitpunkt abgeschlossen sein wird.

items.q: ____ World Trade Organization has repeatedly urged members to notify new trade-defence measures promptly.
items.e: Bestimmter Artikel 'the' bei einmaligen Institutionen/Organisationen ('the World Trade Organization').

items.q: Investigators uncovered new evidence and decided to ____.
items.e: 'look into' ist ein untrennbares Präpositionalverb; das Pronomen steht nach der gesamten Wendung: 'look into it', nicht *'look it into'.

items.q: Had the exporter cooperated with the investigation, the duty rate ____ considerably lower.
items.e: Invertierter 3. Konditionalsatz ('Had + Subjekt...' statt 'If... had'): Konsequenz 'would have been' + Partizip II.

items.q: The final determination ____ by the trade commission after months of hearings.
items.e: Passiv Simple Past: 'was issued by' — das Subjekt (die Entscheidung) erleidet die Handlung, ausgeführt vom Handelsausschuss.

items.q: The delegation avoided ____ any commitment on the timeline for phasing out the duties.
items.e: Nach 'avoid' folgt zwingend das Gerundium ('avoid making'), kein Infinitiv.

items.q: It is essential that the ruling ____ before the appeal deadline.
items.e: Nach 'it is essential that' steht der mandative Subjunktiv: Grundform 'be published'.

items.q: ____ the exporter's objections, the tribunal upheld the original ruling.
items.e: Nach 'Despite' folgt ein Nomen/eine Nominalphrase ('the exporter's objections'), nicht ein vollständiger Nebensatz wie bei 'Although'.

items.q: The revised methodology proved far ____ transparent than the one it replaced.
items.e: Steigerungsform 'far more + Adjektiv + than' für einen verstärkten Vergleich; 'far' verstärkt den Komparativ 'more'.

items.q: The commission ____ conduct a full review, despite claims that the case was closed.
items.e: Emphatisches 'did' vor dem Grundverb betont, dass die Überprüfung entgegen anderslautender Behauptungen tatsächlich stattfand.

items.q: Officials warned that further delay ____ the credibility of the process.
items.e: Backshift: 'may' wird in der indirekten Rede zu 'might'; danach folgt die Grundform des Verbs.

items.q: ____ after the injury test was completed did the commission authorise provisional duties.
items.e: 'Only after...' am Satzanfang erzwingt Inversion (did + Subjekt + Grundform) im Hauptsatz.

items.q: The specific product ____ the complaint was filed fell outside the initial scope.
items.e: Formelle Relativkonstruktion mit vorangestellter Präposition: 'for which' statt 'which... for'.

items.q: ____ that the exporter had circumvented the duties, investigators recommended anti-circumvention measures.
items.e: Perfekt-Partizipialkonstruktion 'Having concluded that...' zeigt an, dass die Schlussfolgerung der Haupthandlung zeitlich vorausging.

items.q: The exporter ____ known about the investigation, given the extensive public notices.
items.e: 'must have + Partizip II' drückt eine logische Schlussfolgerung über die Vergangenheit aus (starke Vermutung).

items.q: ____ investigators found most striking was the sheer scale of the overcapacity.
items.e: Pseudo-Cleft-Satz mit 'What' am Satzanfang hebt das Objekt der Feststellung hervor ('What investigators found... was...').

items.q: At the time, few analysts believed the duties ____ still be in effect a decade later.
items.e: 'would' als 'future in the past' drückt aus, was aus damaliger Sicht die Zukunft war.

run19.label: Run 19 – Trainingslauf (C2) · 60 Fragen / 60 Punkte
run19.note: Aufbau analog Sprachtest Russisch: Teil 1 Textverständnis (8 Fragen zu einem Textabschnitt), Teil 2 Wortschatz/Idiomatik (26 Fragen), Teil 3 Grammatik/Zeitformen (26 Fragen). Jede Frage 1 Punkt, insgesamt 60 Punkte, bestanden ab 30 Punkten (50 %). Trainingsniveau C2 – offizielles Prüfungsniveau C1+. Nicht offiziell.

items.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Central bank independence is being challenged today mainly through overt, public political pressure rather than the quieter institutional channels of the past, and financial markets punish governments that undermine it.
Central banks have lost all practical independence from elected governments in most major economies over the past decade.
Financial markets are indifferent to political interference with central banks as long as inflation remains under control.
Central bank independence was never a genuine constraint on government policy and has always been largely symbolic.
items.e: Der Text argumentiert, dass der aktuelle Druck auf Notenbanken sich vor allem in seiner öffentlichen, offenen Form von den früheren „slow, deniable channels“ unterscheidet und dass Finanzmärkte auf solche Einmischung reagieren („Financial markets tend to punish such interference swiftly“). Die Optionen B, C und D widersprechen dem Text.
items.passage:
Central bank independence, once regarded as a settled tenet of macroeconomic orthodoxy, is again being tested by politicians who resent monetary policymakers' refusal to bend to electoral timetables. The doctrine rests on a simple insight: governments facing re-election have a structural incentive to loosen monetary policy before voters go to the polls, even at the cost of higher inflation further down the road. Insulating rate-setters from short-term political pressure, the argument runs, allows them to pursue price stability over a longer horizon than any elected government could credibly commit to. Yet this insulation has always been a matter of degree rather than an absolute firewall, and the past decade has exposed just how contingent it can be.

In several economies, heads of government have taken to publicly upbraiding their central bankers for keeping borrowing costs too high, framing restrictive policy as an act of economic sabotage rather than a technical judgement about inflation risk. Some have gone further, floating legislation that would curtail a central bank's statutory mandate or allow the executive to remove a sitting governor before the end of a fixed term. Financial markets tend to punish such interference swiftly: currencies depreciate, long-term bond yields rise, and investors demand a fatter premium for the privilege of holding sovereign debt whose issuer's monetary authority can no longer be trusted to resist short-term political calculation.

What makes the current wave of pressure distinctive is not merely its intensity but the manner in which it is conducted. Rather than working through the slow, deniable channels of appointments and budgetary leverage, critics of independence now air their grievances in public, turning what was once a quiet institutional tug-of-war into a spectacle staged for a domestic audience. Central bankers, for their part, have had to cultivate a new kind of political dexterity, one that lets them defend their mandate without appearing to defy the elected government outright. Whether that balancing act can be sustained indefinitely remains an open question, and one that will shape the credibility of monetary institutions for years to come.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the first paragraph, why do governments facing re-election have an incentive to loosen monetary policy before an election?
o: Because central banks legally require government approval before every election.
Because looser policy can boost short-term economic conditions even if it raises inflation later.
Because voters historically prefer higher interest rates during election campaigns.
Because looser monetary policy permanently eliminates inflation risk.
items.e: Der Text nennt als Motiv, dass Regierungen kurzfristig günstigere Bedingungen schaffen wollen, „even at the cost of higher inflation further down the road“ – also auf Kosten späterer, höherer Inflation. Die anderen Optionen sind im Text nicht belegt bzw. widersprechen ihm.

items.q: Which two market reactions does the passage mention as consequences of political interference with central bank independence?
o: Lower borrowing costs and rising stock prices.
Currency depreciation and rising long-term bond yields.
Reduced sovereign debt and stronger banking sector profits.
items.e: Der Text nennt explizit: „currencies depreciate, long-term bond yields rise“ als typische Marktreaktionen auf politische Einmischung in die Notenbankunabhängigkeit.

items.q: According to the second paragraph, what specific legislative step do some governments consider when pressuring central banks?
o: Legislation that would make central bank governors permanently immune from dismissal.
Legislation requiring central banks to publish more frequent inflation reports.
Legislation that would curtail the central bank's statutory mandate or allow removal of a sitting governor before their term ends.
Legislation transferring monetary policy decisions to international organisations.
items.e: Der Text beschreibt Regierungen, die Gesetze erwägen, die „curtail a central bank's statutory mandate or allow the executive to remove a sitting governor before the end of a fixed term“ – also das Mandat einschränken oder eine vorzeitige Absetzung ermöglichen.

items.q: What can be inferred from the passage about the difference between how political pressure on central banks was exerted in the past and how it is exerted today?
o: Pressure today is conducted more publicly and visibly, whereas it used to rely on quieter, harder-to-trace institutional means.
Pressure today relies exclusively on legal action, whereas past pressure was purely informal.
Pressure on central banks has become weaker overall compared to the past.
Governments today no longer have any means of pressuring central banks.
items.e: Der dritte Absatz kontrastiert die früheren „slow, deniable channels of appointments and budgetary leverage“ mit dem heutigen öffentlichen Austragen von Konflikten („air their grievances in public ... a spectacle staged for a domestic audience“), was Option A stützt.

items.q: In the second paragraph, the word "upbraiding" is closest in meaning to:
items.e: „to upbraid“ bedeutet scharf tadeln/kritisieren. Im Kontext geht es darum, dass Regierungschefs ihre Notenbanker öffentlich scharf kritisieren, nicht loben oder ignorieren.

items.q: Which best describes the author's attitude toward the politicians described in the passage who publicly criticize central bankers?
o: Fully supportive, agreeing that central banks should always follow government preferences.
Neutral to the point of expressing no view at all on the matter.
Admiring, praising politicians for holding unelected officials accountable.
Critical and skeptical, portraying such criticism as short-sighted political interference rather than sound economic judgement.
items.e: Der Autor beschreibt die Kritik der Politiker als „an act of economic sabotage rather than a technical judgement about inflation risk“ und stellt sie damit implizit der sachlichen, fachlichen Einschätzung gegenüber – ein kritischer, distanzierter Ton gegenüber den Politikern.

items.q: What is the primary function of the third paragraph in relation to the rest of the passage?
o: It summarises statistical data on central bank interest rate decisions presented earlier in the passage.
It refutes the claim made in the first paragraph that central bank independence is a matter of degree.
It shifts the focus from describing the mechanisms of political pressure to analysing how the manner of exerting that pressure has changed, and raises an open question about the future.
It provides a historical account of the founding of the first independent central bank.
