items.e: Der dritte Absatz beginnt mit „What makes the current wave of pressure distinctive is not merely its intensity but the manner in which it is conducted“ und endet mit einer offenen Frage zur Zukunftsfähigkeit dieser Balance – er verschiebt den Fokus von den Mechanismen (Absatz 2) hin zur Art und Weise des Drucks.

items.q: Facing persistent inflation above target, the central bank decided to ____ monetary policy by raising its key interest rate for the fourth consecutive quarter.
items.e: „tighten“ (monetary policy) bedeutet, die Geldpolitik zu straffen/verschärfen, z. B. durch Zinserhöhungen. „loosen“ wäre das Gegenteil; „abolish“ (abschaffen) und „postpone“ (verschieben) passen inhaltlich nicht.

items.q: As growth slowed sharply and inflation fell back toward target, policymakers began to ____ monetary policy, cutting rates twice within six months.
items.e: „ease“ (monetary policy) heißt, die Geldpolitik zu lockern, meist durch Zinssenkungen. Die Distraktoren passen nicht zum beschriebenen Zinssenkungs-Szenario.

items.q: Several committee members took a distinctly ____ stance at the meeting, arguing that rates needed to rise further to bring inflation firmly under control.
items.e: „hawkish“ beschreibt eine Haltung, die für straffere Geldpolitik/höhere Zinsen plädiert – im Gegensatz zu „dovish“ (für lockere Geldpolitik).

items.q: Given mounting concerns about a slowdown in hiring, one member adopted a more ____ tone, signalling openness to cutting rates sooner than expected.
items.e: „dovish“ bezeichnet eine Haltung, die eher lockere Geldpolitik/niedrigere Zinsen befürwortet.

items.q: With unemployment at record lows and wages rising rapidly, some economists warned that the economy risked ____ , fuelling further price pressures.
items.e: „overheating“ beschreibt eine Volkswirtschaft, die über ihre nachhaltige Kapazitätsgrenze hinaus wächst und dadurch Inflationsdruck erzeugt.

items.q: The combination of stagnant output and stubbornly high inflation left commentators reaching for the term ____ to describe the economy's predicament.
items.e: „stagflation“ bezeichnet die seltene Kombination aus wirtschaftlicher Stagnation und gleichzeitig hoher Inflation.

items.q: Clear communication about the inflation target helps to ____ households' and firms' expectations, making runaway price spirals less likely.
items.e: „to anchor expectations“ bedeutet, Erwartungen (hier: Inflationserwartungen) stabil und verlässlich zu verankern.

items.q: Once inflation expectations become ____ , they are notably harder to bring back down, since workers and firms start building higher price rises into contracts.
items.e: „entrenched“ (verfestigt/festgesetzt) beschreibt Erwartungen, die sich tief eingenistet haben und schwer zu ändern sind.

items.q: By offering explicit ____ about the likely path of interest rates, the bank aimed to reduce uncertainty in bond markets.
items.e: „forward guidance“ bezeichnet die Kommunikation der Notenbank über die voraussichtliche künftige Zinspolitik, um Markterwartungen zu steuern.

items.q: To support the economy once rates were already near zero, the central bank launched a large-scale programme of ____ , buying government bonds in bulk.
items.e: „quantitative easing“ (QE) ist der Ankauf großer Mengen von Anleihen durch die Notenbank, um zusätzliche Liquidität bereitzustellen, wenn der Leitzins an seiner Untergrenze ist.

items.q: Years of asset purchases left the central bank's ____ several times larger than it had been before the financial crisis.
items.e: Die „balance sheet“ (Bilanz) einer Notenbank umfasst u. a. die gehaltenen Wertpapiere; QE-Programme lassen sie stark anwachsen.

items.q: When short-term rates rise above long-term ones, economists say the ____ has inverted, a pattern often watched as a recession signal.
items.e: Die „yield curve“ (Zinsstrukturkurve) zeigt die Renditen von Anleihen unterschiedlicher Laufzeiten; eine Inversion gilt oft als Rezessionsindikator.

items.q: Fears that the central bank's independence was under threat triggered a wave of ____ , as investors rushed to move funds into safer jurisdictions.
items.e: „capital flight“ bezeichnet die plötzliche, massenhafte Abwanderung von Kapital aus einem Land, meist ausgelöst durch Vertrauensverlust.

items.q: During the episode of political turmoil, investors flocked to traditional ____ assets such as gold and highly rated government bonds.
items.e: „safe haven“ assets gelten als sicherer Hafen, in den Investoren in Krisenzeiten flüchten.

items.q: Investors demanded a higher ____ to compensate for the added uncertainty surrounding the central bank's future course of action.
items.e: Die „risk premium“ (Risikoprämie) ist der zusätzliche Ertrag, den Anleger als Ausgleich für ein höheres wahrgenommenes Risiko verlangen.

items.q: In a banking panic, the central bank's role as ____ allows it to provide emergency liquidity to solvent institutions facing a sudden run.
items.e: „lender of last resort“ (Kreditgeber letzter Instanz) beschreibt die Notenbankfunktion, in einer Krise Banken mit Notliquidität zu versorgen.

items.q: The central bank fine-tunes short-term liquidity in the banking system through routine ____ , buying or selling government securities as needed.
items.e: „open-market operations“ sind Käufe/Verkäufe von Wertpapieren durch die Notenbank am offenen Markt, um die Geldmenge zu steuern.

items.q: By raising the ____ , the regulator forced commercial banks to hold a larger share of deposits in reserve rather than lending them out.
items.e: Die „reserve requirement“ (Mindestreservepflicht) legt fest, welchen Anteil ihrer Einlagen Banken bei der Notenbank als Reserve halten müssen.

items.q: Critics warned of creeping ____ , in which the government's heavy borrowing needs effectively force the central bank to keep rates low regardless of inflation.
items.e: „fiscal dominance“ beschreibt eine Lage, in der hohe Staatsschulden die Notenbank faktisch zwingen, die Geldpolitik den fiskalischen Bedürfnissen unterzuordnen.

items.q: Stripping out volatile food and energy prices, ____ remained stubbornly above the central bank's target throughout the year.
items.e: „core inflation“ (Kerninflation) misst die Preisentwicklung ohne die schwankungsanfälligen Komponenten Energie und Nahrungsmittel.

items.q: A spike in energy prices pushed ____ well above the core rate, even though underlying price pressures had barely changed.
items.e: „headline inflation“ ist die Gesamtinflationsrate einschließlich aller Komponenten wie Energie und Lebensmittel.

items.q: Twelve months of rate hikes produced a gradual ____ , with the pace of price increases slowing steadily without tipping the economy into outright deflation.
items.e: „disinflation“ bezeichnet eine Verlangsamung der Inflationsrate, ohne dass die Preise tatsächlich sinken (das wäre Deflation).

items.q: Policymakers acknowledged that inflation would likely ____ the target for several more quarters before gradually returning to normal.
items.e: „to overshoot“ a target bedeutet, ein Ziel (hier: die Inflationszielmarke) zu übertreffen bzw. darüber hinauszuschießen.

items.q: If households start expecting inflation to stay high indefinitely, their expectations are said to have become ____ from the central bank's official target.
items.e: „de-anchored“ beschreibt Erwartungen, die sich von der offiziellen Zielmarke der Notenbank gelöst haben und nicht mehr daran verankert sind.

items.q: Economists feared that rising wages, passed on by firms as higher prices, could trigger a self-reinforcing ____ .
items.e: Eine „wage-price spiral“ (Lohn-Preis-Spirale) entsteht, wenn steigende Löhne zu steigenden Preisen führen, die wiederum weitere Lohnforderungen auslösen.

items.q: A sharp rate hike in one major economy can produce a ____ effect on emerging markets, as capital shifts toward the higher-yielding currency.
items.e: „spillover effect“ bezeichnet eine Übertragung wirtschaftlicher Effekte (hier: geldpolitische Entscheidungen) auf andere Länder/Märkte.

items.q: The finance minister insisted that the central bank governor ____ before the parliamentary committee to explain the recent rate decision.
items.e: Nach „insist that“ im Sinne von „fordern“ steht der mandative Subjunktiv: Grundform des Verbs ohne -s/-ed, unabhängig vom Subjekt („that ... appear“).

items.q: It is essential that the committee's minutes ____ published in full, rather than in a heavily redacted form.
items.e: Nach „It is essential that ...“ steht ebenfalls der mandative Subjunktiv: „be“ statt „are/is“, da es sich um eine Forderung/Notwendigkeit handelt.

items.q: ____ had the announcement been made than currency traders began selling the national currency in large volumes.
items.e: „No sooner had ... than ...“ ist eine feste invertierte Konstruktion nach vorangestelltem negativen Adverbial; nach der Inversion folgt „than“, nicht „when“.

items.q: ____ have policymakers faced such a delicate balancing act between taming inflation and avoiding a sharp downturn.
items.e: Vorangestellte einschränkende Adverbien wie „Rarely“ lösen Inversion von Hilfsverb und Subjekt aus („Rarely have policymakers faced...“).

items.q: If the bank had raised rates earlier last year, inflation ____ considerably lower today.
items.e: Gemischter Konditionalsatz: Bedingung in der Vergangenheit („had raised“), Konsequenz in der Gegenwart („would be ... today“) – eine typische Mixed-Conditional-Struktur.

items.q: If the governor were less cautious by nature, she ____ the emergency measures announced last month.
items.e: Bedingung in der Gegenwart („were less cautious“), Konsequenz in der Vergangenheit („would never have approved ... last month“) – die zweite Variante des Mixed Conditional.

items.q: ____ that finally persuaded markets the bank was serious about controlling inflation, not the earlier speeches.
items.e: Es-Spaltsatz (it-cleft): „It was X that ...“ hebt „the rate hike“ als den entscheidenden Faktor hervor.

items.q: ____ the committee feared most was a sudden loss of confidence in the currency.
items.e: Wh-Spaltsatz (what-cleft): „What the committee feared most was ...“ betont das Objekt der Furcht.

items.q: ____ under mounting political pressure, the governor nonetheless refused to deviate from the bank's inflation target.
items.e: Partizip-Perfekt-Konstruktion (Past Participle) „Placed under...“ ersetzt einen passiven Nebensatz („Although she was placed under...“).

items.q: ____ studied the data for weeks, the analysts concluded that the slowdown was temporary rather than structural.
items.e: „Having + Partizip II“ („Having studied“) drückt eine abgeschlossene Handlung vor der Haupthandlung aus (Perfect Participle, aktiv).

items.q: The spokesperson said that the bank ____ additional measures if inflation failed to ease over the coming months.
items.e: Bei der indirekten Rede verschiebt sich „will“ zu „would“ (Backshift), da der einleitende Satz in der Vergangenheit steht („said that“).

items.q: She admitted that the earlier forecasts ____ overly optimistic, given how quickly conditions had deteriorated.
items.e: Bei Backshift in der indirekten Rede wird ein einfaches Präteritum („were“) zu „had been“ (Plusquamperfekt), da sich die Aussage auf einen noch früheren Zeitpunkt bezieht.

items.q: Given how sharply bond yields reacted, the announcement ____ far more market-moving than officials had anticipated.
items.e: „must have been“ drückt eine sichere Vermutung über die Vergangenheit aus (Modalverb + Perfektinfinitiv).

items.q: In hindsight, the committee ____ rates more gradually instead of raising them so abruptly.
items.e: „should have + Partizip II“ drückt Kritik an einer vergangenen Handlung aus: Eine bessere Alternative wäre möglich gewesen, wurde aber nicht gewählt.

items.q: The reform package addressed ____ the central bank's mandate ____ its governance structure.
items.e: „not only ... but also ...“ ist eine korrelative Konjunktion, die zwei Elemente gleichzeitig hervorhebt und verbindet.

items.q: ____ the finance ministry ____ the central bank was willing to take public responsibility for the policy failure.
items.e: „Neither ... nor ...“ verneint beide genannten Elemente gleichzeitig („weder ... noch“).

items.q: The extent ____ the bank can act independently of the government remains a matter of ongoing legal debate.
items.e: Bei formellem Stil steht die Präposition vor dem Relativpronomen: „the extent to which ...“ statt eines nachgestellten „which ... to“.

items.q: The legislation ____ the governor's dismissal would be based has not yet been drafted in detail.
items.e: „the legislation on which X would be based“ – eine formelle Relativsatzkonstruktion mit vorangestellter Präposition (von „based on the legislation“ zu „on which“).

items.q: The rate increase was ____ unexpected that markets took several days to fully price in its consequences.
items.e: „so + Adjektiv + that“ bildet die emphatische Konsekutivstruktur; „such“ würde ein Substantiv statt eines bloßen Adjektivs verlangen.

items.q: It was ____ a turbulent week for currency markets that several analysts revised their forecasts twice within days.
items.e: „such + a/an + Adjektiv + Substantiv + that“ ist die Konsekutivstruktur mit Substantiv („such a turbulent week“); „so“ würde hier kein Substantiv direkt vor sich zulassen.

items.q: ____ how cautious the governor tried to appear, investors sensed that a shift in policy was imminent.
items.e: „No matter how + Adjektiv + Subjekt + Verb“ leitet einen Konzessivsatz ein („egal wie ...“); „Despite“ würde ein Nomen/Gerundium statt eines vollständigen Satzes verlangen.

items.q: ____ the fact that inflation had eased slightly, the committee remained wary of declaring victory too soon.
items.e: „Despite the fact that ...“ ist eine feste Wendung, bei der „despite“ mit „the fact that“ und einem vollständigen Satz kombiniert wird; die anderen Optionen benötigen kein „the fact that“.

items.q: By the time the next policy meeting takes place, the committee ____ six consecutive rate decisions this cycle.
items.e: Future Perfect („will have made“) beschreibt eine Handlung, die bis zu einem bestimmten zukünftigen Zeitpunkt („by the time ...“) abgeschlossen sein wird.

items.q: By next year, the bank ____ its current tightening cycle for nearly three years without a single pause.
items.e: Future Perfect Continuous („will have been running“) betont die Dauer einer Handlung, die bis zu einem zukünftigen Zeitpunkt ununterbrochen andauert.

items.q: After the controversy broke, the ministry ____ an independent audit of the bank's balance sheet conducted by outside experts.
items.e: Kausativkonstruktion „have something done“: „had an independent audit ... conducted by outside experts“ bedeutet, dass die Prüfung von anderen durchgeführt wurde. „make“ würde „make someone do something“ ohne „by“ verlangen, nicht diese Passivstruktur.

items.q: ____ the government to interfere directly with interest-rate decisions, investor confidence would collapse almost overnight.
items.e: „Were the government to interfere ...“ ist eine invertierte, formelle Variante von „If the government were to interfere ...“ (hypothetischer Konditionalsatz Typ 2 mit „were to“).

run20.label: Run 20 – Trainingslauf (C2) · 60 Fragen / 60 Punkte
run20.note: Aufbau analog Sprachtest Russisch: Teil 1 Textverständnis (8 Fragen zu einem Textabschnitt), Teil 2 Wortschatz/Idiomatik (26 Fragen), Teil 3 Grammatik/Zeitformen (26 Fragen). Jede Frage 1 Punkt, insgesamt 60 Punkte, bestanden ab 30 Punkten (50 %). Trainingsniveau C2 – offizielles Prüfungsniveau C1+. Nicht offiziell.

items.q: Which claim lies at the heart of the author's argument?
o: Sovereign wealth funds no longer pose any real risk to host economies.
Investment screening has become inseparable from industrial rivalry, whatever officials claim.
Screening mechanisms are applied evenly regardless of a fund's country of origin.
Golden shares have replaced screening as the preferred tool of governments.
items.e: Der Schlusssatz macht klar: Sicherheits- und Industriepolitik-Motive sind längst untrennbar verschmolzen, auch wenn Beamte das Gegenteil behaupten.
items.passage:
Few would have predicted, a generation ago, that ministries once preoccupied with tariffs and quotas would find themselves scrutinising the provenance of a bid for a seaport or a semiconductor fab. Yet the screening of inbound investment — once a niche concern of a handful of capitals — has become a fixture of statecraft. State-owned funds, flush with the proceeds of oil, gas or accumulated trade surpluses, now roam global markets in search of yield, and governments on the receiving end have grown correspondingly wary of what such capital might buy alongside a stake.

The mechanics of screening vary, but the underlying anxiety does not. Boards convened to vet foreign purchases typically ask three questions: does the target sit astride critical infrastructure — ports, grids, data pipelines; does the acquirer answer, however indirectly, to a foreign government; and could today's minority stake become tomorrow's lever of coercion. Where the answer to any of these trends towards yes, transactions are delayed, conditioned or blocked outright, often on grounds that stop well short of proving malign intent. Boosters of open capital markets grumble that this amounts to protectionism dressed in the language of security; skeptics of unfettered inflows retort that waiting for proof of harm is a poor strategy when the harm, once done, cannot be undone.

What is seldom acknowledged, in either camp, is how unevenly the burden falls. A fund domiciled in a country with a pliant, opaque state apparatus attracts scrutiny that a fund from a transparent, allied jurisdiction rarely does — a distinction that is defensible on the merits but awkward to state plainly in a communiqué. Reciprocity, the principle that a country should extend to others only the openness it receives in turn, offers a tidy justification, yet it sits uneasily beside the claim that screening is merely about security and not about industrial rivalry. The honest answer, uncomfortable as it is for officials fond of technocratic language, is that the two motives have become inseparable, and pretending otherwise serves nobody's interests but the drafters' own.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, which three questions do screening boards typically ask about a bid?
o: Whether the price is fair, whether shareholders approve, and whether taxes are paid.
Whether the target touches critical infrastructure, whether the acquirer answers to a foreign government, and whether a stake could later become leverage.
Whether the buyer is profitable, whether the sector is regulated, and whether unions object.
Whether the currency is convertible, whether tariffs apply, and whether the deal is public.
items.e: Der zweite Absatz nennt genau diese drei Prüffragen (kritische Infrastruktur, staatliche Anbindung des Käufers, künftiger Hebel/Zwang).

items.q: What do skeptics of unfettered capital inflows argue, per the passage?
o: That waiting for proof of harm is unwise since the damage may be irreversible once done.
That screening boards should be abolished entirely.
That reciprocity is an outdated and unnecessary principle.
That sovereign wealth funds should be banned from all Western markets.
items.e: Zitat: „waiting for proof of harm is a poor strategy when the harm, once done, cannot be undone.“

items.q: What can be inferred about how scrutiny is applied to different funds?
o: All sovereign wealth funds face identical procedures regardless of origin.
Funds from opaque, state-dominated jurisdictions attract more scrutiny than those from transparent allies, even though this is rarely stated openly.
Funds from transparent jurisdictions are screened more strictly to appear fair.
Scrutiny depends solely on the size of the investment, not its origin.
items.e: Der dritte Absatz beschreibt eine ungleiche, aber selten offen ausgesprochene Handhabung je nach Herkunftsstaat.

items.q: In the passage, the word 'pliant' (paragraph 3) most nearly means …
items.e: „pliant“ bedeutet „fügsam/leicht lenkbar“ — hier bezogen auf einen Staatsapparat, der sich leicht beeinflussen lässt.

items.q: Which best characterises the author's attitude towards officials' framing of screening as purely about security?
o: Mildly skeptical, implying the framing is a convenient simplification
Outraged and dismissive of screening altogether
items.e: Formulierungen wie „awkward to state plainly“ und „pretending otherwise serves nobody's interests but the drafters' own“ zeigen dezente Skepsis, keinen offenen Zorn.

items.q: What is the main function of the final paragraph within the passage's overall argument?
o: To introduce the topic of sovereign wealth funds for the first time
To summarise the three screening questions listed earlier
To complicate the security-only justification by exposing the entangled motive of industrial rivalry
To provide statistical evidence for the size of sovereign wealth funds
items.e: Der letzte Absatz stellt die vorher genannte Sicherheits-Begründung infrage, indem er sie mit industriepolitischer Rivalität verknüpft.

items.q: How does the passage define 'reciprocity' in this context?
o: The idea that a country should extend openness to others only to the degree it receives in turn
The requirement that all investors disclose their tax records
A legal doctrine unrelated to investment screening
The practice of mirroring exactly another country's tariff schedule
items.e: Reciprocity wird im Text definiert als Prinzip, Offenheit nur im Ausmaß der erhaltenen Gegenseitigkeit zu gewähren.

items.q: Rising ____ into the ports sector prompted lawmakers to draft new screening legislation.
items.e: „foreign direct investment“ (FDI) ist der feste Fachbegriff für ausländische Direktinvestitionen; die anderen Varianten existieren so nicht.

items.q: The proposed takeover of the chipmaker was referred for a full ____ before any clearance could be considered.
items.e: „national-security review“ ist der feste Fachbegriff für eine sicherheitspolitische Überprüfung von Investitionen.

items.q: Power grids, ports and telecommunications networks are routinely classified as ____.
items.e: „critical infrastructure“ ist die feste Kollokation für sicherheitsrelevante Grundversorgungsanlagen.

items.q: Semiconductors are widely regarded as a ____ in which foreign control is closely watched.
items.e: „strategic sector“ bezeichnet eine für die nationale Sicherheit/Wirtschaft besonders wichtige Branche.

items.q: Even after privatisation, the ministry retained a ____ that allowed it to veto any sale of the port to a foreign buyer.
items.e: „golden share“ ist eine spezielle Vorzugsaktie mit Vetorecht, die dem Staat nach Privatisierungen verbleibt.

items.q: Having failed to obtain clearance, the fund was hit with a ____ requiring it to sell the terminal within a year.
items.e: „divestment order“ ist die feste Bezeichnung für eine behördliche Veräußerungsanordnung.

items.q: The ____ of the shipyard by a state-linked buyer drew scrutiny from three separate ministries.
items.e: „acquisition“ (Erwerb/Übernahme) ist das gebräuchliche Substantiv; die anderen Formen sind unidiomatisch in diesem Kontext.

items.q: Over eighteen months, the fund quietly built up a sizeable ____ in the utility company.
items.e: „a stake in a company“ = ein Anteil an einem Unternehmen; die übrigen Formen passen grammatisch nicht in die Lücke.

items.q: Every bid above the statutory threshold must be ____ by an interagency panel before it can proceed.
items.e: „to vet“ = sorgfältig prüfen/überprüfen; „veto“, „vest“ und „vex“ haben andere Bedeutungen.

items.q: The deal finally received regulatory ____ once the buyer agreed to divest the port terminal.
items.e: „regulatory clearance“ = behördliche Freigabe; die anderen Formen sind kein feststehender Fachbegriff.

items.q: Critics complained that the exemption for portfolio investors left a ____ wide enough for state funds to slip through.
items.e: „loophole“ = Gesetzeslücke, feste Kollokation; die übrigen Ausdrücke existieren so nicht.

items.q: The new clause was billed as a ____ against covert foreign control of the grid operator.
items.e: „safeguard against“ = Schutzmaßnahme gegen; die Alternativen sind keine gängigen Ausdrücke.

items.q: Even a minority stake can, over time, translate into disproportionate ____ over a company's strategic decisions.
items.e: „leverage over“ = Einfluss/Hebelwirkung auf; die übrigen Formen sind grammatisch unpassend.

items.q: The sovereign fund agreed to ____ a substantial share of the terminal's construction costs.
items.e: Nach „agreed to“ folgt der reine Infinitiv: „to underwrite“ = finanziell absichern/übernehmen.

items.q: The conglomerate's ____ in the domestic energy sector had expanded quietly for a decade before regulators noticed.
items.e: „footprint“ = wirtschaftliche Präsenz/Reichweite eines Unternehmens in einem Sektor.

items.q: Investigators complained that the fund's ownership structure was frustratingly ____.
items.e: „opaque“ (Adjektiv) = undurchsichtig; nach „was frustratingly“ wird ein Adjektiv benötigt.

items.q: The takeover bid came under unprecedented ____ from no fewer than three regulators.
items.e: „come under scrutiny“ = einer Prüfung unterzogen werden; die Lücke verlangt das Substantiv.

items.q: The fund is legally ____ in a jurisdiction with minimal disclosure requirements.
items.e: „to be domiciled in“ = seinen (Rechts-)Sitz haben in; Partizip Perfekt nach „is“.

items.q: The consortium's ____ for the port operator was ultimately rejected on national-security grounds.
items.e: „a bid for something“ = ein Übernahmeangebot; die übrigen Formen passen nicht in die Lücke.

items.q: Investigators suspected the shell company served merely as a ____ for capital originating with a foreign ministry.
items.e: „conduit for“ = Kanal/Durchleitungsstelle für (Kapital); Verwechslung mit „conduct“ ist die typische Falle.

items.q: The sale proceeds gave the fund a welcome ____ against falling commodity revenues.
items.e: „a cushion against“ = ein finanzieller Puffer gegen; Substantiv nach unbestimmtem Artikel.

items.q: The fund's ____ spans real estate, port terminals and data centres across four continents.
items.e: „portfolio“ = Anlagenbestand/Beteiligungsportfolio; einzige grammatisch korrekte Option.

items.q: The holding company was widely regarded as a ____ for the ministry that ultimately controlled it.
items.e: „a proxy for“ = ein Stellvertreter/verdecktes Werkzeug für; Singular nach unbestimmtem Artikel.

items.q: The revised rules ____ a narrow exemption for pension and university endowment investors.
items.e: „to carve out an exemption“ = eine Ausnahme schaffen/herausarbeiten; „carve up“ bedeutet etwas ganz anderes (aufteilen).

items.q: A sudden commodity ____ enabled the fund to triple its overseas holdings within two years.
items.e: „windfall“ = unerwarteter (Gewinn-)Zufall, hier durch Rohstoffpreise; feste Kollokation.

items.q: Diplomats justified the tighter rules by invoking ____: openness would be extended only where it was returned in kind.
items.e: „reciprocity“ = Gegenseitigkeitsprinzip; die einzige idiomatische Substantivform hier.

items.q: The committee recommended that the fund ____ its stake in the grid operator within twelve months.
items.e: Nach „recommend that“ steht der mandative Konjunktiv: Grundform ohne -s, unabhängig vom Subjekt.

items.q: If the review board had blocked the acquisition, the port ____ still in domestic hands today.
items.e: Gemischter Konditionalsatz: unreale Bedingung in der Vergangenheit („had blocked“), Ergebnis in der Gegenwart („would be“).

items.q: Not only ____ the deal raise security concerns, it also triggered a parliamentary inquiry.
items.e: Nach vorangestelltem „Not only“ folgt Inversion mit Hilfsverb; da die Handlung abgeschlossen ist, steht „did“.

items.q: It was the finance ministry, not the security services, ____ ultimately blocked the transaction.
items.e: In einem Cleft-Satz („It was X that…“) mit Bezug auf eine Institution ist „that“ die idiomatische Wahl.

items.q: The spokesperson said the fund ____ never sought a controlling stake, only a passive one.
items.e: Backshift in der indirekten Rede: Present Perfect in der direkten Rede wird zu Past Perfect.

items.q: Given the scale of the stake, the acquisition ____ screened long before it reached the board.
items.e: „should have been screened“ drückt eine versäumte, im Nachhinein bedauerte Handlung aus (Modalverb + Perfekt Passiv).

items.q: Funds ____ by opaque state entities face considerably more scrutiny than their transparent counterparts.
items.e: Verkürzter Relativsatz im Passiv: „Funds (which are) controlled by…“ wird zum Partizip Perfekt.

items.q: The more opaque a fund's ownership structure, ____ the scrutiny it is likely to attract.
items.e: Korrelativkonstruktion „the + Komparativ …, the + Komparativ …“; „great“ wird zu „greater“.

items.q: The sector ____ the veto applies is defined narrowly under the new statute.
items.e: Bei vorangestellter Präposition im Relativsatz (formelles Register) ist „to which“ korrekt, nicht „that“.

items.q: By the time the review concludes, the fund ____ its stake for over a year.
items.e: Future Perfect für eine Handlung, die bis zu einem zukünftigen Zeitpunkt abgeschlossen sein wird.

items.q: ____ Secretary of the Treasury chairs the interagency committee that reviews sensitive acquisitions.
items.e: Bei einem einzigartigen Amt (nur eine Person hat diesen Titel) steht der bestimmte Artikel „the“.

items.q: The fund's ownership structure ____ to be far more layered than initially disclosed.
items.e: „is believed to be“ = man nimmt an, dass…; unpersönliches Passiv mit Infinitivkonstruktion.

items.q: The ministry insisted ____ every bid above the threshold before granting clearance.
items.e: Nach der Präposition „insist on“ folgt zwingend das Gerundium.

items.q: Had the golden share not existed, the government ____ the sale of the port entirely.
items.e: Irrealer Konditionalsatz der Vergangenheit (Typ 3) mit invertiertem „Had“ statt „If“.

items.q: The panel ____ raise concerns about reciprocity, even though the final report barely mentions it.
items.e: Emphatisches „did“ vor dem Vollverb betont den Gegensatz zum knappen Abschlussbericht.

items.q: The sooner the disclosure requirements are met, ____ the review can proceed.
items.e: Zweiter Teil der „the…the…“-Konstruktion verlangt ebenfalls „the + Komparativ“.

items.q: The energy sector attracted fresh restrictions, and so ____ the telecommunications industry.
items.e: Elliptische Struktur „so + Hilfsverb + Subjekt“; da „attracted“ im Simple Past steht, folgt „did“.

items.q: Officials later admitted they wished the board ____ the risks more carefully before clearance was granted.
items.e: Nach „wish“ mit Bezug auf die Vergangenheit steht das Past Perfect, um Bedauern über Vergangenes auszudrücken.

items.q: ____ the fund met every disclosure requirement, the acquisition was still delayed by six months.
items.e: Vor einem vollständigen Satz (Subjekt+Verb) steht die Konjunktion „even though“, nicht die Präposition „despite“.

items.q: The clause was drafted ____ regulators could intervene before a controlling stake changed hands.
items.e: „so that“ leitet einen vollständigen Finalsatz mit eigenem Subjekt und Verb ein.

items.q: Once the review board ____ its findings, the ministry will decide whether to grant clearance.
items.e: In Zeitsätzen mit „once“ steht für die Zukunft das Present Simple, nicht „will“.

items.q: The fund had its ownership structure ____ by an independent auditor before submitting the bid.
items.e: Kausativkonstruktion „have something done“: Partizip Perfekt nach dem Objekt.

items.q: Only after the divestment order was issued ____ the fund begin negotiations with a buyer.
items.e: Nach vorangestelltem „Only after…“ folgt Inversion mit „did“ + Grundform des Verbs.

items.q: It is essential that the board ____ independent of political pressure when reviewing sensitive bids.
items.e: Nach „it is essential that“ steht ebenfalls der mandative Konjunktiv (Grundform ohne -s).

items.q: The fund ____ to have quietly acquired stakes in at least four grid operators before regulators intervened.
items.e: „is said to have + Partizip“ = man sagt, dass (in der Vergangenheit) …; unpersönliche Passivkonstruktion.

items.q: Rarely ____ a screening decision provoked as much diplomatic friction as this one.
items.e: Nach vorangestelltem „Rarely“ folgt Inversion; da es sich um ein Ergebnis mit Gegenwartsbezug handelt, steht das Present Perfect „has“.

run21.label: Run 21 – Trainingslauf (C2) · 60 Fragen / 60 Punkte
run21.note: Aufbau analog Sprachtest Russisch: Teil 1 Textverständnis (8 Fragen zu einem Textabschnitt), Teil 2 Wortschatz/Idiomatik (26 Fragen), Teil 3 Grammatik/Zeitformen (26 Fragen). Jede Frage 1 Punkt, insgesamt 60 Punkte, bestanden ab 30 Punkten (50 %). Trainingsniveau C2 – offizielles Prüfungsniveau C1+. Nicht offiziell.

items.q: What is the main point the author seeks to establish?
o: NATO's two-percent target should be abandoned altogether.
A single spending ratio is a poor proxy for genuine military readiness and cannot alone restore alliance credibility.
European governments have secretly agreed to ignore Washington's demands.
Only the United States has ever met the two-percent guideline.
items.e: Kernthese: Eine einzelne Prozentzahl sagt wenig über echte Einsatzbereitschaft aus. Beleg: „Reducing alliance cohesion to a single ratio therefore risks rewarding the wrong behaviour.“
items.passage:
For three decades, NATO's two-percent guideline functioned less as a binding commitment than as a convenient fiction, invoked at every summit and honoured by scarcely a handful of members. That fiction has become considerably harder to sustain since the alliance's eastern flank found itself staring down a revisionist neighbour rather than a hypothetical one. Washington's patience, never limitless even under administrations professedly devoted to the transatlantic project, has worn visibly thin; the refrain that Europe must shoulder a fairer share of its own defence is no longer confined to campaign rhetoric but has hardened into explicit policy.

The difficulty is that burden-sharing, for all the neatness of the percentage target, obscures more than it reveals. A country that spends lavishly on legacy platforms and bloated procurement bureaucracies may hit two percent while fielding forces that could not sustain a fortnight of high-intensity combat; another, spending rather less, may possess niche capabilities — cyber-defence units, special forces, strategic airlift — that punch well above their budgetary weight. Reducing alliance cohesion to a single ratio therefore risks rewarding the wrong behaviour: procurement for its own sake rather than genuine deterrence.

Nor is the politics straightforward. Governments that raise defence spending must find the money somewhere, and few electorates reward ministers who trade hospital beds for howitzers. The temptation, understandably, is to phase increases gradually, back-loading the heaviest commitments onto successors who may never have to honour them. Officials in Brussels profess confidence that the trajectory is now settled beyond dispute; sceptics retort that they have heard such assurances before, at summit after summit, only to watch the promised curve flatten once the cameras were switched off.

What ultimately distinguishes this moment from earlier rounds of transatlantic grumbling is not the rhetoric, which is depressingly familiar, but the underlying threat perception. When the danger was abstract, two percent was an aspiration to be quietly shelved; when it is concrete, the figure becomes a floor rather than a ceiling, and the alliance's credibility rests on proving, this time, that the difference is more than semantic.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, what has historically been true of the two-percent guideline?
o: It was strictly enforced by binding treaty obligations.
It was honoured by nearly every member state.
It functioned more as a convenient fiction than a binding commitment.
It was introduced only after fighting began on NATO's eastern flank.
items.e: Zitat: „functioned less as a binding commitment than as a convenient fiction.“

items.q: Why does the author say that hitting two percent can be misleading?
o: Because some states inflate their figures fraudulently.
Because spending on legacy platforms and bloated bureaucracies may coexist with forces unfit for sustained combat.
Because the target only applies to nuclear-armed members.
Because NATO no longer publishes national spending data.
items.e: Absatz 2: Zwei-Prozent-Erfüllung sagt nichts über echte Kampffähigkeit („could not sustain a fortnight of high-intensity combat“).

items.q: What can be inferred about Washington's attitude towards European burden-sharing?
o: It has grown markedly less tolerant of European under-investment, regardless of which administration is in office.
It has lost all interest in the alliance's future.
It privately supports Europe's reluctance to raise spending.
It considers the two-percent target excessive.
items.e: Schlussfolgerung aus „never limitless even under administrations professedly devoted to the transatlantic project, has worn visibly thin.“

items.q: In the phrase 'punch well above their budgetary weight,' the words most nearly mean that certain capabilities …
o: achieve an effect out of proportion to their modest cost.
are physically located above ground level.
have been discontinued due to budget cuts.
items.e: Idiom „to punch above one's weight“ = größere Wirkung erzielen, als das (Budget-)Gewicht vermuten lässt.

items.q: The author's overall tone towards NATO officials' assurances of a 'settled' trajectory is …
o: sceptical, noting a history of unfulfilled promises.
items.e: „sceptics retort that they have heard such assurances before... only to watch the promised curve flatten.“

items.q: What is the primary function of the third paragraph (beginning 'Nor is the politics straightforward')?
o: To introduce a competing statistical methodology.
To explain the domestic political constraints that slow defence-spending increases.
To refute the entire argument of the preceding paragraph.
items.e: Erklärt die innenpolitische Ökonomie steigender Verteidigungsausgaben („trade hospital beds for howitzers“).

items.q: What does the author identify as the crucial difference between this round of burden-sharing pressure and earlier ones?
o: The rhetoric used by officials has become entirely new.
The underlying threat is now concrete rather than abstract.
The United States has withdrawn from the alliance.
The two-percent target has been officially abolished.
items.e: Schlussabsatz: „When the danger was abstract... when it is concrete, the figure becomes a floor rather than a ceiling.“

items.q: The ministry launched a review of its defence ____ processes after cost overruns.
items.e: „procurement“ = Beschaffung(swesen); „purchasement“ existiert nicht, „acquirement“ ist veraltet/unpassend, „provisioning“ zu unspezifisch.

items.q: Washington has pressed its allies for years to accept a fairer form of ____ .
items.e: Etablierter Fachbegriff „burden-sharing“ = Lastenteilung; die übrigen Optionen sind keine gängigen Fachtermini.

items.q: The supplementary budget has ____ two billion euros for air-defence systems.
items.e: „to earmark funds for“ = Mittel zweckbinden.

items.q: The ministry moved to ____ additional ammunition ahead of a harsh winter.
items.e: „to stockpile“ = Vorräte anlegen, militärischer Fachterminus.

items.q: Several ageing frigates were ____ rather than decommissioned outright.
items.e: „to mothball“ = vorübergehend außer Dienst stellen (militärischer Fachbegriff).

items.q: Joint exercises are designed above all to test allied forces' ____ .
items.e: „interoperability“ ist der feste NATO-Fachbegriff, nicht durch ein allgemeines Synonym ersetzbar.

items.q: Analysts describe the alliance's revised force ____ as markedly more forward-leaning.
items.e: „force posture“ = Streitkräftedislozierung/-haltung, feste Fachfügung im Singular.

items.q: The alliance activated its ____ within hours of the incursion.
items.e: Offizieller NATO-Terminus für die schnelle Eingreiftruppe.

items.q: Few member states retain a genuinely ____ capability able to deploy far from home territory.
items.e: „expeditionary“ = zur Entsendung fähig; Verwechslungsgefahr mit „expedient“ (zweckmäßig) und „expeditious“ (zügig).

items.q: The report identifies a serious ____ in long-range air defence.
items.e: Feste sicherheitspolitische Fachfügung „capability gap“.

items.q: Modern warfare in the region has settled into a grinding war of ____ .
items.e: „war of attrition“ = Abnutzungskrieg, feste Fügung; die anderen Substantive kollokieren nicht mit „war of“.

items.q: Both powers have preferred to fight by ____ rather than risk direct confrontation.
items.e: „to fight by proxy“ = einen Stellvertreterkrieg führen, feste Fügung.

items.q: Insurgents rely on ____ tactics precisely because they cannot match conventional firepower.
items.e: Militärischer Fachbegriff „asymmetric warfare/tactics“.

items.q: ____ of a cyber-attack to a specific state actor can take investigators months.
items.e: Fachbegriff der Cyber-Sicherheit: „attribution“ = Zuordnung eines Angriffs zu einem Urheber.

items.q: Diplomats gathered in Geneva for the latest ____ treaty review conference.
items.e: Offizieller Name: „Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT)“.

items.q: Inspectors are tasked with verifying compliance with the agency's ____ agreements.
items.e: IAEO-Fachbegriff „safeguards agreements“ = Sicherungsabkommen.

items.q: Concerns centre on the country's uranium ____ programme.
items.e: Nuklearer Fachbegriff „enrichment“ = Anreicherung.

items.q: The missile is capable of carrying a single nuclear ____ .
items.e: „warhead“ = Sprengkopf; „spearhead“ (Speerspitze/Vorhut) und „forehead“ (Stirn) sind Wortbildungsfallen.

items.q: Private ____ have increasingly filled roles once reserved for national armies.
items.e: Korrekte Pluralform „mercenaries“; „merchants“ (Kaufleute) ist ein Fehlgriff durch Klangähnlichkeit.

items.q: Firms must obtain a formal ____ before operating as military contractors abroad.
items.e: Britisches Englisch unterscheidet Substantiv „licence“ von Verb „license“.

items.q: Critics argue that private contractors operate with insufficient ____ .
items.e: „accountability“ = Rechenschaftspflicht; „accountancy“ bedeutet Buchhaltung(swesen) — klassische Verwechslung.

items.q: The prosecutor secured an ____ against three former contractors for war crimes.
items.e: Korrekte Schreibweise „indictment“ (stummes 'c'); die übrigen Formen existieren nicht.

items.q: The firm was ____ by the ministry after evidence of unauthorised arms transfers emerged.
items.e: „to blacklist“ = auf die schwarze Liste setzen; „blackball“ bezeichnet Ablehnung/Ausschluss meist bei Vereinsmitgliedschaft.

items.q: A former employee turned ____ after discovering the falsified export licences.
items.e: „whistleblower“ ist der neutrale Fachbegriff; die anderen Optionen sind umgangssprachlich/abwertend und im Register unpassend.

items.q: Analysts insist that a credible ____ posture, not rhetoric, keeps aggressors at bay.
items.e: Adjektivform „deterrent“ vor „posture“; „deterrence“ ist das Substantiv und hier grammatisch falsch.

items.q: Snap inspections are meant to test units' combat ____ at short notice.
items.e: Korrekte Substantivform „readiness“ = Einsatzbereitschaft.

items.q: The council demanded that the ambassador ____ immediately for consultations.

run22.note: Aufbau analog Sprachtest Russisch: Teil 1 Textverständnis (8 Fragen zu einem Textabschnitt), Teil 2 Wortschatz/Idiomatik (26 Fragen), Teil 3 Grammatik/Zeitformen (26 Fragen). items.q: What is the author's central argument about the term 'hybrid warfare'?
o: It is a precise legal category defined by international treaty.
It captures a real phenomenon but has been overused until it risks losing analytical value.
It was invented by authoritarian states to justify aggression.
items.e: „a term so elastic that it risks explaining everything and therefore nothing.“
items.passage:
Hybrid warfare has become one of those phrases that illuminates and obscures in equal measure. Coined to capture a genuine phenomenon — the blending of conventional force, irregular tactics, disinformation and economic coercion beneath the level that would trigger a formal military response — it has since been stretched to cover almost any hostile act a rival state declines to own publicly. The result is a term so elastic that it risks explaining everything and therefore nothing.

What distinguishes the grey zone from either peace or war is precisely its studied ambiguity. An undersea cable is severed by a vessel whose flag state cannot be established with certainty; a disinformation campaign amplifies a genuine grievance until it curdles into unrest; a swarm of drones violates an airspace for minutes rather than hours, long enough to unsettle, too briefly to justify retaliation. Each incident, taken alone, falls beneath almost any level that would warrant a forceful reply. Taken together, over months or years, they constitute something considerably more coherent than coincidence.

Herein lies the strategic logic for the aggressor: deniability is not incidental but the entire point. A state that can plausibly disclaim responsibility forces its adversary to choose between two unappealing options — responding to an attack it cannot conclusively prove occurred, or absorbing repeated provocations for fear of escalating a conflict that officially does not exist. Democracies, bound by domestic legal constraints and coalition politics, are particularly ill-suited to this dilemma; authoritarian rivals, answerable to no such constraints, exploit the asymmetry with evident relish.

Responding effectively therefore demands abandoning the instinct to treat each grey-zone incident in isolation. Cumulative attribution — aggregating a pattern of smaller acts into a single strategic picture — offers one way out of the dilemma, as does lowering, rather than raising, the level at which a coordinated response becomes politically defensible. Neither is straightforward. But the alternative, waiting for an act unambiguous enough to justify retaliation, guarantees that the aggressor will simply calibrate its next move to fall just short of it.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, what defines the 'grey zone'?
o: Open, declared armed conflict between two states.
A deliberate ambiguity that keeps hostile acts beneath the threshold of forceful response.
A legal zone recognised under the UN Charter.
A period of formal ceasefire negotiations.
items.e: „What distinguishes the grey zone from either peace or war is precisely its studied ambiguity.“

items.q: Why, according to the author, is deniability central to grey-zone strategy?
o: Because it allows the aggressor to avoid all economic cost.
Because it forces the target to choose between unproven retaliation and repeated absorption of provocations.
Because international law explicitly permits deniable attacks.
Because it guarantees diplomatic immunity for the attacker.
items.e: „deniability is not incidental but the entire point... forces its adversary to choose between two unappealing options.“

items.q: What can be inferred about democracies' vulnerability to grey-zone tactics?
o: They are immune due to superior military technology.
Domestic legal and political constraints make them comparatively ill-suited to respond.
They deliberately choose not to respond for economic reasons.
They are only vulnerable in wartime.
items.e: „Democracies, bound by domestic legal constraints and coalition politics, are particularly ill-suited to this dilemma.“

items.q: In context, 'curdles into unrest' most nearly means the grievance …
o: gradually turns sour and develops into disorder.
is officially investigated by the state.
items.e: Küchenmetapher (Milch, die gerinnt) für das allmähliche Kippen einer Beschwerde in Unruhe.

items.q: The author's tone towards the term 'hybrid warfare' as currently used is …
o: dismissive of the entire concept as meaningless.
items.e: Kritisch-mahnend, nicht ablehnend: erkennt „a genuine phenomenon“ an, warnt aber vor Überdehnung des Begriffs.

items.q: What is the function of the second paragraph's list of examples (severed cable, disinformation, drone incursions)?
o: To provide statistical evidence for a specific attack.
To illustrate the individually deniable but cumulatively coherent nature of grey-zone incidents.
To argue that these tactics are ineffective.
To describe a single, well-documented historical event.
items.e: Veranschaulicht: Einzelvorfälle bleiben unterhalb der Reaktionsschwelle, ergeben in der Summe aber ein Muster.

items.q: What does the author propose as a partial response to the grey-zone dilemma?
o: Ignoring all incidents until an unambiguous attack occurs.
Aggregating a pattern of smaller acts into cumulative attribution and lowering the response threshold.
Immediate military retaliation after every incident.
items.e: Letzter Absatz: „Cumulative attribution... as does lowering, rather than raising, the level at which a coordinated response becomes politically defensible.“

items.q: The operation was calibrated to avoid crossing the ____ that would trigger a formal military response.
items.e: „threshold“ = Schwelle; feststehender sicherheitspolitischer Fachbegriff für die Reaktionsgrenze („crossing the threshold“); „tightrope“ (Drahtseilakt) und „ceiling“ (Obergrenze) passen semantisch nicht zum Bild einer zu überschreitenden Grenze.

items.q: The saboteurs relied on ____ deniability to avoid direct blame.
items.e: „plausible deniability“ ist die feste strategische Fachfügung.

items.q: Analysts describe the campaign as a textbook case of ____ tactics operating below the level of open war.
items.e: Fachbegriff „grey-zone tactics“.

items.q: The cable was severed by a vessel whose ____ could not be conclusively established.
items.e: Seerechtlicher Fachbegriff „flag state“ = Flaggenstaat.

items.q: Disinformation operators seek to ____ genuine grievances rather than invent them outright.
items.e: Feste Kollokation „amplify a grievance/message“ im Kontext von Desinformation.

items.q: The drones violated national ____ for barely three minutes.
items.e: Völkerrechtlicher Fachbegriff „airspace“ = Luftraum.

items.q: Officials were reluctant to ____ the attack to a specific state without conclusive forensic evidence.
items.e: Feste Kollokation „attribute X to Y“ ist der Standardbegriff in Cyber-/Geheimdienstberichten; „ascribe“ wirkt hier literarisch, nicht fachsprachlich.

items.q: The regiment conducted a ____ incursion, testing the border defences without committing to a full assault.
items.e: „probing incursion/attack“ = feste militärische Fachfügung, „Sondierungsangriff“.

items.q: The convoy was ambushed by ____ fighters operating without uniforms or insignia.
items.e: „irregular fighters/forces“ = Fachbegriff für nicht-reguläre Kombattanten.

items.q: The state's use of ____ proxies allowed it to deny any direct involvement.
items.e: „deniable“ betont die Abstreitbarkeit als strategisches Ziel, nicht nur die Heimlichkeit („covert“).

items.q: The sabotage campaign against undersea infrastructure has been described as a form of ____ warfare.
items.e: Feststehender Fachbegriff „hybrid warfare“.

items.q: Western agencies accused the group of running a coordinated ____ campaign across several platforms.
items.e: „disinformation“ = absichtlich gestreute Falschinformation, im Gegensatz zu unabsichtlicher „misinformation“.

items.q: The militia operated as a ____ force, blurring the line between state and non-state actors.
items.e: „proxy force“ = Stellvertreterkraft, feste sicherheitspolitische Fachfügung.

items.q: The ministry accused its rival of waging a ____ campaign to destabilise the coalition government.
items.e: Korrekte Adjektivform vor dem Substantiv „campaign“.

items.q: Undersea cables have become an attractive target precisely because legal ____ is so hard to establish.
items.e: „culpability“ ist der juristisch-formale Fachterminus, der im diplomatischen Register erwartet wird.

items.q: The government imposed retaliatory tariffs as an act of ____ short of open conflict.
items.e: „act of coercion“ ist die diplomatisch-fachsprachliche Bezeichnung für Zwangsmaßnahmen unterhalb der Kriegsschwelle.

items.q: Intelligence officials warned that the campaign was designed to ____ public trust in the electoral process.
items.e: Feste Kollokation „erode trust/confidence“; die anderen Verben passen nicht zu „trust“.

items.q: The saboteurs left no digital ____ that investigators could trace back to a state sponsor.
items.e: Fachbegriff „digital footprint“; die übrigen Optionen sind keine etablierten Begriffe.

items.q: The two agencies remain locked in a ____ over who first identified the malware.
items.e: Idiom „turf war“ = Kompetenzstreit.

items.q: Officials were careful to keep the response ____ , avoiding any escalation that might be misread as war.
items.e: „proportionate“ ist der im Völkerrecht (jus ad bellum) übliche Terminus; „proportional“ gehört eher ins mathematisch-statistische Register.

items.q: The insurgency drew much of its strength from a sympathetic ____ population willing to shelter fighters.
items.e: „local population“ ist die neutrale Standardkollokation; die anderen Optionen tragen abweichende Konnotationen.

items.q: The report accuses the contractor of operating in a legal ____ , neither clearly licensed nor explicitly banned.
items.e: „grey area“ = rechtliche Grauzone, feste Redewendung.

items.q: The country's leadership has long relied on cyber-enabled ____ to sow discord without firing a shot.
items.e: „subversion“ passt zum Kontext „without firing a shot“ (unblutige Untergrabung); „sabotage“ impliziert physische Zerstörung, „insurrection“ einen bewaffneten Aufstand.

items.q: The alliance's cyber unit works to ____ intrusions before they cause lasting damage.
items.e: „contain an intrusion“ = eindämmen; die anderen Verben kollokieren nicht mit „intrusion“.

items.q: The think-tank's report warned against treating each incident in ____ rather than as part of a broader pattern.
items.e: Feste Fügung „in isolation“ = isoliert betrachtet.

items.q: The saboteurs' methods bore the unmistakable ____ of a state intelligence service.
items.e: Idiom „bear the hallmark of“ = die charakteristischen Merkmale von etwas tragen.

items.q: The council insisted that the ministry ____ full evidence before naming a culprit.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach „insist that“ — Grundform ohne -s.

items.q: Had the sabotage gone undetected, the outage ____ still ongoing.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional: Bedingung Vergangenheit, Folge Gegenwart.

items.q: ____ the drones to cross the border again, the government would consider a proportionate response.
items.e: „Were … to“ — invertierte hypothetische Zukunftsform.

items.q: No sooner had investigators traced the malware ____ the trail went cold.
items.e: Feste Korrelation „no sooner … than“.

items.q: The breach ____ have originated internally; the firewall logs show no external access at all.
items.e: „can't have“ = logische Unmöglichkeit im Rückblick.

items.q: Investigators had already examined the servers before the logs ____ wiped last month.
items.e: Einfaches Präteritum bei abgeschlossenem Zeitpunkt („last month“); die Vorzeitigkeit wird bereits durch „had already examined“ ausgedrückt.

items.q: By the time the report is published, the campaign ____ for over a year.
items.e: Future Perfect nach „by the time“ bei andauernder Handlung.

items.q: A handful of incidents ____ enough to establish the pattern investigators suspected.
items.e: „a handful of“ + Plural.

items.q: The more incidents accumulated, ____ the pattern became to dismiss as coincidence.
items.e: Korrelative Struktur „the … the …“ verlangt zwei Artikel.

items.q: The agency withheld the report ____ it compromise ongoing operations.
items.e: „lest“ + Subjunktiv (Grundform).

items.q: ____ troubled analysts most was the sheer coordination behind seemingly unrelated incidents.
items.e: Pseudo-Cleft „What … was …“.

items.q: The team traced the signal and ____ before it vanished.
items.e: Pronominales Objekt steht zwingend zwischen Verb und Partikel.

items.q: The unit is believed ____ responsible for at least three prior incursions.
items.e: Berichtspassiv mit Vorzeitigkeit: „is believed to have been“.

items.q: After presenting the evidence, the analyst went on ____ several policy recommendations.
items.e: „go on to do“ = zu einer neuen Tätigkeit übergehen.

items.q: The commander would rather the incident ____ unreported until the investigation concluded.
items.e: „would rather“ + Simple Past bei Gegenwarts-/Zukunftsbezug.

items.q: The infrastructure ____ the sabotage was directed forms part of the regional power grid.
items.e: Vorangestellte Präposition verlangt „which“, nie „that“.

items.q: ____ under cover of darkness, the drones evaded early radar detection.
items.e: Passivisches Partizip; die Aktivform würde die Drohnen zum Handelnden machen.

items.q: The denial was ____ implausible given the satellite evidence.
items.e: Adverb modifiziert das Adjektiv „implausible“.

items.q: The spokesperson had claimed the incursion would end ____ ; it did not.
items.e: Deixisverschiebung in der Redewiedergabe: „tomorrow/next week“ → „the following week“.

items.q: ____ did the cable failure disrupt communications, but it also exposed a hidden vulnerability.
items.e: „Not only … but also“ verlangt Inversion nach vorangestelltem „Not only“.

items.q: Hardly had the ministry issued its denial ____ new evidence surfaced online.
items.e: „hardly … when“ (im Unterschied zu „no sooner … than“).

items.q: The officer briefed the press as though the operation ____ already concluded.
items.e: „as though“ + Past Perfect bei Bezug auf eine vorzeitige, irreale Situation.

items.q: The border guards ____ have sounded a full alert; it was only a stray reconnaissance drone.
items.e: „needn't have + Partizip“ = unnötige, aber tatsächlich ausgeführte Handlung.

items.q: He was named ____ special coordinator for hybrid-threat resilience.
items.e: Nullartikel vor einmaligen Ämtern nach „name/appoint“.

items.q: The findings bear directly ____ the question of state responsibility.
items.e: „bear on“ = betreffen; Kontrast zu „bear out“ (bestätigen).

items.q: It is imperative that the alliance ____ a unified position before the summit.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach „it is imperative that“.

items.q: What is the author's overall assessment of the NPT review conference process?
o: It is entirely useless and should be discontinued.
It is imperfect and often fails to reach consensus, yet still serves a constraining and accountability function.
It has fully resolved the tension between disarmament and non-proliferation.
It exists solely to approve new nuclear weapons programmes.
items.e: Letzter Absatz: „None of this renders the exercise pointless... still constrains behaviour.“
items.passage:
Every five years, the states party to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty converge on the same building in New York, rehearse the same grievances, and depart with startling regularity without a consensus final document. The 2022 review conference was only the latest instance in which those hopes were dashed, this time over a single paragraph concerning the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant that one delegation would not accept. Cynics have long since concluded that the ritual matters more than the outcome; the treaty's defenders insist, with rather less confidence than they once possessed, that showing up and arguing is preferable to the alternative.

The bargain struck in 1968 was never symmetrical, and every review conference eventually collides with that asymmetry. Non-nuclear-weapon states accepted permanent renunciation in exchange for two promises: access to peaceful nuclear technology, and progress by the five recognised nuclear powers towards eventual disarmament. The technology has largely materialised; the disarmament has not, and the gap between the two grows harder to paper over with each passing cycle. Delegations from the Non-Aligned Movement no longer bother to disguise their exasperation, pointing to expanding arsenals and modernisation programmes as evidence that Article VI has been quietly abandoned rather than merely delayed.

Meanwhile, the treaty's other central function — preventing new states from acquiring the bomb — has fared rather better than the disarmament pillar, though scarcely well enough to inspire complacency. Three states never joined at all and built weapons regardless; a fourth withdrew and did the same. Each case exposed a structural weakness the treaty's architects never fully resolved: leaving the treaty remains legally permissible, and no mechanism obliges a departing state to return technology acquired under its peaceful-use provisions.

None of this renders the exercise pointless. A near-universal treaty, however imperfect, still constrains behaviour that would otherwise go entirely unchecked, and the review process, however theatrical, remains one of the few forums where nuclear and non-nuclear states are obliged to sit at the same table and account for themselves.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: What caused the 2022 review conference to fail to reach a consensus document?
o: A dispute over the treaty's founding year.
Disagreement over a paragraph concerning the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant.
A walkout by the Non-Aligned Movement.
A disagreement about the conference location.
items.e: „this time over a single paragraph concerning the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant that one delegation would not accept.“

items.q: According to the passage, what did non-nuclear-weapon states receive in exchange for renouncing nuclear weapons?
o: Permanent seats on the UN Security Council.
Access to peaceful nuclear technology and a promise of progress towards disarmament.
items.e: „accepted permanent renunciation in exchange for two promises: access to peaceful nuclear technology, and progress... towards eventual disarmament.“

items.q: What can be inferred about the Non-Aligned Movement's view of nuclear-armed states' disarmament efforts?
o: They believe disarmament promises have been kept in full.
They regard Article VI as effectively abandoned given expanding arsenals.
They have stopped attending review conferences altogether.
They believe disarmament is no longer a treaty obligation.
items.e: „pointing to expanding arsenals and modernisation programmes as evidence that Article VI has been quietly abandoned.“

items.q: 'Paper over' in the phrase 'the gap... grows harder to paper over' most nearly means to …
o: conceal or superficially disguise a problem.
items.e: Idiom „paper over“ = kaschieren/vertuschen, nicht wörtlich „mit Papier bedecken“.

items.q: The author's tone when describing the disarmament pillar's record is best described as …
items.e: Kritisch-resignierter, aber nicht gänzlich verwerfender Ton (vgl. Schlussabsatz: „None of this renders the exercise pointless“).

items.q: What is the function of the third paragraph (beginning 'Meanwhile')?
o: To argue that non-proliferation has been an unqualified failure.
To contrast the treaty's comparatively better record on non-proliferation with its weaker record on disarmament, while noting structural weaknesses.
To describe the treaty's drafting history.
To list every state that currently possesses nuclear weapons.
items.e: Kontrastiert Nichtverbreitungs- mit Abrüstungsbilanz und benennt die strukturelle Schwäche des Austrittsrechts.

items.q: What structural weakness does the author identify regarding treaty withdrawal?
o: Withdrawal is legally impossible under any circumstance.
A withdrawing state must return all its territory to the UN.
Withdrawal is legally permitted and no mechanism forces return of acquired peaceful-use technology.
Withdrawal automatically triggers Security Council sanctions.
items.e: „leaving the treaty remains legally permissible, and no mechanism obliges a departing state to return technology acquired under its peaceful-use provisions.“

items.q: The treaty obliges signatories to submit their facilities to routine safeguards ____ .
items.e: „safeguards inspections“ ist die feste IAEO-Fachfügung; korrekte Substantivform.

items.q: Enrichment levels above twenty percent raise significant proliferation ____ .
items.e: Feste Kollokation „proliferation concerns“.

items.q: The state agreed to cap its enrichment ____ at a strictly civilian level.
items.e: „ceiling“ = Obergrenze, gängiger Fachbegriff in Rüstungskontrollabkommen.

items.q: Inspectors were denied access, a clear ____ of the safeguards agreement.
items.e: „breach of an agreement“ = Verstoß; „break“ ist umgangssprachlicher und keine Fachkollokation mit „agreement“.

items.q: The five recognised nuclear powers pledged to pursue disarmament negotiations in ____ .
items.e: Feste Wendung „in earnest“ = ernsthaft, ohne Adverbendung.

items.q: The reactor operates on a closed nuclear fuel ____ , reprocessing spent material.
items.e: „fuel cycle“ ist der Standard-Fachbegriff der Nuklearindustrie.

items.q: Diplomats warned that a nuclear ____ race in the region could unravel decades of restraint.
items.e: Feste Redewendung „arms race“.

items.q: The agency's mandate includes verifying that no ____ of fissile material has occurred.
items.e: IAEO-Fachbegriff „diversion“ = Umleitung/Abzweigung von Spaltmaterial.

items.q: The warhead's ____ yield was calibrated to remain within treaty limits.
items.e: Korrekte Adjektivform vor „yield“; „explosion“ und „exploding“ sind die falsche Wortart, „explosively“ ein Adverb.

items.q: The state's ____ of the treaty was formally deposited in Washington.
items.e: Korrekte Substantivform „ratification“.

items.q: Analysts fear the collapse of the agreement could trigger regional nuclear ____ .
items.e: Fachbegriff „(nuclear) proliferation“ = (atomare) Weiterverbreitung.

items.q: The treaty's review conference ended without a ____ final document, for the fourth time running.
items.e: Korrekte Substantivform als Attribut vor „final document“.

items.q: Missile ____ technology remains tightly restricted under multilateral export controls.
items.e: „missile delivery technology/systems“ ist die fachsprachlich korrekte Fügung.

items.q: The inspectorate's findings were deemed ____ with the state's declared inventory.
items.e: „consistent with“ ist die feste Standardkollokation in Verifikationsberichten.

items.q: The agency issued a formal ____ after the state failed to explain the discrepancy.
items.e: „censure“ ist der institutionelle Fachbegriff für eine förmliche Rüge durch ein Gremium (z. B. IAEO-Gouverneursrat).

items.q: The state's nuclear programme has long operated under a policy of deliberate ____ .
items.e: „strategic ambiguity“ ist der feste Fachbegriff für diese Politik.

items.q: Negotiators reached a ____ that neither side considers ideal but both can accept.
items.e: „reach a compromise“ ist die gängigste Kollokation.

items.q: The reactor was placed under continuous ____ following the discovery of undeclared activities.
items.e: „continuous monitoring“ ist der spezifische IAEO-Fachbegriff.

items.q: Article X permits a state to leave the treaty by invoking its supreme national ____ .
items.e: Korrekte Pluralform, entspricht dem originalen Vertragswortlaut „supreme interests of the country“.

items.q: The panel's report ____ significant gaps in the verification regime.
items.e: „identify gaps“ ist die Standardkollokation.

items.q: The delegation's proposal was met with a ____ response from nuclear-armed states.
items.e: „a lukewarm response“ ist die feste idiomatische Wendung.

items.q: The state's nuclear ambitions have long been an open ____ among regional diplomats.
items.e: „an open secret“ ist die feste Redewendung.

items.q: Verification measures must be ____ enough to detect covert enrichment yet not so intrusive as to compromise commercial secrets.
items.e: „stringent“ ist die im Kontext von Verifikationsmaßnahmen gebräuchlichste Kollokation.

items.q: The five nuclear-weapon states have resisted calls for a legally ____ disarmament timetable.
items.e: „legally binding“ ist die feste diplomatische Fügung.

items.q: Reactor operators must maintain a detailed ____ trail for all fissile-material movements.
items.e: „audit trail“ ist der feststehende Fachbegriff.

items.q: The treaty's preamble reaffirms the ____ right of all states to peaceful nuclear technology.
items.e: Feste Fügung „inalienable right“, entsprechend dem Wortlaut von Artikel IV des NPT.

items.q: The board demanded that the state ____ full access to the disputed facility.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach „demand that“ — Grundform ohne -s.

items.q: Had the state ratified the protocol earlier, inspectors ____ far greater access today.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional: Bedingung Vergangenheit, Folge Gegenwart.

items.q: ____ the state to resume enrichment above five percent, the agreement would collapse instantly.
items.e: „Were … to“ — invertierte hypothetische Zukunftsform.

items.q: No sooner had the inspectors arrived ____ the centrifuges were dismantled and hidden.
items.e: Feste Korrelation „no sooner … than“.

items.q: The declared stockpile figures ____ have been falsified; the isotope ratios simply do not match.

items.q: The agency ____ its latest report only yesterday.
items.e: Abgeschlossener Zeitpunkt („yesterday“) schließt das Present Perfect aus.

items.q: By the time the next review conference convenes, the safeguards agreement ____ for over a decade.
items.e: Future Perfect nach „by the time“ bei andauernder Handlung.

items.q: A handful of states ____ yet to sign the additional protocol.
items.e: „a handful of“ + Plural.

items.q: The longer negotiations stalled, ____ the prospect of a consensus document became.
items.e: Korrelative Struktur „the … the …“ verlangt zwei Artikel.

items.q: The delegation phrased its objection cautiously ____ it derail the entire conference.
items.e: „lest“ + Subjunktiv (Grundform).

items.q: ____ troubled the inspectors was not the missing material itself but the state's shifting explanations.
items.e: Pseudo-Cleft „What … was …“.

items.q: Technicians recalibrated the sensors and ____ before the inspection resumed.
items.e: Pronominales Objekt steht zwingend zwischen Verb und Partikel.

items.q: The facility is believed ____ undeclared enrichment activity for several years.
items.e: Berichtspassiv mit Vorzeitigkeit: „is believed to have conducted“.

items.q: Having outlined the violations, the inspector went on ____ a formal referral to the Security Council.
items.e: „go on to do“ = zu einer neuen Handlung übergehen.

items.q: The chair would rather the vote ____ until all delegations had spoken.
items.e: „would rather“ + Simple Past bei Gegenwarts-/Zukunftsbezug.

items.q: The protocol ____ the state objected has since been amended.
items.e: Vorangestellte Präposition verlangt „which“, nie „that“.

items.q: ____ under conditions of strict secrecy, the enrichment programme evaded detection for years.
items.e: Passivisches Partizip; die Aktivform würde das Programm zum Handelnden machen.

items.q: The state's compliance record was ____ inconsistent with its public assurances.
items.e: Adverb modifiziert das Adjektiv „inconsistent“.

items.q: The envoy had promised a full report ____ ; none arrived.
items.e: Deixisverschiebung in der Redewiedergabe: „next week“ → „the following week“.

items.q: ____ did the state miss the deadline, but it also refused inspectors entry.
items.e: „Not only … but also“ verlangt Inversion nach vorangestelltem „Not only“.

items.q: Hardly had the conference opened ____ the first walkout occurred.
items.e: „hardly … when“ (im Unterschied zu „no sooner … than“).

items.q: The delegate spoke as though the treaty ____ already collapsed beyond repair.
items.e: „as though“ + Past Perfect bei Bezug auf eine vorzeitige, irreale Situation.

items.q: The technicians ____ have shut down the reactor; the anomaly proved to be a faulty sensor.
items.e: „needn't have + Partizip“ = unnötige, aber tatsächlich ausgeführte Handlung.

items.q: She was appointed ____ director general of the agency last spring.
items.e: Nullartikel vor einmaligen Ämtern nach „appoint“.

items.q: The report's conclusions bear directly ____ the question of the state's compliance.
items.e: „bear on“ = betreffen.

items.q: It is essential that every member state ____ its reporting obligations without exception.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach „it is essential that“.
