items.q: What is the author's central argument about frozen conflicts?
o: They are easier to resolve than active wars because there is no fighting.
Their lack of urgency, and possibly one party's strategic interest in stalemate, makes them unusually resistant to mediation.
International mediators always achieve full resolution eventually.
They are a recent phenomenon unknown before the twentieth century.
items.e: Kernaussage: fehlender Handlungsdruck plus mögliches strategisches Interesse am Status quo erschweren die Vermittlung.
items.passage:
Frozen conflicts earn their name from a deceptive stillness: the guns fall silent, front lines calcify into de facto borders, and the world's attention drifts elsewhere, yet no peace treaty is ever signed and no side abandons its underlying claims. It is precisely this suspended animation that makes such disputes so resistant to mediation. Where an active war creates pressure — casualties mount, economies buckle, populations demand an end to the fighting — a frozen conflict generates none of that urgency. The status quo, however unsatisfactory, is one that most parties can live with indefinitely, which is exactly the problem confronting anyone hoping to broker a settlement.

International mediators arriving in such a theatre typically inherit a negotiating format inherited from an earlier, more acute phase of the dispute — a contact group, a minsk-style process, a rotating chairmanship — whose original urgency has long since evaporated even as its bureaucratic apparatus persists. Meetings convene, communiqués are issued, and yet the underlying territorial dispute remains exactly where it stood a decade earlier. Mediators candidly admit, in private if rarely in public, that their principal achievement in many such settings is not resolution but management: preventing the frozen conflict from reheating into open confrontation, even as a durable settlement recedes ever further from reach.

Some scholars argue that this very durability of stalemate is itself a policy choice, tacitly preferred by at least one party for whom an unresolved dispute serves strategic purposes a final settlement would foreclose. If that diagnosis holds, then the mediator's task is not merely technical but adversarial: persuading a party to relinquish an arrangement that, however costly in principle, continues to serve its interests rather better than any negotiated alternative on offer.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, what typically happens to the urgency of the original negotiating format over time?
o: It increases as the conflict continues.
It evaporates, even as the bureaucratic apparatus persists.
It disappears along with the negotiating format itself.
It is transferred entirely to regional organisations.
items.e: Text: „whose original urgency has long since evaporated even as its bureaucratic apparatus persists.“

items.q: What do mediators privately admit their principal achievement often is, according to the passage?
o: Management — preventing the conflict from reheating rather than resolving it.
Persuading both sides to abandon their claims.
items.e: Text: „their principal achievement in many such settings is not resolution but management.“

items.q: What examples of inherited negotiating formats does the passage give?
o: A contact group, a Minsk-style process, a rotating chairmanship.
A permanent peacekeeping force and a customs union.
A joint military command and a shared currency.
A referendum mechanism and a boundary commission.
items.e: Text: „a contact group, a minsk-style process, a rotating chairmanship“.

items.q: What can be inferred about a party that benefits strategically from an unresolved dispute, per the final paragraph?
o: It will actively push for rapid resolution.
It may have little genuine incentive to accept a final settlement.
It is legally obligated to seek arbitration.
It will withdraw from the negotiating format entirely.
items.e: Aus dem Text: wenn der Status quo strategische Zwecke erfüllt, hat die betreffende Partei wenig echtes Interesse an einer endgültigen Einigung.

items.q: In 'front lines calcify into de facto borders', the word 'calcify' most nearly means …
o: harden into a fixed, unchanging state
items.e: „to calcify“ = übertragen: erstarren, sich verhärten/verfestigen — nicht rechtlich anerkannt, nur faktisch fixiert (‚de facto‘).

items.q: How would the author's overall tone best be characterised?
o: analytically sober, tinged with quiet scepticism about mediators' prospects.
openly hostile toward all international mediators.
purely celebratory of frozen conflicts as a stabilising mechanism.
items.e: Der Text analysiert nüchtern und lässt durchgehend Skepsis gegenüber echten Lösungschancen durchklingen, ohne polemisch zu werden.

items.q: What shift in interpretation does the final paragraph introduce?
o: To summarise the history of the Minsk process.
To introduce a more adversarial interpretation of the mediator's task, based on one party's possible strategic interest in stalemate.
To argue that all frozen conflicts eventually resolve themselves.
To describe the economic costs of active warfare.
items.e: Der Absatz führt die These ein, dass Stillstand bewusst bevorzugt werden kann, was die Vermittlerrolle von einer technischen zu einer gegnerischen Aufgabe macht.

items.q: The dispute has remained ____ for over two decades, with neither side willing to compromise.
items.e: „deadlocked“ = festgefahren/verhärtet.

items.q: The mediator's role is chiefly to ____ the two sides toward a workable framework.
items.e: „to steer parties toward something“ = sie in eine Richtung lenken.

items.q: The contact group meets regularly but has made little tangible ____ .
items.e: „to make headway“ = Fortschritte machen.

items.q: Both sides have dug in, and any ____ now seems remote.
items.e: „a breakthrough“ = ein entscheidender Durchbruch.

items.q: The frozen conflict occasionally threatens to ____ into open confrontation.
items.e: „to flare up“ = plötzlich wieder aufflammen.

items.q: The mediating power has tried to keep both sides ____ the table.
items.e: „around the table“ = gemeinsam verhandelnd; Alternative zu „at the table“.

items.q: The rotating chairmanship has done little to ____ new momentum into the talks.
items.e: „to inject momentum“ = neuen Schwung verleihen.

items.q: The territorial dispute has settled into an uneasy ____ that neither side wishes to disturb.
items.e: „an uneasy equilibrium“ = ein prekäres Gleichgewicht.

items.q: The negotiators have grown increasingly ____ with the lack of progress.
items.e: „disillusioned with“ = desillusioniert/ernüchtert.

items.q: Peacekeepers were deployed to ____ the line of contact.
items.e: „to patrol a line of contact“ = eine Kontaktlinie überwachen.

items.q: The mediator sought to ____ confidence-building measures into the stalled talks.
items.e: „to reintroduce measures“ = Maßnahmen erneut einführen.

items.q: The two sides remain ____ apart on the question of sovereignty.
items.e: „irreconcilably apart“ = unversöhnlich/unüberbrückbar auseinanderliegend.

items.q: The ceasefire has held, but the underlying dispute remains ____ unresolved.
items.e: „substantively unresolved“ = inhaltlich/in der Sache ungelöst.

items.q: The mediator's shuttle diplomacy failed to ____ the impasse.
items.e: „to break an impasse“ = eine Sackgasse überwinden.

items.q: Both governments have ____ any territorial concession publicly.
items.e: „to rule out something“ = etwas ausschließen.

items.q: The negotiating format has become largely ____ , persisting out of habit rather than purpose.
items.e: „ritualistic“ = zur bloßen Ritualhandlung erstarrt.

items.q: The mediator warned that the status quo could not ____ indefinitely.
items.e: „the status quo cannot hold“ = der Status quo lässt sich nicht halten.

items.q: The two delegations agreed to a limited ____ of confidence-building steps.
items.e: „a package of measures“ = ein Maßnahmenpaket.

items.q: The mediating states have been careful not to ____ favouritism toward either side.
items.e: „to betray favouritism“ = Parteilichkeit erkennen lassen.

items.q: The dispute has proven remarkably ____ to international pressure.
items.e: „impervious to pressure“ = unempfänglich/immun gegenüber Druck.

items.q: The frozen conflict has settled into a ____ of low-level skirmishes.
items.e: „a pattern of skirmishes“ = ein wiederkehrendes Muster.

items.q: The mediator's office issued a ____ statement urging both sides to show restraint.
items.e: „a carefully worded statement“ = eine sorgfältig formulierte Erklärung.

items.q: One party appears to derive strategic ____ from the conflict's continuation.
items.e: „to derive advantage from something“ = daraus Vorteil ziehen.

items.q: The mediating team's mandate was quietly ____ for another year.
items.e: „to extend a mandate“ = ein Mandat verlängern.

items.q: Despite years of talks, the two sides have failed to ____ common ground.
items.e: „to find common ground“ = eine gemeinsame Basis finden.

items.q: „eingefrorener Konflikt“ — das exakte englische Äquivalent:
items.e: „frozen conflict“ ist der etablierte politikwissenschaftliche Terminus.

items.q: The mediator recommended that both sides ____ from further provocations.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach „recommend that“: Grundform „desist“.

items.q: It is vital that the ceasefire line ____ respected by both militaries.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv: Grundform „be“.

items.q: Had the mediator pressed harder a decade ago, the conflict ____ resolved by now.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional: Bedingung Vergangenheit, Folge Gegenwart („by now“).

items.q: If one side ____ less invested in maintaining the status quo, a settlement would already exist.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional (Gegenwarts-Irrealis in der Bedingung).

items.q: Rarely ____ a frozen conflict resolved itself without sustained external pressure.
items.e: Inversion nach „Rarely“ + Present Perfect.

items.q: At no point ____ either delegation prepared to discuss sovereignty directly.
items.e: Inversion nach vorangestelltem „At no point“.

items.q: The mediating team ____ have anticipated the stalemate; every prior round had ended identically.
items.e: „should have + Partizip“ = Kritik an einer versäumten Erwartung.

items.q: The renewed clashes ____ have been coordinated; they broke out simultaneously along the entire line.
items.e: „must have + Partizip“ = logische Schlussfolgerung.

items.q: The envoy reported that the ceasefire ____ largely, despite isolated incidents.
items.e: Backshift: Present Progressive → Past Progressive in der indirekten Rede.

items.q: She said the talks would resume ____ , not the following month as originally scheduled.
items.e: Deixisverschiebung in der Redewiedergabe.

items.q: The negotiating format is believed ____ little genuine momentum at this stage.
items.e: Berichtspassiv, gleichzeitige Handlung: einfacher Infinitiv „to retain“.

items.q: The rotating chairmanship is reported ____ several confidence-building proposals over the past year.
items.e: Berichtspassiv mit Vorzeitigkeit: „is reported to have floated“.

items.q: ____ frustrates mediators most is the absence of any real cost to maintaining the status quo.
items.e: Pseudo-Cleft: „What … is …“.

items.q: It is the absence of urgency, not a lack of proposals, ____ explains the stalemate.
items.e: It-Cleft: „It is X that …“.

items.q: The longer the conflict remains frozen, ____ a negotiated settlement appears.
items.e: Korrelative Struktur „the … the …“.

items.q: Hardly had the confidence-building measures been announced ____ one side suspended its participation.
items.e: Feste Korrelation „hardly … when“.

items.q: ____ from an earlier, more acute phase of the dispute, the negotiating format has long outlived its original purpose.
items.e: Passivisches Partizip: das Format wurde geerbt, nicht die Handelnden selbst.

items.q: ____ the line of contact for years, the peacekeepers have grown accustomed to the routine.
items.e: Aktives Partizip Präsens für eine andauernde Begleithandlung: „Patrolling... for years“.

items.q: He was appointed ____ special mediator for the frozen conflict in early spring.
items.e: Nullartikel vor einmaligen Funktionen nach „appoint“.

items.q: The mediator's proposal was met ____ scepticism by both delegations.
items.e: Feste Rektion: „meet with scepticism“.

items.q: The stalemate has proved remarkably resistant ____ international pressure.
items.e: Feste Rektion: „resistant to“.

items.q: The mediator reviewed the ceasefire terms and then ____ before the joint session.
items.e: Pronominales Objekt zwingend zwischen Verb und Partikel: „read out“.

items.q: By the time the next round convenes, the two sides ____ eighteen months without a single breakthrough.
items.e: Future Perfect für eine bis zu einem Zukunftszeitpunkt abgeschlossene Handlung.

items.q: ____ one side to abandon the talks altogether, the entire mediation framework would collapse.
items.e: „Were … to abandon“ — hypothetische Zukunft im formalen Register.

items.q: The mediator avoided any public timetable ____ its breach undermine the process entirely.
items.e: „lest“ + Subjunktiv „undermine“ (Grundform).

items.q: The line ____ both sides adhere has never been formally demarcated.
items.e: Vorangestellte Präposition verlangt „which“: „adhere to“ → „to which“.

items.q: What is the core argument the author is putting forward?
o: The loss-and-damage fund is essentially worthless and should be abandoned.
The fund's creation is significant, but its capitalisation falls far short of the damage it is meant to address.
Donor governments have fully met the demands of vulnerable states.
The World Bank's role as trustee guarantees the fund's success.
items.e: Kernaussage: Die Fondsgründung ist ein Fortschritt, doch die Kapitalisierung bleibt weit hinter dem Bedarf zurück ("bear scant relation to the damage"). A ist zu absolut ("None of this renders the fund worthless").
items.passage:
That a fund now exists is, by the standards of multilateral bargaining, no small feat. After three decades in which the very phrase "loss and damage" was treated in wealthier capitals as an admission of liability best avoided, COP27 produced an agreement to establish one, and COP28 opened it for business with pledges running into the hundreds of millions of dollars. Vulnerable states, whose delegations had pressed the case since the Alliance of Small Island States first raised it in 1991, greeted the outcome as vindication. Yet the self-congratulation obscured a harder truth: pledges are not disbursements, and the sums on offer bear scant relation to the damage they purport to address.

Estimates of the annual finance needed to compensate developing countries for climate-driven destruction — cyclones that flatten harbours, droughts that empty granaries, seas that swallow low-lying atolls — run into the hundreds of billions. Against that backdrop, the fund's initial capitalisation looks less like restitution than a gesture, calibrated to demonstrate good faith without conceding the principle that historical emitters owe a debt proportionate to the harm they have caused. Donor governments, mindful of taxpayers wary of open-ended commitments, have insisted on voluntary rather than assessed contributions, and on hosting arrangements — the World Bank was installed as interim trustee — that recipient states regard with some suspicion, given the institution's chequered record on grants versus loans.

None of this renders the fund worthless. Even modest, predictable flows can crowd in other financing and lend legitimacy to claims that were, until recently, dismissed outright. But the architecture now being assembled will be judged less by the communiqués that inaugurated it than by whether a farmer in the Sahel or a fisherman in the Solomon Islands ever sees a rupee, a franc or a dollar of it. On present trends, that reckoning still lies some years off.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, the idea of a loss-and-damage fund was first raised by...
o: the Alliance of Small Island States in 1991
items.e: Text: "since the Alliance of Small Island States first raised it in 1991".

items.q: Why do recipient states view the World Bank's role as interim trustee with suspicion?
o: Because of its record on grants versus loans
Because it has refused to host the fund at all
Because it favours assessed rather than voluntary contributions
Because it has no experience in development finance
items.e: Text: "given the institution's chequered record on grants versus loans".

items.q: The passage implies that donor governments' insistence on voluntary contributions is motivated primarily by...
o: a wish to avoid domestic political criticism over open-ended fiscal commitments
legal advice that assessed contributions are prohibited under international law
a desire to transfer responsibility to the World Bank
items.e: "mindful of taxpayers wary of open-ended commitments" legt eine innenpolitische Motivation nahe, ohne sie direkt auszusprechen — Inferenzfrage.

items.q: In the final paragraph, 'crowd in other financing' most nearly means...
o: to physically gather donors in one location
to attract or stimulate additional investment
to exclude private capital from a market
items.e: "crowd in" (Gegenteil von "crowd out") = zusätzliche Finanzierung anstoßen/anziehen.

items.q: The author's tone toward the fund's achievements so far is best described as...
o: cautiously skeptical, acknowledging progress while highlighting shortfalls
items.e: Anerkennung ("no small feat", "can crowd in") kombiniert mit Kritik ("bear scant relation") — abgewogen-skeptischer Ton.

items.q: In this passage, the final paragraph's main role is to...
o: summarise the history of the fund's creation
qualify the preceding criticism before restating the real test the fund still faces
argue that the fund should be scrapped entirely
present a purely statistical comparison of pledges
items.e: "None of this renders the fund worthless" leitet eine Konzession ein, danach folgt die eigentliche Bewährungsprobe ("judged... by whether a farmer... ever sees...").

items.q: Per the passage, the sums pledged at COP28 were...
o: equal to independent estimates of annual need
running into the hundreds of millions of dollars, far below estimated need in the hundreds of billions
entirely in the form of loans
rejected by vulnerable states as an insult
items.e: Text: "pledges running into the hundreds of millions" vs. "annual finance needed ... run into the hundreds of billions".

items.q: Donor pledges mean little without prompt ____ .
items.e: "disbursement" = tatsächliche Auszahlung zugesagter Mittel; "endowment" = Stiftungsvermögen, "subscription" = Zeichnung/Abonnement.

items.q: The fund's initial ____ fell far short of independent estimates of need.
items.e: "capitalisation" = Kapitalausstattung; "capitulation" (Kapitulation) ist ein reiner Klang-Distraktor.

items.q: Vulnerable states argue that historical emitters owe a debt ____ to the harm they caused.
items.e: "proportionate to" ist die feste Fügung; "commensurate" verlangt "with", nicht "to".

items.q: Wealthy governments insisted on voluntary rather than ____ contributions.
items.e: "assessed contributions" = nach Beitragsschlüssel verpflichtende Zahlungen (UN-Fachbegriff).

items.q: The report catalogued the ____ wrought by successive cyclones.
items.e: Nach "the" folgt ein Substantiv; nur "devastation" ist eines.

items.q: Negotiators warned that delay would only ____ the gap between promise and delivery.
items.e: "widen a gap" ist die feste Kollokation; die anderen Verben kollokieren in diesem Sinn nicht mit "gap".

items.q: Critics dismissed the pledge as a ____ gesture, unmatched by follow-through.
items.e: Adjektiv vor "gesture" nötig; "perfunctory" = pflichtschuldig-oberflächlich. "preferential" passt semantisch nicht.

items.q: Despite decades of advocacy, small island states struggled to make real ____ in the talks.
items.e: "make headway" = Fortschritte erzielen.

items.q: The World Bank was installed as ____ trustee pending a permanent arrangement.
items.e: "interim" = vorläufig/Übergangs-; "intern" (Praktikant) ist ein Klang-Distraktor.

items.q: Recipients fear the fund will replicate the World Bank's ____ record on grants versus loans.
items.e: "a patchy track record" = eine durchwachsene Bilanz.

items.q: Even modest funding can ____ far larger flows of private investment.
items.e: "catalyse" = als Anstoß/Katalysator wirken.

items.q: The pledges were, by common ____ , unlikely to be honoured in full.
items.e: "by common consent" = wie allgemein eingeräumt wird.

items.q: Negotiators sought to ____ the principle of differentiated responsibility in the fund's rules.
items.e: "enshrine a principle in" = einen Grundsatz verankern.

items.q: The agreement leaves ____ contributions entirely to each donor's judgement.
items.e: "discretionary" = im Ermessen stehend; "discreet" (diskret) und "discrete" (getrennt) sind Homophon-Fallen.

items.q: Sceptics argue the fund merely ____ over the deeper question of liability.
items.e: "paper over" = eine Angelegenheit oberflächlich kaschieren.

items.q: The trustee arrangement drew ____ criticism from recipient governments.
items.e: "pointed criticism" = gezielte, scharfe Kritik; "pointedly" ist Adverb und passt syntaktisch nicht vor dem Nomen.

items.q: Donor states stand accused of using the fund to ____ their own reluctance to cut emissions.
items.e: "offset" = kompensieren/ausgleichen — hier im übertragenen Sinn.

items.q: The scale of destruction has largely ____ doubts about the fund's necessity.
items.e: "dispel doubts" = Zweifel zerstreuen.

items.q: Talks ____ on for two more days before a compromise was reached.
items.e: "drag on" = sich in die Länge ziehen.

items.q: The fund's governance structure remains a ____ issue between donors and recipients.
items.e: "contentious" = umstritten; "contented" (zufrieden) ist die klassische Verwechslung.

items.q: Adaptation measures alone cannot ____ for losses that are already irreversible.
items.e: "compensate for" = ausgleichen für; "account for" = erklären, "amount to" = sich belaufen auf.

items.q: The final communiqué was criticised as an exercise in diplomatic ____ .
items.e: Nach "diplomatic" folgt ein Nomen; "hedging" = Absicherung durch bewusst vage Formulierungen.

items.q: Officials were careful not to ____ any legal liability in public statements.
items.e: "concede liability" = Haftung einräumen.

items.q: In UNFCCC texts, the politically charged term 'reparations' is deliberately avoided in favour of:
items.e: Offizielle Texte verwenden "compensation" statt "reparations", um Haftungsimplikationen zu vermeiden — ein bekannter diplomatischer Sprachkompromiss.

items.q: „treuhänderische Verwaltung“ (des Fonds) — das exakte englische Äquivalent:
items.e: "trusteeship" ist der Fachbegriff für die treuhänderische Fondsverwaltung (vgl. "interim trustee" im Text); die übrigen sind sinnverwandt, aber nicht der institutionelle Terminus.

items.q: „Kapitalzusage“ (an einen Fonds) — das exakte englische Äquivalent:
items.e: "(a) pledge" ist der feste Fachbegriff für eine Finanzierungszusage.

items.q: Delegates said the fund ____ never been intended to cover reconstruction costs.
items.e: Past Perfect nach Backshift der indirekten Rede.

items.q: She was appointed ____ special envoy for climate finance last year.
items.e: Nullartikel vor einmaligen Ämtern nach "appoint".

items.q: The tribunal has yet to rule ____ the admissibility of the claim.
items.e: "rule on" = entscheiden über.

items.q: The proposal remained impervious ____ objections from donor states.
items.e: Feste Rektion: "impervious to".

items.q: If donors ____ to double the pledge, the shortfall would still remain severe.
items.e: "If ... were to" — hypothetische Zukunft im formalen Register.

items.q: Had the fund been capitalised sooner, reconstruction ____ have started by now.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional: Bedingung Vergangenheit, Folge Gegenwart.

items.q: ____ donors to withdraw their pledges, the whole architecture would collapse.

items.e: "would rather" + Simple Past bei Gegenwartsbezug.

items.q: The panel went on ____ a second, far higher estimate of annual need.

items.e: Passivisches Partizip; die Aktivform würde den Fonds zum Handelnden machen.

items.e: "a number of" + Plural — im Gegensatz zu "the number of" + Singular.

items.e: "lest" + Subjunktiv "concede"; "in case" verlangte "they should concede".

items.q: Negotiators drafted the clause and then ____ at the final session.
items.e: Pronominales Objekt steht zwingend zwischen Verb und Partikel.

items.q: No sooner had the fund been announced ____ critics questioned its adequacy.
items.e: Feste Korrelation "no sooner … than"; "then" ist Adverb, kein Konnektor.

items.q: His account of the disbursement delays was ____ at odds with the official record.
items.e: Adverb modifiziert die Präpositionalphrase "at odds".

items.e: Deixisverschiebung in der Redewiedergabe: "next week" → "the following week".

items.q: Not only ____ the pledges fall short, but the disbursement timeline also slipped.

items.q: What is the central tension the passage describes?
o: Whether the International Seabed Authority should be abolished
The competing claims of resource urgency and ecological uncertainty over deep-sea mining
A territorial dispute between Pacific island states
The high cost of terrestrial cobalt mining
items.e: Kernthema: Ressourcendringlichkeit versus ökologische Ungewissheit beim Tiefseebergbau.
items.passage:
The floor of the Pacific, some four thousand metres down, is strewn with potato-sized nodules rich in cobalt, nickel and manganese — the very metals on which the energy transition is said to depend. That such riches lie beyond national jurisdiction, in an area governed by the International Seabed Authority on behalf of humankind as a whole, has turned what might have been a straightforward mining question into a test of the law of the sea itself.

Proponents of extraction argue the case is overwhelming. Terrestrial mining for the same minerals often entails deforestation, child labour and the eviction of indigenous communities; harvesting nodules from an abyssal plain, they contend, spares those harms while supplying metals the world cannot otherwise obtain quickly enough. Sceptics retort that this framing understates what is at stake. The deep sea remains the least studied ecosystem on Earth, and the sediment plumes stirred up by mining vehicles could smother filter-feeding organisms across a far wider radius than the extraction site itself, with recovery times measured in decades if not centuries.

More than thirty states, including several with the technical capacity to mine, have now called for a moratorium until the science is settled and a robust regulatory code is in place. Their position has been strengthened, somewhat awkwardly, by the Seabed Authority's own admission that it cannot yet certify any operation as environmentally sound. Industry lobbyists counter that indefinite delay is itself a decision — one that cedes first-mover advantage to whichever state eventually disregards the moratorium and proceeds unilaterally, a scenario the treaty's architects never intended to make possible.

Whatever the outcome, the episode illustrates a recurring pattern in environmental diplomacy: the temptation to extract now and study later, deferred only for as long as the loudest sceptics can keep the field from opening.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: Proponents of deep-sea mining argue that it is preferable to terrestrial mining because...
o: it avoids harms such as deforestation and child labour associated with land-based extraction
items.e: Text: "Terrestrial mining ... often entails deforestation, child labour ... harvesting nodules ... spares those harms".

items.q: How many states have called for a moratorium, according to the passage?
o: a majority of UN member states
items.e: "More than thirty states, including several with the technical capacity to mine".

items.q: The passage implies that the Seabed Authority's admission it cannot certify any operation as environmentally sound...
o: lends unexpected support to the case for a moratorium
has no bearing on the moratorium debate
was made under pressure from mining companies
items.e: "Their position has been strengthened, somewhat awkwardly, by the Seabed Authority's own admission" — implizite Unterstützung.

items.q: 'Cedes first-mover advantage' most nearly means...
o: surrenders an early competitive edge to another party
shares profits equally among all parties
items.e: "cede" = abtreten/aufgeben; "first-mover advantage" = Vorteil des ersten Akteurs, hier an andere abgetreten.

items.q: The author's attitude toward the debate can best be characterised as...
o: firmly in favour of immediate mining
presenting both sides while noting a recurring, cautionary pattern
items.e: Der Autor stellt Pro- und Contra-Argumente dar und schließt mit einer mahnenden Beobachtung ("recurring pattern... extract now and study later").

items.q: The final paragraph serves chiefly to...
o: provide new statistical evidence about sediment plumes
place the specific dispute within a broader recurring pattern in environmental diplomacy
announce the outcome of the moratorium vote
introduce a new stakeholder not mentioned earlier
items.e: Der Abschlussabsatz verallgemeinert die konkrete Debatte zu einem wiederkehrenden Muster.

items.q: What specific ecological risk does the passage attribute to mining vehicles?
o: sediment plumes smothering filter-feeding organisms over a wide radius
items.e: Text: "sediment plumes stirred up by mining vehicles could smother filter-feeding organisms across a far wider radius".

items.q: Environmental groups called for a ____ on deep-sea mining until the science is settled.
items.e: "moratorium" = befristetes Verbot/Aussetzung; "moratory" ist ein seltenes Adjektiv, "memorandum/mortgage" sind Klang-Distraktoren.

items.q: Sediment plumes could ____ filter-feeding organisms across a wide radius.
items.e: "smother" = ersticken/überdecken; "smoulder" (schwelen) ist ein Klang-Distraktor.

items.q: The Authority has yet to ____ any operation as environmentally sound.
items.e: "certify as sound" = als unbedenklich zertifizieren; "ratify" bezieht sich auf Verträge, nicht auf Betriebsgenehmigungen.

items.q: Mining lobbyists argue that indefinite delay is itself a ____ decision.
items.e: "a de facto decision" = eine faktische Entscheidung, obwohl formal keine getroffen wurde.

items.q: Regulating the abyssal plain falls within the Seabed Authority's ____ .
items.e: "purview" = Zuständigkeitsbereich; "preview" (Vorschau) ist ein Klang-Distraktor.

items.q: Terrestrial mining often entails the ____ of indigenous communities.
items.e: "eviction" = zwangsweise Räumung/Vertreibung von Land — im Text exakt so verwendet.

items.q: The industry insists a robust regulatory ____ must precede any commercial extraction.
items.e: "regulatory code" = Regelwerk; "codicil" ist ein Testamentszusatz, ein Klang-Distraktor.

items.q: Recovery of the seabed ecosystem could take decades, if not ____ .
items.e: "centuries" = Jahrhunderte; die anderen sind Wortbildungs-Fallen.

items.q: Some states fear being ____ by rivals who proceed unilaterally.
items.e: "outflanked" = überflügelt/ausmanövriert — militärische Metapher, im Diplomatiejargon gängig.

items.q: The treaty's architects never intended to ____ unilateral action.
items.e: "sanction" (hier als Verb) = billigen/gutheißen — Achtung, Gegensatz zur häufigeren Bedeutung "bestrafen".

items.q: Critics say the nodules are being treated as a resource ripe for the ____ .
items.e: "ripe for the taking" = reif zur Aneignung, feste Redewendung.

items.q: The Authority's own scientists remain ____ about the risks of large-scale extraction.
items.e: "circumspect" = vorsichtig-zurückhaltend.

items.q: Environmental NGOs accuse the industry of trying to ____ the regulatory process.
items.e: "fast-track a process" = ein Verfahren beschleunigt durchsetzen — feste Kollokation.

items.q: The moratorium coalition has grown to include states with genuine mining ____ .
items.e: "technical capability" = technische Fähigkeit/Kapazität.

items.q: Sceptics warn that the abyssal plain is the least ____ ecosystem on Earth.
items.e: Partizip nach "least" als Adjektiv gebraucht; "studious" bedeutet "fleißig/lernbegierig", nicht "erforscht".

items.q: Mining companies have ____ for expedited approval of test operations.
items.e: Finites Verb nach "have" verlangt Partizip Perfekt: "lobbied".

items.q: The Pacific seabed is ____ with nodules rich in cobalt and manganese.
items.e: "strewn with" = übersät mit — Partizip Perfekt von "strew" (unregelmäßig).

items.q: Several Pacific states depend on licensing fees as a ____ source of revenue.
items.e: "a fledgling source of revenue" = eine im Entstehen begriffene Einnahmequelle.

items.q: The industry frames the debate as one of resource ____ rather than risk.
items.e: "resource scarcity" ist der feste Fachbegriff.

items.q: Opponents accuse regulators of being ____ by industry lobbying.
items.e: "regulatory capture" = Vereinnahmung der Aufsichtsbehörde durch die von ihr beaufsichtigte Industrie.

items.q: The Authority's mandate is to act on behalf of humankind as a ____ .
items.e: "as a whole" = als Ganzes — feste Fügung, Homophon-Falle "hole".

items.q: Nodule extraction could ____ irreversible harm on ecosystems barely understood.
items.e: "inflict harm on" = Schaden zufügen; "afflict" verlangt eine andere Konstruktion ("X is afflicted by").

items.q: The compromise text was criticised as ____ , unable to bind any party to real commitments.
items.e: "a toothless agreement" = eine zahnlose, wirkungslose Vereinbarung — feste Metapher.

items.q: „Tiefseebergbau“ — das exakte englische Äquivalent:
items.e: "deep-sea mining" ist der etablierte Fachterminus; die anderen sind Umschreibungen, kein Standardbegriff.

items.q: „Manganknollen“ — das exakte englische Äquivalent:
items.e: "manganese nodules" ist der Fachbegriff; die übrigen sind umgangssprachliche Umschreibungen.

items.q: „Erschließungslizenz“ (für Meeresbodenabbau) — das exakte englische Äquivalent:
items.e: "exploration licence" ist der im Seerecht gebräuchliche Terminus; "prospecting permit" ist im Bergrecht an Land gebräuchlicher, nicht im ISA-Kontext.

items.q: Officials admitted they ____ never fully assessed the ecological risk before granting the licence.
items.e: Past Perfect nach Backshift.

items.q: He was appointed ____ chief scientific adviser to the Seabed Authority.
items.e: Nullartikel vor einmaligen Ämtern.

items.q: The regulatory code has yet to rule ____ the depth limits for extraction.
items.e: "rule on" = entscheiden über.

items.q: Recovery of the seabed proved impervious ____ every mitigation measure tried so far.
items.e: "impervious to".

items.q: If a single state ____ to defy the moratorium, others would likely follow.
items.e: "If … were to" — formale hypothetische Zukunft.

items.q: Had the code been finalised earlier, extraction ____ have begun by now.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional.

items.q: ____ the Authority to certify an operation, industry would treat it as a green light for others.
items.e: "Were … to certify".

items.q: Little ____ that the sediment plumes would travel so far from the extraction site.
items.e: Negative Inversion nach "Little".

items.q: The coalition insists that any code ____ independent verification before licences are issued.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach "insist that".

items.q: Sceptics would rather the Authority ____ no licences until the science is settled.
items.e: "would rather" + Simple Past.

items.q: The survey team went on ____ a second, more alarming set of readings.
items.e: "go on to do" = mit etwas Neuem fortfahren.

items.q: The company is said ____ test operations months before disclosure.
items.e: Berichtspassiv mit Vorzeitigkeit.

items.q: The plumes ____ have dispersed so quickly; the models all predicted otherwise.
items.e: "can't have" = logische Unmöglichkeit.

items.q: The depth threshold ____ regulators objected has since been lowered.
items.e: Vorangestellte Präposition verlangt "which".

items.q: ____ under intense pressure, the interim code left several loopholes unresolved.
items.e: Passivisches Partizip.

items.q: The Authority ____ its interim guidelines last March.
items.e: Abgeschlossener Zeitpunkt schließt Present Perfect aus.

items.q: By the time a permanent code exists, several states ____ their own unilateral rules.
items.e: Future Perfect nach "by the time".

items.q: A number of coastal states ____ still opposed to any commercial licensing.
items.e: "a number of" + Plural.

items.q: The deeper the survey went, ____ the ecological picture became.
items.e: Korrelative Struktur "the … the …".

items.q: Delegates hedged their statements ____ they seem to prejudge the outcome.
items.e: "lest" + Subjunktiv.

items.q: ____ alarmed regulators was the recovery time, not the extraction method itself.
items.e: Pseudo-Cleft "What … was …".

items.q: Regulators drafted the depth limit and then ____ under industry pressure.
items.e: Pronominales Objekt zwischen Verb und Partikel.

items.q: No sooner had the licence been approved ____ environmental groups filed an appeal.
items.e: "no sooner … than".

items.q: The company's impact assessment was ____ at odds with independent findings.
items.e: Adverb modifiziert "at odds".

items.q: The delegate promised to submit fresh data ____ following month.
items.e: Deixisverschiebung: "next month" → "the following month".

items.q: Not only ____ the moratorium hold, but new signatories also joined it.
items.e: Inversion nach "Not only" mit Simple-Past-Bezug.

items.q: Which of the following best captures the passage's central argument?
o: The Arctic Council has successfully insulated the region from external geopolitics.
Melting ice is intensifying competing claims and straining a governance framework built for a calmer era.
Russia's 2007 flag-planting settled the question of Arctic sovereignty.
China has legally established itself as an Arctic coastal state.
items.e: Kernargument: Das Eisschmelzen verschärft Ansprüche und überfordert ein für ruhigere Zeiten konzipiertes Gremium.
items.passage:
Melting ice has a way of turning cartography into diplomacy. As the Arctic Ocean's summer cover thins, sea lanes once impassable for all but icebreakers edge toward year-round viability, and seabed resources long dismissed as unreachable now look, to some governments, merely inconvenient. The result is a region where eight states, bound since 1996 by the low-key Arctic Council, find cooperative habits increasingly strained by the promise of what lies beneath the retreating ice.

Russia's flag-planting stunt on the seabed beneath the North Pole in 2007 was widely mocked as legally meaningless — sovereignty is not conferred by titanium pennants — yet it captured something real: the scramble to extend continental-shelf claims under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. Moscow, Ottawa and Copenhagen have each submitted overlapping claims to the Lomonosov Ridge, an underwater mountain range each insists is a natural extension of its own landmass. Resolving the overlap could take a further decade, and none of the claimants shows much inclination to accelerate the process while ambiguity still permits exploratory licensing.

The Council itself, designed for an era of low tension, has proved ill-suited to a moment in which one of its eight members is a pariah state under sweeping sanctions. Work on scientific and environmental programmes has continued fitfully through non-Russian channels, but the forum's founding premise — that the Arctic could be quarantined from geopolitics elsewhere — now looks almost quaint. Meanwhile, states with no Arctic coastline at all, China chief among them, have styled themselves "near-Arctic" powers and secured observer status, investing in icebreakers and research stations far from any territory they could plausibly claim.

Whether the region ends up governed by consensus or by whoever arrives first with the means to stay is, for now, an open question — and one the retreating ice will not wait patiently to see answered.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, which states have submitted overlapping claims to the Lomonosov Ridge?
o: Russia, the United States and Norway
items.e: Text: "Moscow, Ottawa and Copenhagen have each submitted overlapping claims" — d. h. Russland, Kanada und Dänemark.

items.q: Why does the author call Russia's 2007 seabed flag-planting 'legally meaningless'?
o: Because Russia lacked the technology to carry it out
Because sovereignty under international law is not established merely by planting a flag
Because the UN annulled the claim immediately
Because Canada had already claimed the same spot
items.e: "sovereignty is not conferred by titanium pennants".

items.q: The passage implies that claimant states are in no hurry to resolve the Lomonosov Ridge overlap because...
o: ambiguity currently allows them to continue exploratory licensing
international law forbids a faster resolution
none of them has the resources to pursue a claim
the ridge has been proven worthless
items.e: "none of the claimants shows much inclination to accelerate the process while ambiguity still permits exploratory licensing".

items.q: 'Near-Arctic' powers, as used in the passage, refers to states that...
o: share a land border with Russia
have no Arctic coastline but claim strategic interest in the region
are full voting members of the Arctic Council
items.e: China bezeichnet sich trotz fehlender Küste selbst als "near-Arctic", um strategisches Interesse zu bekunden.

items.q: The author's tone toward the Arctic Council's founding premise is best described as...
o: admiring and confident in its continued relevance
mildly ironic, suggesting the premise now looks outdated
angrily dismissive of the entire institution
neutral to the point of indifference
items.e: "now looks almost quaint" — leicht ironischer Unterton.

items.q: The passage's closing paragraph serves primarily to...
o: summarise the legal status of the Lomonosov Ridge dispute
leave the reader with an open, forward-looking question framed by the melting ice itself
introduce statistical data on shipping lane traffic
refute the claims made earlier about China
items.e: Rhetorische offene Frage am Schluss, gerahmt durch die Eismetapher.

items.q: How long has the Arctic Council existed, according to the passage?
o: since the Cold War's end in 1991
items.e: "bound since 1996 by the low-key Arctic Council".

items.q: Russia's flag-planting stunt was widely ____ as legally meaningless.
items.e: "deride" = verspotten; die übrigen sind Klang-Distraktoren.

items.q: Melting ice has turned the region into a geopolitical ____ .
items.e: "flashpoint" = Krisenherd/Brennpunkt.

items.q: Claimant states insist the ridge is a natural ____ of their own landmass.
items.e: "a natural extension of" = eine natürliche Fortsetzung — Fachbegriff des Seerechts.

items.q: The Council's founding premise now looks almost ____ .
items.e: "quaint" = altmodisch-liebenswert, hier ironisch für "überholt".

items.q: China has styled itself a 'near-Arctic' power to secure ____ status.
items.e: "observer status" = Beobachterstatus — fester Fachbegriff internationaler Gremien.

items.q: Resolving the overlapping claims could take a further ____ .
items.e: "a decade" = ein Jahrzehnt; "decadal" ist ein seltenes Adjektiv, hier syntaktisch falsch nach "a".

items.q: None of the claimants shows much ____ to accelerate the process.
items.e: Nomen nach "much" nötig: "inclination" = Neigung.

items.q: Work on scientific programmes has continued only ____ through non-Russian channels.
items.e: "fitfully" (Adverb) = unregelmäßig/stockend.

items.q: Sanctions have turned Russia into something of an ____ within the forum.
items.e: "an outlier" = ein Ausreißer/Außenseiter innerhalb der Gruppe.

items.q: Icebreaker construction has become a matter of national ____ .
items.e: "national prestige" = nationales Ansehen.

items.q: The claims process remains mired in legal and scientific ____ .
items.e: "ambiguity" = Mehrdeutigkeit/Unklarheit; "ambivalence" bezieht sich auf innere Zwiespältigkeit einer Person.

items.q: Investment in research stations far from any ____ territory raised eyebrows.
items.e: Adjektiv vor "territory": "plausible" = glaubhaft beanspruchbar.

items.q: The forum was designed for an era of comparatively ____ tension.
items.e: "low tension" = geringe Spannung; "lowly" bedeutet "niedrig im Rang", nicht "gering".

items.q: Cooperative habits have grown increasingly ____ under geopolitical strain.
items.e: Partizip Perfekt als Adjektiv: "strained" = angespannt.

items.q: The eight Arctic states are bound by a ____ framework rather than a binding treaty.
items.e: "low-key" = zurückhaltend/informell — beschreibt den Arktischen Rat treffend.

items.q: Some scholars argue the region risks becoming a new ____ for great-power rivalry.
items.e: "a theatre for rivalry" = ein Schauplatz — im diplomatischen Register gängige Metapher.

items.q: Denmark's claim ____ heavily on geological survey data from Greenland.
items.e: "hinge on" = abhängen von/sich stützen auf.

items.q: The scramble for continental-shelf claims has ____ old alliances.
items.e: "fray" = zermürben/dünn werden (von Beziehungen); "fracture" impliziert einen plötzlichen Bruch, nicht schleichende Abnutzung.

items.q: Coastal states must ____ their claims with the UN Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf.
items.e: "must file a claim" = einen Anspruch einreichen; nach Modalverb steht der bloße Infinitiv.

items.q: The retreating ice has ____ new shipping lanes into year-round viability.
items.e: "nudge into" = allmählich in einen Zustand drängen.

items.q: Arctic states have so far managed to keep the region largely ____ from conflicts elsewhere.
items.e: "quarantine from" = isoliert halten von — im Text als Metapher für die Trennung von globaler Geopolitik.

items.q: The forum's ____ mandate has never included hard-security matters.
items.e: "founding mandate" = ursprüngliches Gründungsmandat.

items.q: Non-Arctic states have shown a marked ____ in the region's resources.
items.e: "a marked interest in" = ein deutliches Interesse an.

items.q: „Festlandsockel“ — das exakte englische Äquivalent:
items.e: "continental shelf" ist der Rechtsbegriff aus UNCLOS Art. 76; "continental margin" ist der weiter gefasste geologische Begriff.

items.q: „Anrainerstaat“ (in Bezug auf die Arktis) — das exakte englische Äquivalent:
items.e: "coastal state" ist der offizielle UNCLOS-Terminus; "riparian state" bezieht sich fälschlich auf Flüsse, nicht auf Meeresanrainer.

items.q: „Beobachterstatus“ (im Arktischen Rat) — das exakte englische Äquivalent:
items.e: "observer status" ist der offizielle Terminus, den etwa China im Arktischen Rat innehat.

items.q: Officials conceded they ____ never anticipated the ridge dispute lasting a decade.
items.e: Past Perfect nach Backshift.

items.q: She was elected ____ chair of the Arctic science working group.
items.e: Nullartikel vor einmaligen Ämtern.

items.q: The commission has yet to rule ____ the overlapping continental-shelf claims.
items.e: "rule on".

items.q: Cooperative habits proved surprisingly impervious ____ the wider sanctions regime.
items.e: "impervious to".

items.q: If Russia ____ to leave the Council altogether, its scientific programmes would stall entirely.
items.e: "If … were to".

items.q: Had the claims process moved faster, exploratory licensing ____ have started years ago.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional.

items.q: ____ a non-Arctic state to secure a permanent seat, the Council's whole character would shift.
items.e: "Were … to secure".

items.q: Little ____ that a single sanctions regime could paralyse decades of cooperation.
items.e: Negative Inversion nach "Little".

items.q: Canada insists that the commission ____ its ruling before any licences are granted.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv.

items.q: Ottawa would rather the ridge dispute ____ settled by science, not by seniority of claim.
items.e: "would rather" + Simple Past.

items.q: The survey vessel went on ____ a second mapping expedition the following summer.
items.e: "go on to do".

items.q: Russia is said ____ new research stations months before the announcement.
items.e: Berichtspassiv mit Vorzeitigkeit.

items.q: The claim ____ have been filed on time; the deadline had already passed.
items.e: "can't have".

items.q: The ridge segment ____ three states lay claim has yet to be resolved.
items.e: Vorangestellte Präposition.

items.q: ____ in 1996, the Council was never designed to manage hard-security disputes.
items.e: Passivisches Partizip.

items.q: Russia ____ its seabed flag in 2007.
items.e: Abgeschlossener Zeitpunkt.

items.q: By the time the ridge dispute is settled, the ice ____ further still.
items.e: Future Perfect.

items.q: A number of observer states ____ eager to expand their Arctic research presence.
items.e: "a number of" + Plural.

items.passage:
Few acronyms have travelled from technical annex to trade-war flashpoint as quickly as CBAM. The European Union's carbon border adjustment mechanism, which began charging importers of steel, cement, fertiliser, aluminium, hydrogen and electricity for the emissions embedded in their goods, was conceived to solve a problem long thought intractable: how to price carbon domestically without simply exporting the emissions, and the jobs, to jurisdictions with laxer rules.

The logic is elegant enough. If European producers must buy allowances under the bloc's emissions trading system, importers escaping that cost enjoy an unearned advantage — and domestic manufacturers face an incentive to relocate rather than decarbonise, a phenomenon economists call carbon leakage. By levying an equivalent charge at the border, Brussels hopes to neutralise that advantage and, not incidentally, nudge trading partners toward carbon pricing of their own.

Trading partners have not received the logic warmly. India has called the mechanism protectionism dressed in green language; South Africa warns it could shave a percentage point off GDP growth in emissions-intensive sectors; and several developing economies argue the scheme was drafted without meaningful consultation, penalising exporters who had no say in the rules now applied to them. Even sympathetic observers concede the compliance burden falls disproportionately on smaller producers lacking the auditing capacity to document emissions with the precision Brussels demands.

Whether the mechanism survives a challenge at the World Trade Organisation remains untested; no case has yet been brought, in part because rivals fear an adverse ruling might legitimise the approach rather than kill it. What is already clear is that CBAM has become a template. Britain is drafting its own version, and several other jurisdictions are watching closely, aware that a world of divergent carbon prices cannot indefinitely coexist with a single market in traded goods.

items.q: Which statement best summarises the passage's central argument?

items.passage:
Of the world's 310 river basins shared by two or more countries, fewer than half are governed by any functioning agreement on how to divide the water that flows through them. As populations grow, glaciers retreat and rainfall patterns shift, that gap between hydrological interdependence and legal arrangement has become one of the quieter but more combustible fault lines in international relations.

The Nile illustrates the pattern starkly. Egypt has long relied on colonial-era treaties granting it the lion's share of the river's flow, treaties that upstream states such as Ethiopia never signed and increasingly refuse to honour. The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, filled over several years despite Cairo's objections, has become a proxy for a larger argument: whether historical entitlement or present-day need should govern access to a resource neither side can do without. No shots have been fired, but Egyptian officials have not ruled out that water scarcity could, in extremis, constitute grounds for war — language rarely used so plainly about any other resource.

Elsewhere the pattern repeats with local variations. India and Pakistan's Indus Waters Treaty, once cited as a rare success story surviving three wars, has been placed in abeyance by New Delhi amid deteriorating relations, leaving downstream irrigation in Pakistan's Punjab hostage to a bilateral relationship it cannot control. Central Asia's Amu Darya and Syr Darya, meanwhile, remain contested between upstream states eager to generate hydropower and downstream states dependent on the same flow for cotton irrigation, a tension inherited largely intact from Soviet-era water-sharing arrangements never designed for independent, competing states.

What unites these disputes is not any single grievance but a structural mismatch: rivers observe no border, while the institutions meant to manage them almost always do. Absent a stronger habit of joint governance, engineers upstream will keep making decisions that farmers downstream can only watch unfold.

items.q: What is the main thrust of the passage's argument?

items.passage:
When South Africa signed the first Just Energy Transition Partnership at COP26, the arrangement was billed as a template: wealthy donors would mobilise concessional finance to help a coal-dependent economy retire ageing power stations early, retrain displaced miners and build renewable capacity, all while sparing the country the higher borrowing costs it would face financing the shift alone. Indonesia, Vietnam and Senegal followed with partnerships of their own, and the concept acquired the status of a flagship model for climate diplomacy conducted, for once, as genuine partnership rather than conditionality imposed from outside.

Three years on, the record is more sobering than the launch ceremonies suggested. South Africa's plan has been repeatedly revised downward as the promised billions turned out to be overwhelmingly loans rather than grants, adding to a debt burden Pretoria was already struggling to manage. Coal communities in Mpumalanga report seeing little of the retraining funding pledged on their behalf, and the country's state utility remains financially precarious even as donor governments tout the partnership as evidence of climate finance innovation.

Indonesia's experience has proved scarcely more encouraging. Its partnership, nominally worth twenty billion dollars, has been slowed by disputes over which power plants qualify for early retirement and by donor insistence on terms Jakarta considers unduly restrictive given the scale of its coal fleet. Officials there have grown blunter in private about a mismatch between the rhetoric of partnership and the reality of finance still dominated by instruments that leave recipient governments carrying most of the risk.

None of this means the model is beyond repair. Advocates argue that early partnerships were always likely to expose flaws that later iterations could correct, provided donors accept that grants, not further loans, must anchor any partnership deserving the name. Whether that lesson is absorbed before the next round of pledges is announced remains, for now, an open question.

items.e: "Coal communities in Mpumalanga report seeing little of the retraining funding pledged on their behalf".

items.q: The passage implies that donor governments' framing of the South African partnership as 'climate finance innovation'...
o: is fully justified by the facts on the ground
sits awkwardly alongside the partnership's troubled implementation record
has been officially retracted by all donors
refers exclusively to Indonesia, not South Africa
items.e: "even as donor governments tout the partnership as evidence of climate finance innovation" folgt direkt auf die kritische Bilanz — impliziter Kontrast.

items.q: 'Anchor any partnership deserving the name' means that grants should...
o: be a minor, optional component of financing
form the essential foundation without which a partnership is not genuine
be distributed only after a partnership concludes
items.e: "anchor" = verankern/als Grundlage dienen - Grants sollen das Fundament bilden.

items.q: The author's tone toward the partnerships discussed can best be described as...
o: sympathetic to the concept but critical of its implementation so far
entirely dismissive of the model's potential
neutral and purely descriptive, offering no evaluation
items.e: "None of this means the model is beyond repair" — Konzept wird nicht verworfen, Umsetzung aber kritisiert.

items.q: The passage's last paragraph is chiefly intended to...
o: introduce a fourth country case study
qualify the preceding criticism by suggesting the model can still be corrected in future iterations
announce that all partnerships have been cancelled
provide new statistical data on coal plant closures
items.e: Konzessive Struktur: "None of this means..." leitet einen abschließenden, vorsichtig optimistischen Ausblick ein.

items.q: What figure does the passage cite for the nominal value of Indonesia's partnership?
items.e: "Its partnership, nominally worth twenty billion dollars".

items.q: Donors pledged to mobilise ____ finance to help retire ageing power stations early.
items.e: "concessional finance" = Finanzierung zu Vorzugskonditionen — Fachbegriff der Entwicklungsfinanzierung.

items.q: The promised billions turned out to be overwhelmingly loans rather than ____ .
items.e: "grants" = nicht rückzahlbare Zuschüsse — der zentrale Streitpunkt des Textes.

items.q: Coal communities report seeing little of the ____ funding pledged on their behalf.
items.e: Gerundium als Attribut: "retraining funding" = Umschulungsmittel.

items.q: The state utility remains financially ____ even as donors tout the deal.
items.e: "precarious" = prekär/wackelig; "precocious" (frühreif) ist ein Klang-Distraktor.

items.q: Jakarta considers the donor terms unduly ____ given the scale of its coal fleet.
items.e: Adjektiv nach "unduly": "restrictive" = übermäßig einschränkend.

items.q: Officials have grown blunter about the ____ between rhetoric and financial reality.
items.e: "mismatch between" = Missverhältnis zwischen — feste Kollokation.

items.q: Finance is still dominated by instruments that leave recipients carrying most of the ____ involved.
items.e: "carry the risk" = das Risiko tragen; "riskiness" ist in dieser Kollokation unüblich.

items.q: Advocates argue early partnerships were bound to ____ flaws that later versions could fix.
items.e: Infinitiv nach "to": "expose" = offenlegen.

items.q: Grants, not further loans, must ____ any partnership deserving the name.
items.e: Grundform nach Modalverb "must": "anchor" = als Grundlage verankern.

items.q: The partnership was billed as a ____ for future climate-finance deals.
items.e: "a blueprint for" = ein Muster-/Vorlagenkonzept für künftige Abkommen.

items.q: South Africa's plan has been repeatedly revised ____ as pledges fell short.
items.e: "revised downward" = nach unten korrigiert.

items.q: Vietnam and Senegal followed with partnerships of their ____ .
items.e: "of their own" = eigene/ihrer eigenen — feste possessive Fügung.

items.q: The debt burden Pretoria was already struggling to ____ has only grown.
items.e: "manage a debt burden" = eine Schuldenlast bewältigen.

items.q: Indonesia's fleet of coal plants complicates disputes over which plants ____ for early retirement.
items.e: "which plants qualify" = welche Anlagen infrage kommen — Plural-Kongruenz.

items.q: Donor governments ____ the partnership as evidence of climate-finance innovation.
items.e: "tout" = anpreisen/als Erfolg verkaufen.

items.q: The scheme's early flaws were, advocates insist, always ____ to surface.
items.e: "likely to" + Infinitiv; "likelihood" ist ein Nomen, passt syntaktisch nicht.

items.q: Wealthy donors hoped to spare the country higher ____ costs.
items.e: Gerundium als Attribut: "borrowing costs" = Finanzierungskosten.

items.q: The concept quickly acquired the ____ of a flagship model.
items.e: "acquire the status of" = den Status erlangen von.

items.q: Coal-dependent economies face a ____ transition unless financing terms improve.
items.e: Komparativ als Adjektiv: "a bumpier transition" = ein holprigerer Übergang.

items.q: The lesson may not be ____ before the next round of pledges.
items.e: Partizip Perfekt im Passiv: "lesson... absorbed" = die Lektion verinnerlicht.

items.q: Recipient governments end up ____ most of the financial risk under current instruments.
items.e: Gerundium nach "end up": "shouldering" = schultern/tragen.

items.q: The partnership model is not, advocates insist, beyond ____ .
items.e: "beyond repair" = nicht mehr zu reparieren — feste Redewendung, hier verneint.

items.q: Renewable capacity has been slow to ____ the gap left by retiring coal plants.
items.e: "bridge a gap" = eine Lücke schließen.

items.q: „Kohleausstieg“ — das exakte englische Äquivalent:
items.e: "coal phase-out" ist der etablierte energiepolitische Terminus.

items.q: „zinsvergünstigtes Darlehen“ — das exakte englische Äquivalent (informeller Fachbegriff):
items.e: "soft loan" ist der gängige informelle Fachbegriff für ein zinsvergünstigtes Darlehen, Gegenstück zum formelleren "concessional loan".

items.q: „Mischfinanzierung“ (öffentliche und private Mittel kombiniert) — das exakte englische Äquivalent:
items.e: "blended finance" ist der etablierte Fachbegriff für die Kombination öffentlicher/konzessionärer und privater Finanzierung.

items.q: Officials admitted they ____ never modelled the debt impact of the loans so precisely.
items.e: Past Perfect nach Backshift.

items.q: He was appointed ____ special envoy for the coal transition.
items.e: Nullartikel.

items.q: The panel has yet to rule ____ which plants qualify for early retirement.
items.e: "rule on".

items.q: The utility's finances proved impervious ____ years of proposed reform.
items.e: "impervious to".

items.q: If donors ____ to convert the loans into grants, the debt burden would ease considerably.
items.e: "If … were to" — gilt für alle Personen im hypothetischen Konditional.

items.q: Had the pledge been honoured in full, retraining programmes ____ have begun by now.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional.

items.q: ____ Jakarta to reject the terms outright, the entire partnership would collapse.
items.e: "Were … to reject".

items.q: Little ____ that so much of the pledge would arrive as loans rather than grants.
items.e: Negative Inversion.

items.q: Advocates demand that future partnerships ____ grants as their financial foundation.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach "demand that" — Grundform ohne -s.

items.q: Coal communities would rather the retraining funds ____ disbursed before the plants close, not after.
items.e: "would rather" + Simple Past.

items.q: Indonesia went on ____ a revised list of plants eligible for retirement.
items.e: "go on to do".

items.q: The utility is said ____ its debt figures months before the audit was released.
items.e: Berichtspassiv mit Vorzeitigkeit.

items.q: The pledge ____ have covered retraining in full; the shortfall was reported almost immediately.
items.e: "can't have".

items.q: The terms ____ Jakarta objects have remained largely unchanged since signing.
items.e: Vorangestellte Präposition.

items.q: ____ under considerable diplomatic pressure, the original pledge overstated the share of grants.
items.e: Passivisches Partizip.

items.q: South Africa ____ its transition plan last November.
items.e: Abgeschlossener Zeitpunkt.

items.q: By the time the next pledge round opens, donors ____ few concrete lessons in practice.
items.e: Future Perfect.

items.q: A number of coal communities ____ still waiting for promised retraining funds.
items.e: "a number of" + Plural.

items.q: The slower disbursement became, ____ local scepticism grew.
items.e: Korrelative Struktur.

items.q: Officials hedged their public statements ____ they seem to concede the model's failure.
items.e: "lest" + Subjunktiv.

items.q: ____ frustrated Jakarta most was the share of loans, not the total sum pledged.
items.e: Pseudo-Cleft.

items.q: Donors drafted the financing terms and then ____ after sustained criticism.
items.e: Pronominales Objekt zwischen Verb und Partikel.

items.q: No sooner had the partnership been signed ____ analysts began questioning its terms.
items.e: "no sooner … than".

items.q: The loan share was ____ higher than the launch ceremony had implied.
items.e: Adverb vor Komparativ.

items.q: The minister promised a revised breakdown ____ following quarter.
items.e: Deixisverschiebung.

items.q: Not only ____ the retraining funds arrive late, but they also fell short of the sum pledged.
items.e: Inversion nach "Not only".
