items.q: What is the author's overall assessment of the conditionality mechanism?
o: It is a purely symbolic gesture with no legal basis.
It has proved more usable than Article 7 but is still applied with excessive caution.
It has been struck down by the Court of Justice as unlawful.
It applies exclusively to Hungary and Poland by name.
items.e: Der Text zeigt: leichter auszulösen als Art. 7, aber „a lever pulled only halfway is scarcely a lever at all“ — halbherzige Anwendung.
items.passage:
When the European Union's finance ministers agreed, after a fraught all-night session, to tie the disbursement of cohesion funds to respect for judicial independence, the mechanism they created was hailed by its architects as a quiet revolution in the Union's constitutional order. Unlike Article 7 of the Treaty on European Union — the so-called 'nuclear option', which requires unanimity among the remaining member states and has consequently never been triggered to its conclusion — the conditionality regulation operates by qualified majority, a threshold considerably easier to clear. Its logic is disarmingly simple: where breaches of the rule of law are shown to affect, or seriously risk affecting, the sound management of Union funds, the Commission may propose suspending payments, and the Council may adopt that proposal without a single dissenting government holding an effective veto.

Hungary and Poland challenged the regulation before the Court of Justice, arguing that it smuggled in, through the back door of budgetary policy, a political sanction the treaties reserve for Article 7 alone. The Court's rebuff was unambiguous: respect for the rule of law is not merely one value among others but a precondition for the mutual trust on which the entire edifice of Union law depends, and a mechanism confined to the narrow question of fund management was, the judges found, a legitimate exercise of the Union's budgetary competence rather than a disguised political weapon.

Whether the ruling will translate into sustained pressure on backsliding governments is another matter. Billions in frozen funds have already been partially released following cosmetic legislative concessions, prompting accusations that the Commission, wary of a broader confrontation, has been too quick to declare victory. The mechanism's champions insist that its mere existence has altered the calculus in Budapest and Warsaw alike; its sceptics retort that a lever pulled only halfway is scarcely a lever at all.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, how does the conditionality regulation differ procedurally from Article 7?
o: It requires a two-thirds majority in the European Parliament.
It can be adopted by qualified majority rather than unanimity.
It applies only to candidate countries, not member states.
items.e: Der Text nennt explizit „operates by qualified majority“ im Gegensatz zur Einstimmigkeit bei Art. 7.

items.q: Under the mechanism described, what must be shown before the Commission may propose suspending payments?
o: That a government has lost a national election.
That the country has left the eurozone.
That rule-of-law breaches affect or risk affecting the sound management of EU funds.
That the European Parliament has passed a vote of no confidence.
items.e: Zitat: Voraussetzung ist, dass Verstöße „affect, or seriously risk affecting, the sound management of Union funds“.

items.q: How did the Court of Justice rule on Hungary's and Poland's challenge?
o: It annulled the regulation as an unlawful sanction.
It upheld the regulation as a legitimate exercise of budgetary competence.
It referred the matter back to national courts.
It suspended its judgment pending further evidence.
items.e: Das Gericht bestätigte den Mechanismus als „legitimate exercise of the Union's budgetary competence“.

items.q: What can be inferred about the Commission's approach to releasing frozen funds?
o: It has refused to release any funds under any circumstances.
It has released funds strictly in proportion to fully implemented judicial reforms.
It has been criticised for releasing funds too readily after only limited concessions.
It has delegated the decision entirely to national parliaments.
items.e: Aus „cosmetic legislative concessions“ und „too quick to declare victory“ lässt sich diese Kritik ableiten.

items.q: In context, the accusation that the regulation is 'a disguised political weapon' means that it allegedly...
o: is secretly funded by outside powers.
conceals a political sanction behind a technical, budgetary justification.
was withdrawn due to public pressure.
items.e: Die Formulierung greift den Vorwurf Ungarns/Polens auf: eine politische Sanktion getarnt als Haushaltsmaßnahme.

items.q: The author's tone toward the mechanism's practical impact is best described as...
o: outright hostile to the European Commission.
items.e: Der Autor erkennt die rechtliche Wirkung an, zweifelt aber an der konsequenten Durchsetzung — abgewogene Skepsis.

items.q: What function does the final paragraph serve in the passage's overall structure?
o: It introduces a new legal challenge not previously mentioned.
It weighs competing assessments of the mechanism's real-world effectiveness after establishing its legal validity.
It summarises the historical origins of Article 7.
It predicts the mechanism's replacement by a new treaty.
items.e: Nach der rechtlichen Bestätigung im zweiten Absatz stellt der dritte Absatz Befürworter- und Skeptikerpositionen zur tatsächlichen Wirkung gegenüber.

items.q: Member states may request a temporary ____ from certain provisions of the directive.
items.e: „derogation“ = zeitlich befristete Ausnahmeregelung von EU-Recht; „diversion“/„digression“ passen inhaltlich nicht.

items.q: The Commission opened ____ against three member states for failing to transpose the directive on time.
items.e: „infringement proceedings“ (Vertragsverletzungsverfahren) ist der feste EU-Rechtsbegriff nach Art. 258 AEUV.

items.q: Under the principle of ____, the Union acts only where objectives cannot be sufficiently achieved by member states themselves.
items.e: „subsidiarity“ = Subsidiaritätsprinzip; die anderen drei sind thematisch verwandte, aber falsche EU-Prinzipien.

items.q: A domestic court referred the question to Luxembourg for a ____ on the directive's interpretation.
items.e: „preliminary ruling“ = Vorabentscheidungsverfahren (Art. 267 AEUV).

items.q: The emergency budgetary powers were subject to a ____, lapsing automatically after eighteen months.
items.e: „sunset clause“ = Verfallsklausel, die eine Regelung automatisch befristet.

items.q: The accession treaty included a ____ permitting temporary restrictions in the event of serious disturbances.
items.e: „safeguard clause“ = Schutzklausel; die übrigen sind keine etablierten Rechtsbegriffe.

items.q: Monitors expressed concern about democratic ____ in the candidate country.
items.e: „democratic backsliding“ ist der etablierte Fachbegriff für den schrittweisen Rückbau rechtsstaatlicher Standards.

items.q: Reformers argued the judicial overhaul had eroded the system of ____.
items.e: Feste Zwillingsformel „checks and balances“ (Gewaltenteilung); die Wortumstellung in Option 3 ist unidiomatisch.

items.q: The directive strengthens protection for ____ who report breaches of Union law.
items.e: „whistleblower“ = Hinweisgeber; feststehender Terminus der EU-Whistleblower-Richtlinie.

items.q: Journalists warned that the criminal libel provision would have a ____ on investigative reporting.
items.e: „chilling effect“ = einschüchternde Wirkung; feste Kollokation, die übrigen Optionen sind keine etablierten Wendungen.

items.q: Negotiators secured a ____ exempting judicial salaries from the freeze.
items.e: „carve-out“ = punktuelle Ausnahmeregelung innerhalb eines größeren Abkommens; „carve-up“ bedeutet Aufteilung/Zerschlagung.

items.q: A share of the recovery fund was ____ specifically for judicial reform projects.
items.e: „earmark funds for“ ist die im Haushaltskontext idiomatisch übliche Kollokation.

items.q: The new authority acts as an independent ____ over data-protection compliance.
items.e: „watchdog“ = Kontrollorgan; feste Kollokation „independent watchdog“.

items.q: Lawyers quickly identified a ____ in the regulation's wording.
items.e: „loophole“ = ausnutzbare Regelungslücke; feste Kollokation „find/identify a loophole“.

items.q: Critics accused the assembly of merely ____ decisions taken elsewhere.
items.e: „to rubber-stamp“ = unkritisch billigen/durchwinken, ohne eigene Prüfung.

items.q: Without enforcement powers, the new body risked becoming ____.
items.e: „toothless“ = zahnlos/wirkungslos, feste idiomatische Wendung für Gremien ohne Durchsetzungsmacht.

items.q: Sceptics accused the government of trying to ____ the benefits of membership while rejecting its obligations.
items.e: „cherry-pick“ = sich selektiv die Rosinen herauspicken; feste Redewendung in der EU-Debatte über Sonderrechte.

items.q: Mutual trust between national courts is described as the ____ of the Union's legal order.
items.e: „cornerstone“ = Eckpfeiler/Grundpfeiler; feste Metapher, die übrigen Optionen existieren nicht.

items.q: The committee called for a thorough ____ of the appointment procedure.
items.e: „overhaul“ = grundlegende Überarbeitung; die anderen sind klangähnliche, aber inhaltlich falsche Verben.

items.q: Judicial independence is ____ in the constitution and cannot be altered by a simple majority.
items.e: „entrenched“ betont, dass eine Bestimmung besonderen Schutz vor Änderung durch einfache Mehrheit genießt — anders als das bloß deklarative „enshrined“.

items.q: Any single government retains ____ over amendments to the founding treaties.
items.e: „veto power“ ist die feste Kollokation; die übrigen Wortkombinationen sind unidiomatisch.

items.q: Unanimity requirements have repeatedly produced institutional ____.
items.e: „gridlock“ = Stillstand durch blockierte Entscheidungsprozesse; im politischen Register die gängigste Kollokation mit „institutional“.

items.q: The reform aims to strengthen ____ toward the European Parliament.
items.e: „accountability“ = Rechenschaftspflicht; „liability“/„culpability“ beziehen sich auf Schuld/Haftung, nicht auf demokratische Rechenschaft.

items.q: Parliament demanded greater ____ of the Commission's use of discretionary funds.
items.e: „oversight“ = Aufsicht/Kontrolle; „overlook“ bedeutet übersehen — ein klassischer Fehlgriff.

items.q: Judicial budgets were ____ from the wider austerity measures.
items.e: „ring-fence“ = etwas gesondert absichern/vor Kürzungen schützen; feste Wendung.

items.q: Analysts accused both sides of engaging in ____ over the budget veto.
items.e: „brinkmanship“ = Politik des bewussten Vabanquespiels/an-den-Rand-Gehens; „statesmanship“ trägt eine hier unpassende positive Konnotation.

items.q: The treaty requires that each state ____ its obligations without delay.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach „require that“ — Grundform ohne -s.

items.q: The presidency insisted that the vote ____ postponed until consensus emerged.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach „insist that“: „be postponed“, keine Personalendung.

items.q: Not only ____ the mechanism survive the legal challenge, but its scope was also broadened.
items.e: Inversion nach vorangestelltem „Not only“: Hilfsverb „did“ + Grundform „survive“.

items.q: Under no circumstances ____ the Council waive the requirement of unanimity.
items.e: Inversion nach negativem Adverbial „Under no circumstances“: Hilfsverb vor Subjekt, nicht Subjekt vor Hilfsverb.

items.q: Had the veto not been exercised, the sanctions package ____ already in force.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional: Bedingung Vergangenheit (Had…not), Folge Gegenwart (already).

items.q: If the court ____ jurisdiction, the case would still be pending today.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional: vergangene Ursache (had lacked), gegenwärtige Folge (would still be pending).

items.q: The delegation ____ have anticipated the backlash; the warning signs were everywhere.
items.e: „should have“ = Kritik an einer versäumten Handlung in der Vergangenheit.

items.q: She ____ have signed the protocol herself; her signature does not appear on any copy.
items.e: „can't have“ = logischer Ausschluss im Rückblick.

items.q: ____ concerns the drafters most was the absence of an enforcement mechanism.
items.e: Pseudo-Cleft: „What … was …“.

items.q: ____ came under scrutiny was not the treaty's text but its implementation.
items.e: Pseudo-Cleft: „What … was …“ hebt den Kontrast hervor.

items.q: The spokesperson said the ruling ____ into force the following month.
items.e: Backshift in indirekter Rede: will → would; „the following month“ ersetzt „next month“.

items.q: He claimed he ____ the file weeks before the leak became public.
items.e: Past Perfect für Vorzeitigkeit in indirekter Rede.

items.q: ____ by both chambers, the bill was sent to the president for signature.
items.e: Passivisches Partizip: Die Aktivformen würden den Gesetzentwurf fälschlich zum Handelnden machen.

items.q: ____ the implications carefully, the committee decided to delay the vote by a week.
items.e: Vorzeitiges Partizip „Having weighed“ zeigt eine abgeschlossene Handlung vor der Hauptaussage.

items.q: The longer the negotiations dragged on, ____ the compromise seemed.
items.e: Korrelative Struktur „the … the …“ verlangt den bestimmten Artikel vor dem Komparativ.

items.q: ____ did the reform pass unopposed, but it also won cross-party praise.
items.e: Feste Korrelation „not only … but also …“ mit obligatorischer Inversion nach vorangestelltem „Not only“.

items.q: The minister is believed ____ the document before it was leaked.
items.e: Vorzeitiger Infinitiv nach Berichtspassiv: „is believed to have seen“.

items.q: The treaty is reported ____ ratified by a narrow margin next week.
items.e: „is reported to be ratified“ — Passiv-Infinitiv für ein bevorstehendes Ereignis.

items.q: The clause ____ the parties agreed has since been renegotiated.
items.e: „agree to“ verlangt bei vorangestellter Präposition „to which“, niemals „that“.

items.q: The precedent ____ the ruling relies has been widely contested.
items.e: „rely on“ → vorangestellte Präposition erzwingt „on which“.

items.q: If only the delegation ____ more time before the summit, the outcome might have differed.
items.e: „If only“ + Past Perfect für einen unerfüllten Wunsch in der Vergangenheit.

items.q: The committee ____ examine the evidence thoroughly before reaching its verdict, contrary to the accusations of haste.
items.e: Emphatisches „did“ zur Betonung/Widerlegung eines Vorwurfs, gefolgt vom Grundverb „examine“.

items.q: She was appointed ____ special envoy to the region shortly after the ceasefire.
items.e: Nullartikel vor einmaligen Ämtern/Funktionen nach „appoint“.

items.q: By the time the summit convenes, the drafting committee ____ its final report.
items.e: Future Perfect für ein Ereignis, das vor einem zukünftigen Zeitpunkt abgeschlossen sein wird.

items.q: The commissioner went on ____ the second half of the reform package in a separate statement.
items.e: „go on to do“ = mit etwas Neuem fortfahren, im Gegensatz zu „go on doing“ (dasselbe fortsetzen).

items.q: The envoy chose his words with extreme care ____ he inadvertently provoke a diplomatic incident.
items.e: „lest“ + Subjunktiv „provoke“ (ohne -s); „in case“ verlangte „he should provoke“.

items.q: What is the passage's central argument about the prospects for a binding international AI treaty?
o: A binding treaty is imminent and will be signed within the year.
Divergent national interests make a single binding regime unlikely; overlapping voluntary arrangements are the more probable outcome.
No country has any interest in regulating artificial intelligence at all.
Only the United Nations can legitimately negotiate such an agreement.
items.e: Der Autor argumentiert, dass unterschiedliche nationale Interessen ein verbindliches Einzelabkommen unwahrscheinlich machen und stattdessen ein Flickenteppich freiwilliger Regelungen entsteht.
items.passage:
Diplomats accustomed to negotiating arms control or trade agreements have discovered, somewhat to their discomfort, that artificial intelligence resists the categories those disciplines were built around. A missile can be counted; a warhead can be inspected. A model's weights, by contrast, can be copied in seconds, retrained beyond recognition, and deployed by an actor no treaty ever anticipated. Small wonder, then, that the flurry of summits convened over the past several years — in Bletchley, in Seoul, in San Francisco — has produced communiqués rich in aspiration and thin on enforceable commitment.

The fault line is not, as popular commentary often suggests, simply between an AI-cautious Europe and an AI-permissive United States. It runs instead through the incompatible premises each bloc brings to the table. Washington has resisted anything resembling binding external oversight of frontier laboratories, wary of ceding a technological edge accumulated at enormous private expense. Brussels, having already legislated a risk-tiered framework of its own, presses for that model's export, only to find third countries reluctant to import rules they had no hand in drafting. Beijing, for its part, professes support for multilateral governance while quietly ring-fencing the domestic deployment of the technology as a matter of sovereign prerogative, not international negotiation.

What has nonetheless emerged, almost by default, is a lattice of narrower arrangements: information-sharing pacts between safety institutes, voluntary testing commitments extracted from the largest developers, and a UN resolution notable chiefly for what it declines to mandate. Sceptics dismiss this patchwork as an alibi for inaction; its defenders counter that, absent verifiable technical means of enforcing any grander bargain, a loose architecture of overlapping, mutually reinforcing commitments may be the only regime the technology's own volatility will currently permit. Whether that architecture can be tightened before the gap between capability and governance widens further is, at this point, an open question that no summit communiqué has yet answered.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, why do arms-control analogies fail to fit artificial intelligence?
o: Because AI models, unlike missiles, cannot be counted or physically inspected and can be copied instantly.
Because no international summits on AI have ever taken place.
Because artificial intelligence is not considered a security issue by any government.
Because arms-control treaties have never involved verification mechanisms.
items.e: Der erste Absatz kontrastiert zählbare/inspizierbare Waffen mit kopierbaren, umtrainierbaren Modellgewichten.

items.q: What does the passage identify as the true 'fault line' between blocs, as opposed to the popular narrative?
o: A divide between rich and poor countries over funding.
Incompatible underlying premises about oversight and sovereignty, not simply caution versus permissiveness.
A dispute over which language negotiations should be conducted in.
A disagreement about which city should host future summits.
items.e: Der Text weist die vereinfachte „vorsichtiges Europa vs. permissive USA“-Erzählung zurück und nennt stattdessen unvereinbare Grundannahmen zu Aufsicht und Souveränität.

items.q: What can be inferred about Beijing's stated position versus its actual practice, according to the passage?
o: Beijing rejects multilateral governance outright and says so publicly.
Beijing supports multilateral governance rhetorically while shielding domestic deployment from outside negotiation.
Beijing has fully opened its domestic AI deployment to international inspection.
Beijing has withdrawn from all UN discussions on the topic.
items.e: „professes support … while quietly ring-fencing the domestic deployment … as a matter of sovereign prerogative“ zeigt die Diskrepanz zwischen Rhetorik und Praxis.

items.q: In context, 'a lattice of narrower arrangements' refers to...
o: a single comprehensive binding treaty replacing all summits.
a network of smaller, overlapping voluntary agreements rather than one grand bargain.
a legal ban on frontier AI development.
a physical infrastructure project shared between safety institutes.
items.e: Der Begriff beschreibt das Geflecht kleinerer, sich überschneidender freiwilliger Vereinbarungen, das anstelle eines großen Abkommens entstanden ist.

items.q: The author's tone toward the current patchwork of AI arrangements is best described as...
o: wholly dismissive, viewing it as worthless.
evenhandedly weighing both sceptical and defensive views without fully endorsing either.
indifferent to whether governance succeeds or fails.
items.e: Der Autor stellt Kritiker- und Verteidigerpositionen gegenüber, ohne sich eindeutig festzulegen — abwägender Ton.

items.q: What role does the passage's final sentence play?
o: It provides the definitive answer to whether governance will succeed.
It leaves the central question about tightening the governance architecture explicitly open.
It announces a new summit location.
It contradicts the passage's earlier argument about enforcement.
items.e: Der Schlusssatz formuliert die Frage bewusst als offen — „an open question that no summit communiqué has yet answered“.

items.q: Why does Brussels struggle to export its risk-tiered regulatory model, according to the passage?
o: Because third countries are unwilling to adopt rules they had no part in drafting.
Because the European Union has abandoned the model itself.
Because no other country has any AI regulation whatsoever.
Because the United States has banned the model's use abroad.
items.e: Zitat: „third countries reluctant to import rules they had no hand in drafting“.

items.q: The summit's final statement was long on ambition but ____ on enforceable commitments.
items.e: „thin on“ ist die feste Kollokation für einen Mangel an Substanz; „slim/slight/narrow“ passen hier nicht idiomatisch.

items.q: Negotiators struggled to find ____ ground between the two competing regulatory models.
items.e: „common ground“ ist die feste Redewendung für eine gemeinsame Verhandlungsbasis.

items.q: The laboratory's ____ compliance with the testing protocol drew praise from regulators.
items.e: „voluntary compliance“ = freiwillige Einhaltung; „wilful“ bedeutet vorsätzlich/eigensinnig, nicht freiwillig.

items.q: Governments have been reluctant to cede any ____ over frontier model development to outside bodies.
items.e: „cede oversight“ = Aufsicht abtreten; „overlook“ bedeutet übersehen — ein klassischer Fehlgriff.

items.q: Developers were asked to sign up to a set of ____ safety commitments ahead of the summit.
items.e: „non-binding safety commitments“ ist der in der KI-Governance-Debatte (z. B. AI Safety Summit) etablierte Begriff für rechtlich unverbindliche Zusagen; „informal“ und „tentative“ treffen die rechtliche Nuance nicht, „conditional“ bedeutet an Bedingungen geknüpft.

items.q: Critics warned that the resolution was little more than a face-saving ____.
items.e: „fig leaf“ = Feigenblatt, feste Metapher für eine dünne Rechtfertigung ohne echten Gehalt.

items.q: The proposed framework classifies systems by ____ , ranging from minimal to unacceptable.
items.e: „risk tier“ ist der in der EU-KI-Verordnung etablierte Terminus für die Risikoeinstufung.

items.q: Smaller states fear being left out of the ____ where the rules of frontier AI are actually being written.
items.e: „where the rules are being written“ verlangt die feste Metapher „the tables“ (am Tisch sitzen = mitentscheiden).

items.q: The company's safety pledge was widely seen as a ____ exercise rather than a substantive change.
items.e: „box-ticking exercise“ = reine Formsache ohne inhaltliche Substanz; feste Redewendung.

items.q: The institute was set up to act as an independent ____ on frontier model capabilities.
items.e: „watchdog“ = Kontrollorgan; feste Kollokation im regulatorischen Kontext, gebräuchlicher als die übrigen Optionen.

items.q: Delegates conceded that verification remained the ____ of any future agreement.
items.e: „sticking point“ = der strittige Kernpunkt, an dem Verhandlungen hängen bleiben; feste Redewendung.

items.q: The declaration was criticised for being aspirational rather than ____.
items.e: Feststehendes Gegensatzpaar „aspirational rather than binding“ im diplomatischen Register.

items.q: Model weights can be ____ within hours of release, complicating any export-control regime.
items.e: „exfiltrate“ = unbemerkt herausschleusen; die klanglich ähnlichen Verben bedeuten etwas völlig anderes.

items.q: The two delegations remained ____ apart on the question of third-party audits.
items.e: „worlds apart“ = grundverschieden/an entgegengesetzten Enden (Plural ohne Apostroph); „world's“ ist der Possessiv-Fehlgriff, „words“ der Homophon-ähnliche Distraktor.

items.q: The taskforce was given a broad ____ to draft technical standards without political interference.
items.e: „mandate“ = Auftrag/Vollmacht eines Gremiums; die übrigen Optionen passen nicht in diesem institutionellen Kontext.

items.q: The report's authors were careful to ____ their conclusions with numerous caveats.
items.e: „hedge conclusions with caveats“ = Aussagen vorsichtig einschränken; feste Kollokation.

items.q: The safety institute's findings were later ____ by an independent replication study.
items.e: „corroborate“ = bestätigen/erhärten; „collaborate“ (zusammenarbeiten) ist der klassische Verwechslungsfehler.

items.q: Developers who ignore the testing protocol risk being named and ____ in the institute's public register.
items.e: Feste Zwillingsformel „naming and shaming“; die übrigen Reimwörter ergeben hier keinen Sinn.

items.q: The two blocs' regulatory philosophies proved fundamentally ____ despite years of dialogue.
items.e: „irreconcilable“ ist die korrekt gebildete Adjektivform; die übrigen sind keine existierenden Wörter.

items.q: Smaller economies warned against a regulatory ____ that only the largest labs could afford to comply with.
items.e: „regulatory straitjacket“ = übermäßig einengende Regulierung; feste Metapher.

items.q: The negotiators finally reached a ____ compromise on data-sharing thresholds after months of deadlock.
items.e: „hard-won compromise“ = mühsam erkämpfter Kompromiss; feste Kollokation.

items.q: The proposal was quietly ____ after industry lobbying intensified.
items.e: „jettison a proposal“ = einen Vorschlag fallenlassen/aufgeben; nur die finite Vergangenheitsform passt hier.

items.q: Critics called the laboratory's internal testing process worryingly ____.
items.e: „opaque“ ist im Governance-Register das feste Gegenteil von „transparent“ und die übliche Kollokation für undurchsichtige Verfahren.

items.q: Some governments accused others of ____ international talks by legislating unilaterally first.
items.e: „front-run“ = anderen zuvorkommen und einseitig Fakten schaffen; die übrigen Formen sind fehlerhafte Wortbildungen.

items.q: Negotiators insisted the verification clause be legally ____.
items.e: „watertight“ = rechtlich lückenlos/hieb- und stichfest, feste Metapher im Rechtsregister; „waterproof“ bezieht sich auf physische Gegenstände.

items.q: The interim guidelines were widely seen as a ____ measure pending a permanent framework.
items.e: „stopgap measure“ = vorübergehende Notlösung; nur die erste Form ist ein existierendes Wort.

items.q: The protocol requires that every laboratory ____ its testing results before deployment.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach „require that“ — Grundform ohne -s.

items.q: Delegates demanded that the taskforce ____ its findings publicly.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach „demand that“ — Grundform ohne -s.

items.q: Rarely ____ negotiators found themselves so far apart after months of technical talks.
items.e: Inversion nach vorangestelltem „Rarely“: Hilfsverb „have“ vor Subjekt (Present Perfect).

items.q: Not until the third summit ____ any concrete testing commitment secured.
items.e: Inversion nach vorangestelltem „Not until“: Hilfsverb vor Subjekt, hier Passiv „was … secured“.

items.q: Had the summit produced a binding text, enforcement ____ a separate problem entirely today.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional: Bedingung Vergangenheit (Had produced), Folge Gegenwart (today).

items.q: If the treaty ____ verification clauses, compliance would be far easier to assess now.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional: vergangene Ursache (had included), gegenwärtige Folge (would be).

items.q: The taskforce ____ have anticipated the leak; internal warnings had circulated for weeks.
items.e: „should have“ = Kritik an einer versäumten Handlung in der Vergangenheit.

items.q: The delegation ____ have approved that clause; it directly contradicts their earlier statement.
items.e: „can't have“ = logischer Ausschluss im Rückblick.

items.q: ____ troubled the smaller delegations most was their exclusion from the drafting sessions.
items.e: Pseudo-Cleft: „What … was …“.

items.q: ____ the report exposed was not the technology's risks but the regulators' unpreparedness.
items.e: Pseudo-Cleft „What … was …“ hebt den Kontrast zwischen zwei Möglichkeiten hervor.

items.q: The envoy said the resolution ____ adopted at the next session.
items.e: Backshift in indirekter Rede: will be → would be.

items.q: She admitted she ____ the draft text before the leak occurred.
items.e: Past Perfect für Vorzeitigkeit in indirekter Rede.

items.q: ____ by three governments, the joint statement carried unusual diplomatic weight.
items.e: Passivisches Partizip: Die Aktivformen würden die Erklärung fälschlich zum Handelnden machen.

items.q: ____ the technical annex thoroughly, the committee approved the framework without further amendment.
items.e: Vorzeitiges Partizip „Having reviewed“ zeigt eine abgeschlossene Handlung vor der Hauptaussage.

items.q: The more capable the models became, ____ the enforcement gap grew.
items.e: Korrelative Struktur „the … the …“ verlangt den bestimmten Artikel vor dem Komparativ.

items.q: ____ did the resolution avoid binding language, but it also omitted any timeline for review.
items.e: Feste Korrelation „not only … but also …“ mit obligatorischer Inversion nach vorangestelltem „Not only“.

items.q: The lab is believed ____ its most capable model months before public release.
items.e: Vorzeitiger Infinitiv nach Berichtspassiv: „is believed to have tested“.

items.q: The framework is reported ____ formally adopted at the ministers' meeting next month.
items.e: „is reported to be adopted“ — Passiv-Infinitiv für ein bevorstehendes Ereignis.

items.q: The clause ____ the delegations objected has since been dropped from the draft.
items.e: „object to“ verlangt bei vorangestellter Präposition „to which“, niemals „that“.

items.q: The standard ____ compliance is measured has yet to be agreed by either bloc.
items.e: „measure against a standard“ → vorangestellte Präposition erzwingt „against which“.

items.q: If only the taskforce ____ verification standards earlier, the current dispute might not exist.
items.e: „If only“ + Past Perfect für einen unerfüllten Wunsch in der Vergangenheit.

items.q: The institute ____ flag the anomaly weeks before the incident, contrary to claims of negligence.
items.e: Emphatisches „did“ zur Widerlegung eines Vorwurfs, gefolgt vom Grundverb „flag“.

items.q: She was appointed ____ special rapporteur on emerging technologies shortly after the summit.
items.e: Nullartikel vor einmaligen Ämtern/Funktionen nach „appoint“.

items.q: By the time the next summit convenes, the taskforce ____ its technical standards.
items.e: Future Perfect für ein Ereignis, das vor einem zukünftigen Zeitpunkt abgeschlossen sein wird.

items.q: The chair went on ____ the dissenting delegations' objections in a closed session.
items.e: „go on to do“ = mit etwas Neuem fortfahren, im Gegensatz zu „go on doing“ (dasselbe fortsetzen).

items.q: The drafters phrased the clause ambiguously ____ any single bloc feel singled out.
items.e: „lest“ + Subjunktiv „feel“ (ohne -s); „in case“ verlangte „it should feel“.

items.q: What is the passage's central claim about the 1967 Outer Space Treaty?
o: It comprehensively regulates the commercial extraction of space resources.
Its silence on resource extraction has left a legal vacuum that national legislation is filling unilaterally.
It explicitly grants ownership of asteroids to the first state to reach them.
It has been formally superseded by the Artemis Accords.
items.e: Der Text beschreibt, wie das Schweigen des Vertrags zur Ressourcengewinnung eine Lücke hinterlässt, die einzelne Staaten nun im Alleingang füllen.
items.passage:
The treaty that has governed the exploration of outer space since 1967 was drafted by diplomats who could not plausibly have imagined a private company mining platinum from an asteroid, and it shows. Article II forbids any state from appropriating celestial bodies through claims of sovereignty, yet it says nothing whatsoever about whether a company, licensed by its home state, may extract and sell what it hauls from the lunar surface. Into that silence, several spacefaring nations have stepped with domestic legislation asserting precisely such a right, reasoning that whatever is not expressly prohibited must, by implication, be permitted.

Critics of this approach — a sizeable bloc within the UN's Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space — regard it as a thinly veiled land grab dressed up in the language of legal interpretation. If extraction rights may simply be legislated into existence by whichever state moves first, they argue, the treaty's foundational premise that space belongs to no one is quietly hollowed out from within, one national statute at a time. Supporters of the unilateral route counter that waiting for a comprehensive multilateral mining code, given the glacial pace of consensus-based negotiation, would condemn commercial space activity to indefinite paralysis, ceding the field in practice to whichever actor is least troubled by legal ambiguity.

A parallel accord, championed chiefly by Washington and signed by a growing roster of partners, attempts to bridge the gap by affirming that resource extraction is lawful while insisting it need not constitute national appropriation — a distinction that satisfies its signatories rather more than it satisfies the treaty's original drafters, several of whom are, notably, not among the signatories. Whether this coalition of the willing amounts to an emerging customary norm or merely a convenient reading shared by those who stand to benefit from it remains, for now, a matter on which reasonable international lawyers profoundly disagree.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, what does Article II of the treaty actually prohibit?
o: Any commercial activity in space whatsoever.
States from appropriating celestial bodies through claims of sovereignty.
Private companies from operating without a state licence.
The signing of any parallel bilateral accords.
items.e: Zitat: „Article II forbids any state from appropriating celestial bodies through claims of sovereignty“.

items.q: What reasoning do spacefaring nations use to justify domestic extraction legislation, per the passage?
o: That the UN has explicitly authorised such legislation.
That whatever is not expressly prohibited by the treaty must be permitted.
That the treaty has expired and no longer applies.
That extraction rights were granted by a prior international court ruling.
items.e: Zitat: „whatever is not expressly prohibited must, by implication, be permitted“.

items.q: What is the critics' main objection to the unilateral legislative approach, according to the passage?
o: That it is too expensive for most states to pursue.
That it risks hollowing out the treaty's premise that space belongs to no one, state by state.
That it violates a specific clause banning private companies.
That it has been rejected by every spacefaring nation.
items.e: Zitat: „the treaty's foundational premise that space belongs to no one is quietly hollowed out from within, one national statute at a time“.

items.q: What can be inferred about the relationship between the parallel accord and the original treaty's drafters?
o: All original drafters have enthusiastically endorsed the accord.
Several original drafters are notably absent from among the accord's signatories, implying reservations.
The accord was drafted by the same individuals who wrote the original treaty.
The original drafters have publicly demanded the accord's repeal.
items.e: Zitat: „several of whom are, notably, not among the signatories“ deutet auf Vorbehalte der ursprünglichen Verfasser hin.

items.q: In context, 'a thinly veiled land grab dressed up in the language of legal interpretation' means the critics view unilateral extraction laws as...
o: genuinely novel legal scholarship with no ulterior motive.
an appropriation of resources disguised as a legitimate legal argument.
a purely symbolic gesture with no practical effect.
a proposal that has already been withdrawn.
items.e: Die Metapher beschreibt den Vorwurf, dass eine faktische Aneignung als bloße Rechtsauslegung getarnt wird.

items.q: The author's tone in the final paragraph is best described as...
o: dismissive of both sides of the debate.
noncommittal, presenting the disagreement as genuinely unresolved.
strongly supportive of the parallel accord.
items.e: Der letzte Satz lässt die Frage bewusst offen — „remains … a matter on which reasonable international lawyers profoundly disagree“.

items.q: What is the function of the second paragraph within the passage's overall structure?
o: It introduces the treaty's text for the first time.
It sets out the two opposing arguments about the legitimacy of unilateral extraction legislation.
It describes the technical process of asteroid mining.
It announces the treaty's formal repeal.
items.e: Der zweite Absatz stellt Kritiker- und Befürworterargumente zur unilateralen Gesetzgebung einander gegenüber.

items.q: The treaty's silence on extraction rights left a legal ____ that states have since tried to fill.
items.e: „legal vacuum“ = rechtliche Regelungslücke; feste Kollokation im Völkerrecht.

items.q: Several delegations accused the initiative of being a thinly ____ attempt to claim resources ahead of any agreed framework.
items.e: „thinly veiled“ = kaum verschleiert; feste Kollokation, die übrigen Wörter kollokieren hier nicht idiomatisch.

items.q: Without a comprehensive mining code, commercial actors operate in a state of legal ____.
items.e: „legal limbo“ = ungeklärter, schwebender Rechtszustand; feste Redewendung.

items.q: The coalition's members insist their reading of the treaty reflects an emerging ____ norm.
items.e: „customary norm“ = Völkergewohnheitsrechtsnorm, die sich durch Staatenpraxis herausbildet; „conventional“ meint gerade das Vertragsrecht, nicht die Praxis.

items.q: Negotiators fear that unilateral mining laws could ____ decades of carefully built consensus.
items.e: „unravel consensus“ = mühsam aufgebauten Konsens auflösen; feste, im diplomatischen Register gängige Kollokation.

items.q: The parallel accord was designed to ____ the gap left by decades of stalled multilateral talks.
items.e: „bridge the gap“ = eine Lücke überbrücken; feste Redewendung.

items.q: Some spacefaring states are accused of trying to ____ the field before any binding rules exist.
items.e: „stake out“ = ein Gebiet/Feld für sich beanspruchen; feste Wendung, historisch von Grundstücksabsteckung übertragen.

items.q: Given the glacial pace of consensus-based talks, some officials argue commercial actors cannot ____ negotiations to conclude.
items.e: „wait around for“ = untätig auf etwas warten; einzig idiomatisch korrekte Präpositionalverbindung.

items.q: Critics say the unilateral approach amounts to a de facto ____ of a shared resource.
items.e: „appropriation“ = Aneignung eines Gemeinguts durch einseitiges Handeln; „expropriation“ setzt einen ursprünglichen Eigentümer voraus, der hier gerade fehlt.

items.q: The committee's mandate is limited to drafting recommendations; it has no ____ authority.
items.e: „binding authority“ = verbindliche Entscheidungsgewalt; feste Kollokation.

items.q: The accord's drafters were careful to ____ any suggestion that it constitutes national appropriation.
items.e: „disclaim“ = ausdrücklich zurückweisen/dementieren; „declaim“ bedeutet öffentlich vortragen — ein klassischer Verwechslungsfehler.

items.q: Smaller states worry about being permanently ____ from the benefits of space resource extraction.
items.e: „shut out from“ = von etwas ausgeschlossen sein; feste Partikelverbverbindung.

items.q: The negotiations have been ____ by disagreement over benefit-sharing with non-spacefaring nations.
items.e: „hampered by“ ist im diplomatischen Register die gebräuchlichste Kollokation für ein Verhandlungshemmnis; alle Optionen sind hier semantisch nah, „hampered“ jedoch die idiomatisch dominante Wahl mit „by disagreement“.

items.q: The proposed mining code remains, for now, little more than a ____ on paper.
items.e: „a blueprint on paper“ = ein bislang rein theoretischer Entwurf ohne praktische Umsetzung; feste Wendung.

items.q: Some delegations accused Washington of trying to ____ its national framework as the de facto international standard.
items.e: „entrench a framework as the standard“ betont die Absicht, es dauerhaft und schwer revidierbar zu verankern.

items.q: Legal scholars remain sharply ____ over whether the accord reflects genuine customary practice.
items.e: „sharply divided over“ ist die feste Kollokation für tiefgreifende Meinungsverschiedenheit unter Fachleuten.

items.q: The treaty's drafters could scarcely have ____ commercial asteroid mining when they wrote Article II.
items.e: Nach dem Modalverb-Perfekt „could scarcely have“ folgt das Partizip Perfekt „foreseen“.

items.q: The coalition's reading of the treaty is convenient for those who ____ from it.
items.e: „stand to benefit from“ = voraussichtlich profitieren; feste idiomatische Wendung.

items.q: Without an agreed code, commercial mining risks becoming a lawless ____.
items.e: „free-for-all“ = ungeregeltes Durcheinander, in dem sich jeder selbst bedient; feste Redewendung.

items.q: Officials from non-signatory states dismissed the accord as a ____ arrangement serving only its members.
items.e: „self-serving“ = eigennützig; nur diese Form ist ein korrektes, gebräuchliches Adjektiv.

items.q: The committee's annual report is largely ____ rather than a genuine negotiating text.
items.e: Adjektivform „symbolic“ nach „largely“; die übrigen Formen sind grammatisch fehlerhaft oder falsche Wortarten.

items.q: The committee's resolutions remain purely ____ , carrying moral rather than legal weight.

items.q: The accord was hailed as a ____ step, whatever its legal shortcomings.

items.q: Several states reserved the right to ____ of the accord's dispute-resolution clause.

items.q: Delegates called the ruling a ____ moment for the future governance of celestial resources.
items.e: „watershed moment“ ist die feste Kollokation für einen entscheidenden Wendepunkt; die anderen Substantive kollokieren weniger natürlich mit „moment“.

items.q: The committee recommended that the code ____ binding provisions on benefit-sharing.

items.e: Gemischter Konditional: Bedingung Vergangenheit (Had addressed), Folge Gegenwart (today).

items.q: If the drafters ____ commercial mining, the treaty's wording would look very different now.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional: vergangene Ursache (had anticipated), gegenwärtige Folge (would look).

items.q: The agency ____ have consulted the smaller states before publishing the framework; the omission caused an outcry.

items.q: ____ divides the two camps is not the treaty's wording but its silence.

items.q: ____ the accord achieved was not consensus but a coalition of the willing.
items.e: Pseudo-Cleft „What … was …“ kontrastiert zwei Ergebnisse.

items.q: The spokesperson said the code ____ finalised within the decade.

items.q: She explained that the committee ____ the proposal months earlier.
items.e: Past Perfect für Vorzeitigkeit in indirekter Rede.

items.q: ____ by a handful of spacefaring nations, the accord lacks universal legitimacy.
items.e: Passivisches Partizip: Die Aktivformen würden das Abkommen fälschlich zum Handelnden machen.

items.q: ____ the treaty's original text closely, the tribunal found no explicit prohibition on extraction.
items.e: Vorzeitiges Partizip „Having examined“ zeigt eine abgeschlossene Prüfung vor der Hauptaussage.

items.q: The more states legislate unilaterally, ____ any multilateral code becomes.
items.e: Korrelative Struktur „the … the …“ verlangt den bestimmten Artikel vor dem Komparativ.

items.q: ____ did the accord bypass the UN process, but it also excluded several major spacefaring states.
items.e: Feste Korrelation „not only … but also …“ mit obligatorischer Inversion nach vorangestelltem „Not only“.

items.q: The agency is believed ____ the extraction license months before it was made public.
items.e: Vorzeitiger Infinitiv nach Berichtspassiv: „is believed to have approved“.

items.q: The mining code is reported ____ debated again at the next committee session.
items.e: „is reported to be debated“ — Passiv-Infinitiv für ein bevorstehendes Ereignis.

items.q: The provision ____ the delegation objected has since been reworded.
items.e: „object to“ verlangt bei vorangestellter Präposition „to which“, niemals „that“.

items.q: The principle ____ the accord rests remains contested among legal scholars.
items.e: „rest on a principle“ → vorangestellte Präposition erzwingt „on which“.

items.q: If only the treaty's drafters ____ commercial extraction explicitly, decades of dispute might have been avoided.
items.e: „If only“ + Past Perfect für einen unerfüllten Wunsch bezogen auf die Vergangenheit.

items.q: The committee ____ raise the benefit-sharing question repeatedly, despite claims that it was ignored.
items.e: Emphatisches „did“ zur Widerlegung eines Vorwurfs, gefolgt vom Grundverb „raise“.

items.q: She was appointed ____ rapporteur on space resource governance last year.
items.e: Nullartikel vor einmaligen Ämtern/Funktionen nach „appoint“.

items.q: By the time the next committee session opens, the working group ____ its draft code.
items.e: Future Perfect für ein Ereignis, das vor einem zukünftigen Zeitpunkt abgeschlossen sein wird.

items.e: „go on to do“ = mit etwas Neuem fortfahren, im Gegensatz zu „go on doing“ (dasselbe fortsetzen).

items.q: The drafters phrased Article II broadly ____ any single interpretation dominate future practice.
items.e: „lest“ + Subjunktiv „dominate“ (ohne -s); „in case“ verlangte „it should dominate“.

items.q: What is the author's main point about the rhetoric surrounding data localisation laws?
o: The rhetoric of privacy protection is entirely accurate and uncontested.
The declared aim of protecting citizens' data often coincides conveniently with protecting domestic industry from foreign competition.
Data localisation laws have been abandoned by every major economy.
Such laws exist solely to comply with United Nations directives.
items.e: Der Text zeigt, dass Datenschutzargumente und industriepolitischer Protektionismus im Diskurs über Datenlokalisierung eng verwoben sind.
items.passage:
Few pieces of digital-policy jargon have travelled as far, or been stretched to cover as much, as 'data sovereignty'. Governments invoking the term range from those genuinely alarmed at the prospect of a foreign intelligence service subpoenaing a citizen's medical records to those rather more interested in ensuring that the servers, the jobs and the tax revenue attached to their citizens' data remain firmly within national borders. The two motives are not mutually exclusive, which is precisely what makes the resulting legislation so difficult to unpick.

Requirements that certain categories of data be stored, and in some cases processed, on domestic soil have proliferated across jurisdictions with strikingly different political systems, from privacy-conscious European capitals to states with considerably less enthusiasm for judicial oversight of surveillance. Proponents insist that localisation shields citizens from extraterritorial reach — a foreign court order, for instance, cannot easily compel disclosure of data that never left the country. Detractors retort that a server's physical location offers scant protection against a government determined to access what sits on it, while imposing very real costs on smaller firms unable to replicate costly infrastructure in every market they wish to serve.

The deeper irony, rarely voiced aloud in official communiqués, is that localisation mandates frequently benefit precisely the large incumbent cloud providers they are nominally meant to discipline, since only firms of a certain scale can afford to build redundant, jurisdiction-specific data centres on demand. Smaller domestic challengers, ostensibly the intended beneficiaries of digital-sovereignty policy, often find themselves squeezed out by compliance costs that only the largest multinationals can readily absorb. Whatever else localisation achieves, it has not, on the evidence so far assembled, produced the flourishing domestic data economies its architects promised.
items.src: Übungstext im Stil von Foreign Affairs / The Economist (nicht offiziell)

items.q: According to the passage, why does the mixture of motives behind 'data sovereignty' make the resulting legislation hard to interpret?
o: Because privacy concerns and protectionist economic interests are not mutually exclusive and often overlap.
Because no government has ever explained its reasoning publicly.
Because the term has an identical legal definition in every jurisdiction.
Because courts have unanimously rejected all such legislation.
items.e: Zitat: „The two motives are not mutually exclusive, which is precisely what makes the resulting legislation so difficult to unpick.“

items.q: What argument do detractors of localisation make regarding server location, per the passage?
o: That physical location offers little real protection against a determined government's access.
That servers should never be located within national borders under any circumstances.
That localisation always reduces costs for smaller firms.
That foreign courts have no interest in accessing any data whatsoever.
items.e: Zitat: „a server's physical location offers scant protection against a government determined to access what sits on it“.

items.q: What can be inferred about the actual beneficiaries of localisation mandates, according to the passage?
o: Small domestic challengers benefit most, exactly as intended.
Large incumbent cloud providers often benefit, contrary to the policy's stated aim of disciplining them.
No commercial entity of any kind benefits from such mandates.
Only foreign governments benefit from localisation requirements.
items.e: Zitat: „localisation mandates frequently benefit precisely the large incumbent cloud providers they are nominally meant to discipline“.

items.q: In context, 'squeezed out by compliance costs' means that smaller domestic firms...
o: are forced out of the market because they cannot afford the costs of compliance.
receive generous subsidies to help them comply.
are exempted entirely from all compliance requirements.
voluntarily choose to leave the market for unrelated reasons.
items.e: Die Formulierung beschreibt eine Verdrängung kleinerer Anbieter, die die Compliance-Kosten nicht tragen können.

items.q: The author's tone toward official justifications for data localisation is best described as...
o: quietly ironic, pointing to a gap between stated aims and actual outcomes.
items.e: Der Autor spricht von einer „deeper irony, rarely voiced aloud“ — eine subtil-ironische Distanz zu den offiziellen Begründungen.

items.q: How does the passage's last sentence relate to what precedes it?
o: It confirms that localisation has fully achieved its stated economic goals.
It concludes, based on the evidence presented, that the promised domestic data economies have not materialised.
It introduces an entirely new topic unrelated to the preceding discussion.
It predicts that all localisation laws will be repealed within a year.
items.e: Der Schlusssatz zieht die Bilanz: die versprochene florierende heimische Datenwirtschaft ist ausgeblieben.

items.q: Why do proponents of localisation argue it protects citizens, per the second paragraph?
o: Because data that never leaves the country cannot easily be reached by a foreign court order.
Because localisation automatically encrypts all citizen data.
Because it eliminates the need for any domestic judicial oversight.
Because it guarantees lower prices for digital services.
items.e: Zitat: „a foreign court order … cannot easily compel disclosure of data that never left the country“.

items.q: The term 'data sovereignty' has been ____ to cover an unusually wide range of policy motives.
items.e: „stretch a term (to cover)“ = einen Begriff überdehnen; feste idiomatische Kollokation im Diskursanalyse-Kontext.

items.q: Critics find the overlapping motives behind localisation laws difficult to ____.
items.e: „unpick“ = analytisch entwirren/auseinandernehmen; feste übertragene Bedeutung im Diskurs, die übrigen Verben bleiben wörtlich.

items.q: Localisation rules aim to shield citizens' data from ____ reach by foreign courts.
items.e: „extraterritorial reach“ ist der etablierte völkerrechtliche Terminus; die übrigen Wortbildungen existieren nicht.

items.q: Smaller providers cannot easily ____ the costly infrastructure that localisation mandates require in every market.
items.e: „replicate infrastructure“ ist die im Technologie-Register übliche Kollokation für den mehrfachen Aufbau identischer Anlagen.

items.q: Regulators insist the rules apply ____ of a company's country of origin.
items.e: „regardless of“ ist im formellen Register die gebräuchlichste feste Präpositionalwendung dieser vier Optionen.

items.q: The policy's architects promised a flourishing domestic data ____ that has yet to materialise.
items.e: Substantiv „economy“ nach „data“ als Kompositum; die übrigen Formen sind falsche Wortarten.

items.q: Only the largest multinationals can readily ____ the compliance costs of jurisdiction-specific data centres.
items.e: „absorb costs“ ist die feste betriebswirtschaftliche Kollokation; die übrigen Verben sind hier unidiomatisch.

items.q: Domestic challengers, ostensibly the ____ of the policy, often find themselves squeezed out instead.
items.e: „intended beneficiaries“ ist die feste Kollokation für die eigentlich begünstigte Gruppe einer Maßnahme.

items.q: The regulator's new powers give it ____ over cross-border data transfers it previously lacked.
items.e: Substantiv „leverage“ (Einflussmöglichkeit) nach „gives it“; die übrigen Formen sind grammatisch fehlerhaft.

items.q: Critics accuse the law of being protectionism ____ in the language of privacy.
items.e: „dressed up in the language of“ = als etwas Anderes getarnt/verkleidet dargestellt; feste idiomatische Wendung.

items.q: Firms operating across borders must now navigate a genuine ____ of divergent national data rules.
items.e: „a patchwork of rules“ = ein Flickenteppich uneinheitlicher Regelungen; feste Metapher.

items.q: The proposed rule has been widely ____ as thinly disguised industrial policy.
items.e: Partizip Perfekt „derided“ nach „has been widely“; die übrigen Formen sind falsche Wortarten.

items.q: The two capitals remain at ____ over whether localisation genuinely improves cybersecurity.
items.e: „at loggerheads“ = in offenem Streit/unversöhnlich uneinig; feste Redewendung, nur diese Schreibweise ist korrekt.

items.q: Officials were quick to ____ that the measure was purely a security matter, not an economic one.
items.e: „assert“ betont eine nachdrückliche, autoritative Behauptung; im Kontext offizieller Stellungnahmen die treffendste der vier Optionen.

items.q: The compliance burden falls ____ on smaller firms than on established multinationals.
items.e: „fall disproportionately on“ = unverhältnismäßig stark treffen; feste Kollokation im Regulierungskontext.

items.q: The ministry's proposal was quietly ____ back after backlash from smaller tech firms.
items.e: „scale back a proposal“ = einen Vorschlag zurückstufen/abschwächen; feste Partikelverbverbindung.

items.q: Some regulators privately concede that enforcement remains ____ at best.
items.e: Adjektiv „patchy“ = lückenhaft/uneinheitlich; die übrigen Formen sind falsche Wortarten.

items.q: The rule was framed as a ____ measure, though its scope has since expanded considerably.
items.e: „narrowly targeted measure“ ist die korrekt gebildete, feste Kollokation; die übrigen Varianten enthalten Bildungsfehler.

items.q: Compliance officers describe the overlapping rules as a bureaucratic ____.
items.e: „a bureaucratic minefield“ = ein Bereich voller versteckter Risiken/Fallstricke; feste Metapher, nur diese Schreibweise korrekt.

items.q: The government's real motive, sceptics argue, is to ____ domestic providers from foreign competition.
items.e: „shield from competition“ ist die feste wirtschaftspolitische Kollokation; die übrigen Verben passen hier nicht idiomatisch.

items.q: The largest cloud providers have quietly turned localisation rules to their own ____.
items.e: „turn something to one's advantage“ ist die feste idiomatische Wendung für das geschickte Ausnutzen einer Situation.

items.q: Some firms have found ways to ____ the localisation requirement using encrypted proxies.
items.e: „circumvent a requirement“ = eine Vorschrift umgehen; „circumvene“ existiert nicht, „circumscribe“ bedeutet einschränken/begrenzen.

items.q: The rule risks ____ the dominance of the largest cloud providers still further.
items.e: „cement dominance“ = eine marktbeherrschende Stellung festigen; feste Metapher, die übrigen Verben sind hier unidiomatisch.

items.q: Smaller firms complain the rule fails to create a ____ .
items.e: „a level playing field“ ist die feste, unveränderliche Redewendung für faire Wettbewerbsbedingungen.

items.q: Compliance officers describe the new requirements as needless ____ .
items.e: „red tape“ = Bürokratie/übermäßige Verwaltungsvorschriften; feste idiomatische Wendung.

items.q: The clause is meant to act as a ____ against arbitrary data seizure.
items.e: „safeguard against“ ist die feste Kollokation; die übrigen Optionen sind keine etablierten Wendungen in diesem Kontext.

items.q: The regulator demanded that the provider ____ all domestic user data within national borders.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach „demand that“ — Grundform ohne -s.

items.q: The ministry recommended that the exemption ____ extended to smaller providers.
items.e: Mandativer Subjunktiv nach „recommend that“: „be extended“, keine Personalendung.

items.q: Rarely ____ regulators faced such fierce lobbying from both domestic and foreign firms simultaneously.
items.e: Inversion nach vorangestelltem „Rarely“: Hilfsverb „have“ vor Subjekt (Present Perfect, Plural).

items.q: Not until the exemptions were published ____ smaller firms the true scope of their new obligations.
items.e: Inversion nach vorangestelltem „Not until“: Hilfsverb „did“ vor Subjekt, Grundform „realise“.

items.q: Had the exemption been broader, compliance costs ____ far lower for smaller firms today.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional: Bedingung Vergangenheit (Had been), Folge Gegenwart (today).

items.q: If the ministry ____ smaller firms before drafting the rule, the current backlash might not exist.
items.e: Gemischter Konditional: vergangene Ursache (had consulted), gegenwärtige Folge (might not exist).

items.q: The ministry ____ have foreseen the backlash from smaller providers; industry groups had warned repeatedly.
items.e: „should have“ = Kritik an einer versäumten Handlung in der Vergangenheit.

items.q: The regulator ____ have approved that exemption; it directly contradicts the published guidance.
items.e: „can't have“ = logischer Ausschluss im Rückblick.

items.q: ____ troubled smaller providers most was the cost of duplicating infrastructure in every market.
items.e: Pseudo-Cleft: „What … was …“.

items.q: ____ the report revealed was not weak enforcement but an entirely absent one.
items.e: Pseudo-Cleft „What … was …“ kontrastiert zwei mögliche Erklärungen.

items.q: The spokesperson said the exemption ____ reviewed at the next regulatory cycle.
items.e: Backshift in indirekter Rede: will be → would be.

items.q: She admitted the ministry ____ the smaller firms' objections before finalising the rule.
items.e: Past Perfect für Vorzeitigkeit in indirekter Rede.

items.q: ____ by three major providers, the compliance scheme gained an early appearance of legitimacy.
items.e: Passivisches Partizip: Die Aktivformen würden das Compliance-Programm fälschlich zum Handelnden machen.

items.q: ____ the compliance costs carefully, the smaller provider decided to exit the market entirely.
items.e: Vorzeitiges Partizip „Having calculated“ zeigt eine abgeschlossene Handlung vor der Hauptaussage.

items.q: The stricter the localisation rules became, ____ the compliance burden grew for smaller firms.
items.e: Korrelative Struktur „the … the …“ verlangt den bestimmten Artikel vor dem Komparativ.

items.q: ____ did the rule raise compliance costs, but it also entrenched the position of the largest providers.
items.e: Feste Korrelation „not only … but also …“ mit obligatorischer Inversion nach vorangestelltem „Not only“.

items.q: The ministry is believed ____ the exemption months before it was formally announced.
items.e: Vorzeitiger Infinitiv nach Berichtspassiv: „is believed to have drafted“.

items.q: The exemption is reported ____ extended to smaller domestic providers next quarter.
items.e: „is reported to be extended“ — Passiv-Infinitiv für ein bevorstehendes Ereignis.

items.q: The clause ____ smaller firms objected has since been softened considerably.
items.e: „object to“ verlangt bei vorangestellter Präposition „to which“, niemals „that“.

items.q: The threshold ____ compliance is assessed has yet to be clarified by the regulator.
items.e: „assess against a threshold“ → vorangestellte Präposition erzwingt „against which“.

items.q: If only the ministry ____ smaller firms before drafting the rule, this dispute might have been avoided.
items.e: „If only“ + Past Perfect für einen unerfüllten Wunsch in der Vergangenheit.

items.q: The ministry ____ warn industry groups repeatedly, contrary to claims that consultation was skipped.
items.e: Emphatisches „did“ zur Widerlegung eines Vorwurfs, gefolgt vom Grundverb „warn“.

items.q: She was appointed ____ chief data-protection officer shortly after the rule took effect.
items.e: Nullartikel vor einmaligen Ämtern/Funktionen nach „appoint“.

items.q: By the time the new rule takes effect, most providers ____ their infrastructure.
items.e: Future Perfect für ein Ereignis, das vor einem zukünftigen Zeitpunkt abgeschlossen sein wird.

items.q: The regulator went on ____ a separate exemption for research institutions in a later announcement.
items.e: „go on to do“ = mit etwas Neuem fortfahren, im Gegensatz zu „go on doing“ (dasselbe fortsetzen).

items.q: The drafters worded the exemption cautiously ____ larger providers exploit it disproportionately.
items.e: „lest“ + Subjunktiv „exploit“ (ohne -s); „in case“ verlangte „they should exploit“.
